Republican congresswoman Lauren Boebert has forcefully denied allegations that she had affairs with male and female staffers, denouncing the claims as “salacious bull****.”

The Colorado Republican issued a video response Sunday after David Wheeler, co-founder of Democratic-aligned PAC American Muckrakers, filed a House Ethics Committee complaint on September 17, alleging she had sexual relationships with three employees.

“Hey journalists… I have a few words for you,” Boebert said in the roughly two-minute video, which has since been viewed over two million views on X. “You all ran a smear and called it news... It’s a scam. And you fell for it.”

She continued: “No member of Congress certified in writing that his salacious, bull**** attack was made in good faith and warrants review as required by ethics. And it’s evident that you didn’t even bother to look up House Ethics Committee rules that clearly state the committee can’t even accept a complaint filed inside 60 days of an election.”

Under House Ethics Committee rules, an elected official must certify that a complaint submitted by a nonmember was made in good faith. The rules bar the committee from accepting nonmember complaints within 60 days of an election, where the subject is a candidate. Boebert is up for reelection in November.

open image in gallery Representative Lauren Boebert, a Colorado Republican who is running for reelection this November, denounced media reports alleging she had affairs with staff members as 'salacious bull****' ( @laurenboebert, X )

In 2018, following the #MeToo movement, the House barred members from having sexual relationships with employees they supervise. There is an exception if the two individuals are married.

The complaint, first reported by the Colorado Times Recorder, alleges Boebert had relationships with her former district director Clarice Navarro, her chief of staff Raven Finegan and her former chief of staff Jeffrey Small. Some encounters allegedly took place during official hours, in a district office and in hotel rooms paid for by a campaign committee.

The complaint further alleges that a $200,000 payment was arranged for Navarro in order to “secure her silence” after she threatened to file her own ethics complaint. Navarro has called the claims “entirely false and defamatory,” according to the outlet.

Boebert, 39, who divorced from her husband in 2023, lambasted the media for targeting her employees in her video.

“Nobody in your newsroom checked the rulebook before they put my teams’ names in your stories,” she said. “Their photos are everywhere now. And they are under attack because of your laziness.”

She further noted that Wheeler has a history of making allegations against her, describing him as a “sloppy, desperate, obsessive hack.” In 2022, Wheeler alleged that Boebert had worked as an escort, according to the Colorado Times Recorder. Boebert denied the allegation and obtained a temporary restraining order against Wheeler.

“I know that you’re more than willing to attack me and shame my household, but this is different and you crossed a line,” Boebert said in Sunday’s X video.

In a statement to Newsweek on Sunday, Wheeler said: “Ms. Boebert runs her classic denial scheme learned straight out of the swamp and carried out by her minions... She deflects and tries to make the allegations about me."

“Boebert truly believes she is not accountable for her actions, nor do the laws apply to her,” he added.

open image in gallery Boebert, first elected in 2020, was initially one of President Donald Trump’s staunchest allies in Congress ( Lauren Boebert / Twitter )

Boebert was first elected in 2020 and was initially among President Donald Trump’s staunchest allies in Congress. She had campaigned on being anti-abortion, a supporter of gun rights and focused on conservative family values.

But she drew Trump’s ire earlier this year after joining several Republicans who helped force a House vote to require the Justice Department to release the Epstein Files.

Trump later threatened to back a primary challenger after Boebert campaigned with Representative Thomas Massie, the Kentucky Republican who has become one of Trump’s most outspoken GOP critics. She has also broken with Trump over spending on the Iran war.

In August, her 21-year-old son was arrested on child exploitation charges.

“I love my son. We take these allegations very seriously and pray for everyone affected during this challenging time,” Boebert told The Independent at the time.

The Independent has contacted the House Ethics Committee for comment.

News.title: Afghan medical students face expulsion from Pakistan
News.content:
An educational lifeline for young Afghan women banned by the Taliban from training as doctors in their homeland is in jeopardy after Pakistan’s medical authorities tried to have them expelled.

Several hundred Afghan female students studying across the border in Pakistan have been threatened with removal, amid rising tensions and tit-for-tat exchanges between the neighbours.

The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) which regulates medical education earlier this month ordered medical and dental colleges with Afghan students to kick them out.

Within days, major institutions including King Edward Medical University (KEMU), Shaikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Al Nahyan Medical and Dental College, and the Services Institute of Medical Sciences, had ordered Afghan students to leave.

The nationwide order was estimated to have affected around 1,000 Afghan students, with 35 per cent of those thought to be female students.

Provincial high courts have now temporarily halted the expulsion pending further hearings, but Afghan students told The Telegraph they were terrified their careers would be ended.

“The government’s decision aimed to send us to the Stone Age because the Taliban in Afghanistan have banned female education,” said Sabiha Daftani, one of the 22 Afghan students given orders on September 7 by KEMU in Lahore on to leave within 24 hours.

“The fear is constant and haunting us,” she said.

News.title: Michael Carrick will not survive unless Manchester United change
News.content:
But so passive was their football that is the way he felt in the moment. For a club with United’s “attack, attack, attack” tradition – becoming something of a distant memory as seasons pass – that is a damning as it gets.

Neville’s Sky paymasters will be delighted by his emotive, insulting, headline-grabbing language. But he of course exaggerated a point to make a point. United, and Carrick, were, indeed, far too passive, lacking aggression, urgency and belief. They just do not press. United did, for too long, play like a team of dummies.

Against Fulham they almost played walking football until they conceded, desperation kicked in and they chased the game to salvage a late draw.

It begs the question: what is Carrick doing with this team? Yes, he may have been let down by no defensive signings in the summer – even if he must have bought into the plan to prioritise a midfield rebuild – but he is far from absolved from blame.

He will cling to the response to Lisandro Martínez’s own goal, to striking a post twice in the first half from Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes, to managing to avoid a third successive defeat in a week, which would have led to the crisis klaxon being sounded. Carrick can talk about how ridiculous it would be to question his position as head coach. But is it?

We now go into a three-week international break and the Premier League vacuum would have been filled by a debate over Carrick’s future, whether he is up to the job and another existential examination as to where United are heading. And who is to blame.

That still might happen. United did not lose. But they were not remotely good enough, as has been the case for most of the season. Their only league win in five was against newly promoted Ipswich Town, having lost to newly promoted Hull City. They have also drawn at Everton and now at Fulham, who started the day bottom of the table and remain winless. Apart from facing Manchester City, it has hardly been the most taxing of starts. Except they are down in 12th and have not played well at all.

News.title: Alisson’s brilliance takes the breath away to show way forward for Liverpool
News.content:
It proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

“It was a really good fight,” Alisson said, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”

Any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

“He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”

News.title: All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper
News.content:
It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Asked if Tottenham had made a big mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

“We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”

News.title: An A to Z guide to what’s in your laundry detergent
News.content:
Laundry is one of those jobs that most of us do on autopilot. Throw a load of washing and your favourite detergent into the drum and wait for the machine to work its magic. Perhaps you’ve never even thought to ask yourself what chemicals you’re putting in with your clothes.

In the UK, detergent brands are legally required to state the use of surfactants and enzymes (the main ingredients for stain removal) in a way that is easy to understand, but you may see additional compounds that leave you scratching your head.

Here, I break down the words on the back of the bottle to help you understand exactly what you’re putting in your washing. Given that I’ve just tested 26 laundry detergents and developed an app to help you clean your clothes better, I’m the best woman for the job.

Below, you’ll find the most common detergent ingredients listed A to Z. If you’ve got a burning question about a laundry buzzword, I should be able to help. Add any in the comments section below.

Anionic

There are two main types of surfactants: anionic and non-ionic. A surfactant has a hydrophilic head that loves water and a hydrophobic tail that hates it. Anionic surfactants have a negative charge on their head, which is what helps lift soils and stains from the fabric, though they’re not so good at getting rid of oils. They create a lot of foam but their effectiveness can be limited by minerals found in hard water, which is why they are paired with non-ionic surfactants.

Bio

Short for biological, this label means that a detergent contains enzymes. These are proteins that break down fats, starches and grease, so use bio formulations when you need to tackle stubborn food stains. They are effective at lower temperatures but they can be abrasive on sensitive skin. If your skin is easily irritated, opt for non-bio, instead.

Millwall manager Alex Neil said after the game that fourth official Lewis Smith had confirmed a spitting accusation had been made.

Asked if he had spoken to Marschall about the claim, Neil replied: “I haven’t asked him about it. But it’s like anything else; I’m sure there’ll be footage of it, or not of it, if it didn’t happen.

News.title: Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

Brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

That 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

With Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

Elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

Everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Ipswich are sitting comfortably on six points after their win at Crystal Palace, though they did have the extra man for the majority at Selhurst Park.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Red Roses’ 39-match winning streak brought to end in Canada draw
News.content:
The record books will show that this meeting, a proper Test full of ebbs and flows, was neither. And, no matter the pre-match belief of England head coach John Mitchell, Canada are not on the same level of professionalism and funding as his side. Mitchell had brought back nine players, many of whom featured in last year’s World Cup final victory, after the thrashing of Australia last week with the expectation that the history of 2025 would repeat itself. Canada had other ideas.

“The plan on the field at the last scrum was to go for the win,” Canada captain Sophie de Goede said. “And then the message came on from the sideline to kick it out. In that moment you have to trust your coach and your coaching staff, and we’ll have a discussion about it later. If we had given away a penalty off the next breakdown, we’d be sitting here going, ‘Why didn’t you kick it out?’”

England’s downfall came at the set-piece, where their line-out malfunctioned and their scrum never gained dominance, in a tale which was not too dissimilar to last week. The hosts came second in the physical battle, too, which was uncharacteristic of them; losing Hannah Botterman to a shoulder injury did not help, either. All told, Canada just looked as though they wanted it a little bit more and maybe this was the wake-up call the Red Roses needed: when you are at the top, and at the top by a margin, every team want to be the one to dethrone you.

Sports.title: How footballers fared on I’m A Celeb from Ian Wright to Harry Redknapp as Wayne Rooney prepares to enter jungle
Sports.content:
Next

WAYNE ROONEY is the latest footballer ready to take on the jungle.

The England legend, 40, is set to 



He will follow wife Coleen, who was runner-up on the ITV show in 2024.

Insiders tell The Sun that Rooney is keen to impress his four sons by taking on the Bushtucker Trials Down Under, and would be the hit show’s biggest-ever signing.



The all-time Man Utd top scorer is one of a number of footballers who have tried their luck on the reality TV series.

SunSport looks at the best of the rest and how they fared – with two notable winners coming from the Beautiful Game.

John Fashanu

The Wimbledon legend was a renowned hard man on the pitch.

In 2003, with a TV audience knowing him well after a stint as a presenter of Gladiators with Ulrika Jonsson, he appeared in the second series of I’m A Celeb… and finished second to Phil Tufnell.

Fash already warned viewers before the show that he was afraid of heights, but he was handed the cruellest of Bushtucker Trials.

The former striker had to bob his head into a Perspex box of water, picking out stars with his teeth as eels were fired into it from either side.



“That was hell,” he admitted after the challenge. “Whoever thought of that I’d like to meet in a dark alley.”

Neil Ruddock

‘Razor’ Ruddock’s time in the jungle was a miserable one.

He was surrounded by a great line-up, including Katie Price, Peter Andre, Kerry Katona, and John Lydon.



Despite his larger-than-life personality, Ruddock couldn’t adapt and was third to be voted out.

But that wasn’t before he faced a Trial called Fill Your Face alongside Price.

The pair had their heads in a fish bowl that was filled with all sorts of creepy crawlies.



It was Ruddock’s crowning glory, as they won enough stars to feed the whole camp.

Rodney Marsh

Controversial Marsh managed to get himself into a lot of bother in 2007.

He had an almighty row with PR Lynne Franks, was accused of sexist jokes, and even flashed his bum. But, he wasn’t sorry.

“I acted like a five year old kid sometimes. I don’t apologise. What you see is what you get,” he told Ant and Dec in his post-eviction interview.

On Franks he said: “I despise everything she stands for. I think it is fair to say that she irritated me.”



Jimmy Bullard

It seemed that Marsh’s outburst put the pin in footballers appearing on the show.

It was seven years until we saw another one, this time loveable jester Bullard joined the show.

His cheeky chappy status on the football pitch didn’t translate to the TV screens, where Bullard was the third celebrity voted off by the viewers.



Before he was given the boot, we saw him eat sheep’s testicles and memorably sing naked in the shower with Jake Quickenden.

Last year, TV producers brought Bullard back for the South Africa version of the show. However, that ended in tears after he quit a trial and got into a barney with fellow campmate Adam Thomas.

Kieron Dyer

The former Newcastle United footballer immediately won over viewers when he announced he was donating his I’m A Celeb fee to charity.



He was thrust into the deep end with a horrific challenge called Scarier 52 in which he had to trawl through a room filled with rotten meat and flies and find two stars.

It all got a bit too much Dyer, who broke down and almost quit the show after everyone turned on Lady Colin Campbell.

But Chris Eubank talked him into staying, and Dyer finished a respectable fourth in the end.



Wayne Bridge

The former Chelsea defender signed up to the 16th series of I’m A Celeb in 2016, and didn’t disappoint.

Bridge finished fifth after a shock double elimination with Martin Roberts – just two nights before the final.

From the offset, he had to confront his fears – skydiving into the jungle from 10,000 feet.

He made friends with Gavin & Stacey star Larry Lamb, breaking down in tears when he discussed his family life.



Bridge also tussled with creepy-crawlies, which he hated. He was TV gold, to be fair.

Dennis Wise

Keeping their reputation as the go-to club for I’m A Celeb contestants, it was Chelsea legend Wise who followed Bridge into the jungle in 2017.

And, the former midfielder made it to day 19 before he was booted off the show.

However, there was some controversy when viewers thought he was a bully after telling Iain Lee he shouldn’t do a Bushtucker Trial in case he failed because he wasn’t good enough.



Good guy Wise made up for after the show, getting Iain tickets for Chelsea for him and his kids, and the pair became friends the moment they stepped out the jungle.

Harry Redknapp

The ‘King of the Jungle’ in 2018, Redknapp became an instant favourite with the viewers gushing about missing wife Sandra, his love of a jam roly-poly and fearless attitude towards tasks, as well as a cold shower.

The West Ham legend even proved that he could stomach anything when he shoved a load of maggots in his mouth and chomped on them.



A worthy-winner, Redknapp set the bar for future footballing contestants.

Last year he returned in the all-star series in South Africa, finishing in third place.

Ian Wright

TV pundit and Arsenal icon Wrighty joined a year after Redknapp’s heroic stint and was tipped to be a star.



However, his struggles with hunger, as well as the harsh realities of being in camp affected his mental health.

Couple that with clashes with comedian Andrew Maxwell, we didn’t see the best side of the Gunners legend.

He lasted 18 days, was the fifth contestant to be voted out, and told hosts Ant and Dec about his short fuse in his post-eviction interview, “I lose it too quickly… I’ve got a lot to work on.”



David Ginola

In 2021, the series switched to Gwrych Castle in North Wales due to Covid-19 travel restrictions.

And our faith in footballers was restored again when ‘Camp Dad’ Ginola finished fourth on the show.

He talked candidly about his near-death experience from a heart attack during a charity football match in 2016 to his fellow campmates.



The former French footballer also charmed viewers and contestant Arlene Phillips by singing Come On Arlene to the tune of the Dexys Midnight Runners’ hit, Come On Eileen.

Right before his exit, Ginola also survived the Celebrity Cyclone challenge.

Jill Scott

In 2022, Jill became the ‘Queen of the Jungle’ and football’s second ever winner.

It was so richly deserved, with the former Lionesses proving to be a hit with viewers because of her down-to-earth personality, her leadership, and brilliant sense of humour.

She kept her composure when a cockroach got stuck in her ear during one trial, and in her final challenge had to lie down in a glass box with over 70 rats crawling all over her for several minutes, as she won enough stars to feed her campmates.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Jill went viral for her dance moves when the campmates created a song about hot banana water.

While she also drew praise for openly discussing her sexuality and coming out to the football community in a heartfelt conversation with Boy George.

Sports.content:

MANCHESTER UNITED were slammed by Gary Neville after producing “the worst 15 minutes I have seen them play” in the second half of their 1-1 draw with Fulham.

United fans might argue with that claim after watching some awful displays over the years – including a cup exit to Grimsby, a 4-0 hammering by Brentford and a 7-0 demolition by Liverpool.



Michael Carrick‘s side were poor at Craven Cottage, however, especially in the first 15 minutes of the second half, and United didn’t have a single shot during this spell up until Lisandro Martinez’s own goal in the 63rd minute.

While United did salvage a point thanks to Matheus Cunha‘s late strike, Neville was scathing of their opening quarter of an hour, calling them “absolutely pathetic”.



The former Red Devils right-back said: “I’ve watched Manchester United since the age of five and that’s the worst 15 minutes I have ever seen them play.

“Absolutely pathetic. They have walked for 15 minutes and you get what you deserve in a football match.

“Maybe there will be a reaction but I’ve never seen a lack of effort for 15 to 20 minutes like I have just seen there. What must he (Carrick) be thinking?”

Sun Sport has re-watched the first 15 minutes of United’s second half – so you don’t have to – in a bid to see if Neville’s got a point.

46′: Good cross from Marcus Rashford is poorly controlled by Cunha in a scoring position – but the Brazilian gives away a foul anyway.

48′: Rashford loses the ball after poor touch that sparks a Fulham counter attack.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

49′: Better from United as they launch their own counter. Rashford wins a free kick after being fouled by Timothy Castagne, who is booked.

49′: Diogo Dalot is dispossessed in a promising position for United.

51′: Kobbie Mainoo over-hits pass into the box and another United attack comes to nothing.

52′: United try to play out from the back but Martinez’s pass upfield is intercepted by Fulham, who launch an immediate counter.

53′: Nice give and go between Youri Tielemans and Rashford sets the England winger away… but his cross-field pass to Mbeumo is poor and the ex-Brentford man fouls his man trying to get the ball back.



55′: Mbeumo races through on the breakaway after long spell of possession for Fulham, but gets clattered after a heavy touch – allowing the hosts to recycle the ball again.

57′: United keeper Senne Lammens boots the ball down the pitch under pressure, but he can’t find a team-mate and Fulham take control again.

59′: Mbeumo fails to control Mainoo’s pass under pressure from Alex Iwobi and gives away a Fulham throw.



60′: Iwobi smashes a shot at goal, which cannons off Tielemans and out for a corner.

61′: Rare opening for United as a wayward Fulham pass is pounced on by Mbeumo, but his touch is horrendous and gifts ball back to the home side once again.

62′: Luke Shaw gets skinned by Oscar Bobb, who get a cross into the box.

Sports.title: Brian Brobbey mega haul gives Dream Team managers something to ponder over international break
Sports.content:
Next

BRIAN BROBBEY (£2.7m) joined an exclusive club on Sunday.

Sunderland’s No9 became just the fifth man in Premier League history to score a hat-trick in defeat.

Brobbey struck three times against Manchester City but Enzo Maresca’s goals scored five goals of their own to claim the three points and maintain their 100% record this campaign.



In taking the match ball home after a loss, the Dutchman emulated Matt Le Tissier (x2), Dion Dublin, Dwight Yorke and Roque Santa Cruz.



The Black Cats will be disappointed to have scored three goals at the Etihad and come away with nothing but nobody can take Brobbey’s hat-trick away from him, or the Dream Team points he earned for it.

The 24-year-old banked 25 points in one fell swoop and was the top performer in Gameweek 5, edging out Antoine Semenyo (£5.7m) who earned 21 points in the same fixture.



Truth be told, Brobbey was in desperate need of a big return.

He mustered just 10 points across the first four Gameweeks and registered one shot on target in five appearances.

However, his 25-point injection has propelled him up to eighth in the rankings among players in his position.

The ex-Ajax forward is one of the most physical players in the Premier League and many Sunderland fans would say that his hat-trick was just reward for the work he’s put in since the start of the season.



No doubt Brobbey’s mega haul will percolate over the course of the extended international break.

Provided he doesn’t injure himself while on international duty with Netherlands, he may be a popular recruit for Gameweek 6 come early October.

Sunderland’s Gameweek 6 double header is an interesting one: Brighton (h) & Torreense (a).

It would be foolish to underestimate the Seagulls, especially after their 3-0 win over Arsenal, but the Black Cats’ next European fixture is surely one to target.



Torreense ply their trade in the second tier of Portuguese football — they qualified for the Europa League by upsetting Sporting CP in the Portuguese cup final last season.

The club, based approximately 30 miles north of Lisbon, are currently 14th in the second flight having won just one of their first six league games.

Torreense won their first Europa League game (against Norwegian outfit Lillestrom) but Dream Team bosses will see them as favourable opponents for Sunderland after the break.

Brobbey currently features in 4.2% of teams.

Sports.title: ‘I’ve played brilliantly’ – Fulham star questions Alvaro Arbeloa after being dropped by new manager amid winless start
Sports.content:

JOACHIM ANDERSEN has questioned the wisdom of Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa – with the Spaniard yet to win a Premier League game since taking charge at Craven Cottage.

Danish defender Andersen voiced his “surprise” at being left out of the team – and insisted he has played “brilliantly” for the West Londoners.



Fulham are 19th in the table after Sunday’s 1-1 home draw with Manchester United. They led through Lisandro Martinez’s farcical own goal before Matheus Cunha rescued an 89th-minute point for the Red Devils.

Centre-back Andersen came on as a late sub. The former club skipper previously remained on the bench during his side’s 0-0 draw at Liverpool.



Danish broadcaster Viaplay quizzed the former Crystal Palace star about his recent omissions.

“It comes as a bit of a surprise to myself,” Andersen, 30, admitted. “I was captain in many, many games last season.



“Then we lost the first three [league] games this season. I was suspended in the first of them [a 3-2 home loss to Chelsea].

“And then the coach thinks he should change [the team].

“I don’t have much to say, because I can’t do much about it. I think I’ve played quite brilliantly.

“But sometimes the coach wants to try something different – and then that’s how it is.”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Under new skipper Calvin Bassey, Fulham lost 1-0 at Sunderland and 3-2 at home to Palace before picking up their first point at Liverpool.

They have, meanwhile, reached the Carabao Cup fourth round with wins over AFC Wimbledon and West Ham, and will host Andersen’s old club Palace on October 28.

Fulham paid the Eagles £30million to bring Andersen back to Craven Cottage in 2024.

He had previously spent the 2020/21 campaign there on loan from French club Lyon.

Sports.title: Former Chelsea star tells Xabi Alonso that Lamine Camara is ‘better off at Monaco’ after failed deadline day transfer

FORMER CHELSEA flop Denis Zakaria has told Lamine Camara he is ‘better off’ at Monaco after the midfielder’s dramatic deadline-day move to Stamford Bridge collapsed.

Chelsea made a late push to sign the Senegal international from Monaco on the final day of the transfer window.



A deal worth around £47million was verbally agreed between the clubs in the frantic final hours of the window, only for Monaco to pull the plug at the last minute.

Chelsea were left furious by the U-turn, with reports in the French media saying the midfielder’s behaviour has been “extraordinary and deeply unprofessional”.



The Senegalese star has wasted little time putting the disappointment behind him and has played a key role in Monaco’s impressive start to the season.

The 22-year-old midfielder helped Filipe Luis’ side beat Lens 2-1 to remain top of Ligue 1, with the victory taking Monaco to four wins from their opening five matches.



And after the final whistle, former Chelsea man Zakaria delivered a blunt message to his team-mate, forget about the Blues.

Zakaria told reporters, according to Get French Football News. “Chelsea? I told him that it was good but that it is better here.

“I know the player and the person that he is. He is very professional. I think [the failed transfer] has given him even more strength.

“He was incredible [against Lens].”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Zakaria knows all about life at Stamford Bridge after enduring a difficult loan spell there during the 2022-23 campaign.

The Switzerland international joined Chelsea from Juventus but made just seven Premier League appearances during a chaotic season which saw three different managers take charge as the club finished 12th.

Camara, meanwhile, appears determined to ensure his own failed move does not derail his season.

He told French media earlier this month: ” There was a possibility I could leave.



“It didn’t go through at the last minute and that’s part of football. I’ve turned the page and am focusing on the season.”

Chelsea could certainly have done with another midfielder after their own deadline-day dealings left them short in the centre of the pitch.

Moises Caicedo has been restricted to just 14 minutes so far this season because of injury, while Enzo Fernandez completed a £125million move to Manchester City on deadline day.

Camara’s form at Monaco means the failed transfer could yet prove costly for Chelsea, particularly if the Senegal star continues to flourish in France.

There is also an interesting Stamford Bridge connection on the Monaco bench, with boss Filipe Luis having been part of Chelsea’s title-winning squad in 2015 and previously considered as a possible replacement for Rosenior before Xabi Alonso was appointed.

Sports.title: ‘We’ll enjoy having him’ – Arsenal and Barcelona sent message over Julian Alvarez after failed Atletico transfer exit

MARC PUBILL has sent Arsenal and Barcelona a message after failed bids for Julian Alvarez.

Pubill, 23, has insisted that Atletico Madrid are fortunate to have retained the services of the forward after he missed out on a major European move over the summer.



Alvarez, 26, made his intentions on moving clear after two seasons in the Spanish capital, with strong interest coming from Barcelona and Arsenal.

However, no deal was agreed as Atletico refused to let the World Cup winner join his favoured club, Barcelona.



Now Pubill has explained to MARCA that he hopes Atletico can still get the best out of their star player.

Pubil said: “We experienced it inside the dressing room in the same way as people did from the outside.



“Julian is a spectacular player, extremely good, and luckily we have him here. We’re all going to enjoy having him. We will help him. Hopefully he gives us his maximum because he’s a top player.”

It comes after Alvarez received a hostile welcome from his own fans during the opening stages of the 2026-27 LaLiga season.

Atletico fans shockingly booed the forward during their derby against Real Madrid on Sunday.

Even Atletico chief Miguel Angel Gil Martin, 63, has hit out at the Argentine as he has been accused of harming the club.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The saga has resulted in the forward considering whether to ditch his agent Fernando Hidalgo.

Alvarez is yet to start a LaLiga match for Atletico since the transfer window closed, making three substitute appearances.

He also missed two games against Real Sociedad and Osasuna after dealing with muscular issues.

However, Alvarez assisted Marcos Llorente, 31, as he played 90 minutes in the side’s 2-1 defeat against Liverpool in their opening Champions League fixture.

Alvarez will get another opportunity to impress as he has been called up alongside the retiring Lionel Messi, 39, to Argentina’s squad for the upcoming international break.



Argentina will face Bolivia in Cordoba on Wednesday, September 30, before fixtures against Burkina Faso and Benin in Buenos Aires.

FORMER Tottenham defender Cristian Romero says that Lionel Messi should win the Ballon d’Or each year “until he retires”.

Sports.title: Brook relishing working with mentor of Pietersen's calibre
Sports.content:
Captain Harry Brook says leaning on a mentor of Kevin Pietersen's calibre will only help the continued upward trajectory of England's white-ball sides.

Pietersen, regarded as one of the greatest batters of the 21st century, has been brought into the England white-ball set-up in a mentoring role by head coach Brendon McCullum in the build-up to next year's 50-over World Cup.

Brook shed light on the impact Pietersen was already having on the squad, both on and off the field, with the team's approach to playing spin already addressed in a masterclass from the former England captain.

"KP has been very good," Brook told a press conference. "He's enjoying the role, he's enjoying himself.

"He's been good to have around, little chats here and there. Away from the game, sat having a coffee and a chat about how he sees the game and how he thinks it should be played.

"He was a hero to many of us growing up, so it's good to have a man of his calibre in our side."

On the masterclass, Brook added: "A lot of it was about picking the length of spin. That is key to facing spin and being able to rotate strike as well as possible.

"In ODI cricket that's an area we probably need to improve as a side. It can make a massive difference to winning games of cricket.

"He [Pietersen] was a hell of a player against spin, alongside [Joe] Root and [Marcus] Trescothick. They were very good players at playing spin, so it's about picking their brains and asking them what worked for them and putting that into your game."

'Higher-octane cricket'

England, fresh from a 3-0 series sweep over Sri Lanka that lifted them to the top of the T20 world rankings, face Sri Lanka again in their first ODI since teaming up with Pietersen.

The three-match series starts in Durham on Tuesday, live on Sky Sports, and Brook has challenged England to maintain their momentum.

"We can take a hell of a lot of confidence from being unbeaten in the T20s," Brook said.

"Going into this ODI series we want more of the same. We're trying to play a higher-octane style of cricket and put them [the opposition] under pressure with bat and ball.

"We want to be one of the fittest sides in the world. To do that, we've got to work hard on and off the field.

"We are trending in the right direction. There are a few touches here and there which we can improve."

Brook - better than Pietersen?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Southampton as England thumped Sri Lanka by 119 runs in the first T20 international of the three-match series thanks to Harry Brook's century.

Brook was hailed as an "absolute freak" by Ben Stokes as he tonked a 42-ball hundred, England's joint-second-fastest in T20Is, to pave the way for a 119-run victory in the T20 series opener against Sri Lanka in Southampton.

The swashbuckling innings was played in front of England legend Pietersen, and commented on by Stokes, who took to social media to say that, in his opinion, the Yorkshireman's ability outstrips that of Pietersen.

Asked to comment on Stokes' assessment, Brook said: "They are his opinions. I'm just trying to stay in the moment and in the present as much as possible.

"It's good to have KP to work alongside and pick his brains. There are plenty of good players in the squad to chat to about cricket, different surfaces, and playing different styles of bowlers. I'm trying to learn as much as I possibly can."

England change three for Sri Lanka opener

England have made three changes to the side which secured a 2-1 ODI series victory over India with a 27-run victory at Lord's on July 19.

Tom Banton replaces Jacob Bethell at the top order, Jamie Overton has been deployed as an all-rounder role in Sam Curran's absence, while Rehan Ahmed replaces the injured Adil Rashid.

Sports.title: Trott replaces Flintoff as England Lions head coach
Sports.content:
Jonathan Trott will coach the England Lions this winter, filling the role vacated by Andrew Flintoff.

Flintoff stood down from the position with immediate effect in August, with Trott stepping in to lead the side's recent T20 series win over the touring Sri Lanka side.

Now the three-time Ashes winner, who previously enjoyed success as head coach of Afghanistan, has agreed to stay in post for next six months.

Trott, 45, will oversee a white-ball tour of the West Indies starting on October 27, a trip to South Africa which runs until December 23 and a third leg in Sri Lanka running between February and March.

Image: Andrew Flintoff stepped down as England Lions head coach in August

Trott was one of the names in the frame when England were looking for a new Test coach, a role which ultimately went to Stephen Fleming, having seen his stock rise by taking Afghanistan to a groundbreaking semi-final appearance at the T20 World Cup in 2024. He also completed a short consultancy stint with Ireland in July.

"I'm delighted to be back working in the England set-up and hugely excited to take on the role of head coach of the England Lions," he said.

"Having played for the Lions myself, I know how valuable the experience can be in helping players develop, both on and off the field, and it played an important part in my own journey.

Sports.title: What now for O'Neill and Celtic?
Sports.content:
There is no denying Martin O'Neill is a legend at Celtic, but is a change needed before their problems become a crisis?

The 74-year-old has already said he will take stock and decide if it is "time to wrap it up" following the 1-0 loss to Rangers at Parkhead.

That defeat was their second against the Old Firm rivals inside a week that also saw them go down 3-1 to Ferencvaros in the Europa League.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Rangers

Each display has been as concerning as the last, with the Hoops fans worried about what the rest of the season holds if nothing changes during the international break.

What the form says

Celtic started the latest defence of their Scottish Premiership title with six straight wins, but at times they were unconvincing.

Their epic collapse in their Champions League play-off against LASK - from 4-0 up to crashing out 5-4 on aggregate - raised questions about O'Neill and his players.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kris Boyd and Neil Lennon were left fearful for Celtic following a dismal display against Rangers

A pasting last weekend against Rangers in the Scottish League Cup, followed by another abject display in the Europa League, saw the pressure increase.

Then came a 1-0 loss to their Old Firm rivals in front of 60,000 of their own fans.

They are still top of the league heading into a three-week international break, but it is a two-point gap rather than the commanding eight-point lead they could have had.

Who is to blame for results?

Image: The Celtic fans have regularly protested against the board

It is easy to point the finger at the manager when the results do not come, but Celtic's problems are bigger than that.

There were fan protests against the club's board last season and calls for change at the top have not gone away.

Questions have been asked about the quality and timing of the summer signings.

While record signing Kasper Hogh and Camilo Duran were brought in before their Champions League exit, the club then spent almost £20 on Mika Baur, Haissem Hassan and Joel van den Berg before the transfer deadline.

O'Neill is still trying to find the best way to use them and his other five late signings in his team.

Image: Mika Baur and Haissem Hassan are two of the big summer signings

He has tried a series of different midfielders to no avail. He even dropped his wingers entirely in Sunday's Old Firm defeat, instead starting with five defenders and moving Kieran Tierney further forward. It was the same outcome.

Celtic have won 14 of the last 15 league titles without replacing some key players when they have been sold.

Some supporters feel domestic dominance has led to complacency from the board. But now there is a far stronger challenge from Rangers and Hearts.

Celtic have spent big this summer but many of them fear only a trophyless season will deliver their message that having vast money in the bank might not be more important than the right players on the pitch.

Is O'Neill's legacy at risk?

Image: Martin O'Neill delivered a league and cup double last season

Things can turn quickly in Scottish football.

O'Neill returned to Celtic twice last season as interim manager and managed to steady the ship to deliver what had seemed an unlikely league and cup double.

The 74-year-old decided he was not ready to return to retirement and took over at Parkhead on a permanent basis, 21 years after his first spell came to an end.

The Irishman was a force to be reckoned with during his first spell at Parkhead when he delivered seven major trophies and a UEFA Cup final place in 2003.

He had a side hard to beat, which is the opposite of what can be levelled at them this season.

Image: Martin O'Neill led Celtic to the UEFA Cup final in 2003

The Celtic supporters love Martin O'Neill, but even the most loyal are questioning whether it is time for him to walk away.

He made huge calls from the previous weekend's loss at Ibrox going into the clash with Ferencvaros in midweek.

They did not work. He made more changes for Rangers on Sunday and they also did not work.

He could still match last season's achievements. But if he cannot fix the big issues in his squad, he could be left with a trophyless season and a tarnished legacy.

Reason for optimism

With all the doom and gloom, it could be forgotten that Celtic are still top of the Scottish Premiership.

After Sunday's defeat to Rangers, O'Neill told Sky Sports he did not think "there's very much between the teams" and insisted "the history of the club proves it will fight back" from a week of turmoil.

He called for a bit of perspective, adding: "It's concerning. Is it a disaster? I don't think so. We have to rethink and reset."

He is right; the season is far from over.

They have played just seven of their 38 Premiership games and have another seven Europa League matches to play.

The current turmoil could still end in another season of success at Celtic.

He helped Les Bleus win the Championship three times, but head coach Fabien Galthie revealed in June he wanted to shake-up a back-room team that had been place in long-term.

Joining the England Women set-up on a short-term basis clears Edwards to be involved in the men's Six Nations, with his ambition being to link up with a side in time for the competition.

Sports.title: How Warwickshire can seal three-way battle for County Championship title
Sports.content:
The final round of fixtures in the County Championship begins on Thursday with three teams still in contention for the title, while who will be relegated from and promoted to Division One is also still to be decided.

Can Warwickshire close out title?

Warwickshire are the clear favourites to claim the Division One title for the first time since 2021.

They begin the final round 11 points clear at the top of the table and know that victory at home over Leicestershire will confirm them as champions.

Warwickshire could also win the title if they draw or lose, depending on the results of second-placed Somerset and third-placed Nottinghamshire.

If Somerset won, Warwickshire drew and the sides were tied on points, Somerset would claim the title by having seven victories to Warwickshire's six.

It's possible that Nottinghamshire and Warwickshire could finish tied on points with the same number of wins, losses and draws, which would see the title decided by which of the pair claimed more points in their two fixtures against each other this season.

That would be Nottinghamshire, who outpointed Warwickshire 27-24 by achieving more bonus scoring as the sides drew both of their clashes.

Leicestershire and Essex in battle for survival

With Hampshire's relegation from Division One already confirmed, Leicestershire and Essex are the other two sides at risk of going down.

Ninth-placed Leicestershire are 19 points behind eighth-placed Essex, which makes the former a heavy favourite to be relegated.

Leicestershire must achieve an upset victory over league leaders Warwickshire, and hope that Essex lose at Glamorgan.

Sports.title: Out-run? Walking too much? Man Utd's running stats examined
Sports.content:
Manchester United's intensity levels are back in the spotlight after their 1-1 draw at Fulham in the Premier League.

Matheus Cunha gave a damning view from inside the squad, telling Sky Sports: "They put in more energy than us, we cannot accept this."

Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville said: "I've never seen a Man Utd team walk out of possession as much as that."

So what do the stats say about United's work-rate at Craven Cottage - and how big a problem is it for Michael Carrick?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville was unhappy with the lack of running from the Manchester United team out of possession during their draw with Fulham in the Premier League.

High-speed runs

Man Utd rank joint-bottom in the Premier League for high-speed runs, according to Opta.

They are level with Man City on 1691 high-speed runs - but their neighbours played with 10 men for the majority of the derby at Old Trafford, which needs to be factored into their figures.

Walking

Man Utd spent 52.98 per cent of their time out of possession at Fulham walking.

Seven teams have posted a higher figure this term, although it is the highest percentage Man Utd have recorded this season.

United's average for this campaign of 51.13 per cent ranks them 17th in the Premier League.

Image: Manchester United's numbers out of possession, according to Genius IQ

Since the start of last season there have been 30 times a team has spent a greater percentage of time walking out of possession in a Premier League match than Man Utd did at Fulham.

That includes the 54.59 per cent United recorded in their 3-0 win at Brighton on the final day of last season.

Distance covered

Man Utd ran 110.2km on Sunday - the second-lowest total of the Premier League weekend, behind Liverpool's 108.4km figure at Bournemouth.

Image: Fulham and Manchester United - running stats from their Premier League match

United ran 6.5km less than Fulham - the second biggest difference between teams this season when both keep 11 men on the pitch. (Arsenal out-ran Coventry by 6.8km on the opening night of the season).

Man Utd have also been out-run in terms of distance by Hull, Ipswich and Everton this season. Man City - who had Phil Foden sent off after 23 minutes - are the only side United have run further than in the Premier League this term.

Image: Man Utd have been out-run by every Premier League opponent this season, except for Man City, who had a player sent off

Dropping deep

Man Utd allowed Fulham to start their passing sequences, on average, 36.9m from the United goal. That is the nearest any team allowed their opponents to begin from, on average, in the Premier League this past weekend.

It reflects how United sat deep out of possession at Craven Cottage.

Fulham, by contrast, allowed United to start attacks 43.4m from their goal, on average - the third-highest figure of the latest round of matches.

Allowing Fulham to pass

In his post-match analysis, Neville referenced Fulham's amount of 10+ passing sequences.

Fulham had more 'build-up attacks' (10+ passing sequences that end in a shot or touch in the opposition box) than any other side this weekend.

But was it all part of the plan?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manchester United boss Michael Carrick reflects on their draw with Fulham in the Premier League.

It's worth pointing out United boss Carrick rejected the suggestion United had energy issues in the game when Cunha's quotes were put to him in his post-match press conference. "The way we finished the game it didn't look like that for me," he said.

Their 'progress' stat, measuring metres gained per passing sequence, was top for this latest round of Premier League games, showing how they were able to advance far up the pitch from their deep starting position when they won the ball back off Fulham.

In fact, their 36 penalty-box entries was the most of any team in any Premier League game this season.

United had 29 shots at Fulham - including two against the woodwork in the first half. That has contributed to their total of 113 shots this season, which is the most of any team.

They also have the third-best Expected Goals total in the Premier League of 10.24.

So what does it all mean?

The problem for Carrick is those positive numbers around their attacking play are overshadowed by taking just five points from their first five games - at the beginning of a campaign where United fans had been excited about their team kicking on from their third-place finish last season.

Their frustrations around results and performances have then been further fuelled by low-ranking running stats.

A failure to beat bottom-of-the-table Tottenham after the international break would turn this into United's worst-ever start to a Premier League season and raise more hard-hitting questions about the output of Carrick's team.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel rocked by five key withdrawals from England squad
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel has been rocked by a host of withdrawals from his England squad, with Cole Palmer, Declan Rice, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento all out because of injury issues. The manager has called up James Garner and Morgan Gibbs-White to boost his options for the upcoming Nations League programme.

Tuchel gave Palmer a high-profile recall last Friday for the beginning of the new two-year international cycle that he hopes will end in glory at Euro 2028. England are back in Nations League Group A and they kick off against Spain at Wembley on Saturday. They then play Czechia and Croatia away before returning to Wembley to face Czechia.

Palmer has felt a minor muscle issue and, not for the first time under Tuchel, has been forced to make himself unavailable. The Chelsea midfielder, who has started the season in fine form, has made only three appearances under Tuchel. He was left out of the World Cup squad after his formed ebbed last season and Tuchel spoke at his squad announcement of a fresh opportunity for Palmer. That will have to wait. The 24-year-old has been a virtual ever-present for Chelsea this season, contributing four goals and two assists in all competitions.

Rice’s withdrawal is not a complete surprise given his workload for a number of seasons. He needed to manage a nerve issue in a hamstring in the second-half of last season which also affected his lower back and caused the midfielder discomfort at the World Cup. He has started all of Arsenal’s Premier League matches so far this season – plus their Champions League opener against Napoli. It has been decided that a rest at this point is the wisest course of action.

Mainoo was taken off after 80 minutes of Manchester United’s game at Fulham on Sunday; a move from the manager, Michael Carrick, that led to boos from the travelling support. The midfielder was in the World Cup squad but he was the only outfield player not to get a single minute on the pitch. Tuchel has said that Mainoo’s lack of involvement was no slight on him; his ability or application levels. It was, instead, purely down to decisions that Tuchel took for technical reasons. The manager had promised to give Mainoo minutes over the coming fortnight or so.

Mainoo’s United teammate, Rashford, was substituted in the 77th minute of the Fulham game and he was seen holding the area by the front of his hip and groin as he slowly walked off. Tuchel has always championed Rashford; he called him up when he named his first squad in March of last year when the player was struggling for form. The manager wanted to show Rashford that he believed in him and he has always included the 28-year-old when he has been available.

Tuchel seemed to lose a bit of faith after Rashford played poorly against the Democratic Republic of the Congo in the last 32 of the World Cup over the summer. Thereafter, Tuchel barely used him until England’s semi-final exit against Argentina, giving him a couple of minutes as a stoppage-time substitute in that game but nothing more. He did play him for the first 45 minutes of the third place play-off against France.

Livramento was named in the World Cup squad only to suffer a calf injury in training on the eve of the tournament. The Newcastle full-back had to fly home. He underwent surgery and only returned for his club as a substitute against Bournemouth at the start of the month. He suffered a set-back in training before Newcastle’s win over Hull on Saturday and was not in the matchday squad. The 23-year-old is yet to start a game this season.

Garner comes in as a central midfield replacement for Rice and Mainoo while Gibbs-White adds to Tuchel’s options in the No 10 position in the absence of Palmer. Tuchel also has Jude Bellingham, Morgan Rogers and Eberechi Eze as No 10s. The players are due to report to St George’s Park on Tuesday.

Sports.title: WSL talking points: Arsenal’s attacking woes and Goodwin makes England case
Sports.content:
1 Why do Arsenal struggle to break down low blocks?

After being unable to find a way through Crystal Palace’s backline last time out, Arsenal were again frustrated at home in a draw with Manchester United on Saturday and Renée Slegers was asked post-match about how her team can turn their dominance of possession and territory into more goals. It could have been worse, of course, if Smilla Holmberg had not made it 1-1 in the 95th minute. “It’s not one thing, it’s a combination of things,” Slegers said. “It’s a cocktail of things, there are some details in decision making, some details in the technical execution. It’s also the ruthlessness in front of goal but I know the players want it and they want to do that, they want to execute for Arsenal.” Tom Garry

2 A good win for Lionesses, Goodwin for England?

Just over a week before Sarina Wiegman names her Lionesses squad for October’s World Cup play-off tie against Greece, the England Under-23 international Isobel Goodwin did her chances of a first senior selection no harm at all, as she scored twice for London City Lionesses in a comprehensive 4-1 victory at Charlton. The 23-year-old, who linked up well with Alexia Putellas, scored five times in the WSL last term but will be keen to exceed that this season and impress Wiegman, particularly at a time when Chelsea’s Aggie Beever-Jones has been out with a minor ankle injury and Arsenal’s Michelle Agyemang is still returning from her ACL. Wiegman may be considering alternative options for a backup striker to Alessia Russo for these key fixtures. TG

3 Hemp adds goals to her repertoire

She was the WSL’s leading assist-provider in the 2023-24 and 2024-25 seasons and supplied the joint-second highest number of assists last season, but goals were not coming regularly for the England winger Lauren Hemp, who had not scored in the WSL since last November until she decisively found the net twice on Friday night in a 4-2 win over Liverpool. The Manchester City boss, Andrée Jeglertz, heaped praise on Hemp as he told Sky Sports: “She’s an amazing player. I don’t know what she’s made of, because she just loves to be on the field and looks like she has so much energy. She’s a game-changer.” Hemp nearly had a hat-trick but she saw an early, rising strike tipped over the bar by Khiara Keating. TG

View image in fullscreen Manchester City’s Lauren Hemp scores against Liverpool Photograph: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

4 Potter shines at the heart of Chelsea’s midfield

There has been plenty of debate in recent months about the future of young English players in theWSL and whether they are being hampered by limited opportunities. England’s Lexi Potter, however, is one such young talent who has been catching the eye at the heart of Chelsea’s midfield. The 2-0 win over Birmingham City was her second start in as many matches and she produced yet another assured performance. The 20-year-old’s calmness and ability to work in tight spaces enables her to escape pressure while the timing of her runs into the box is a huge asset. She opened the scoring at Stamford Bridge by being alert to the second ball in the area while her burgeoning relationship with Keira Walsh has been notable. “They understand each other, and even when they are on the pitch and they close their eyes, they know where each other is,” Sonia Bompastor told Chelsea media. Like Goodwin, may she have done enough to catch Wiegman’s eye? Sophie Downey

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

5 Another own goal sends Everton up to fifth

How do you register six points without scoring a single goal? Everton completed this remarkable feat after a late winner at West Ham – an own goal from defender Laia Codina – gave them all three points. It was the second time in as many weeks that a touch from their opponent handed them a victory but it will not matter to Scott Phelan’s side who sit pretty at fifth in the table. It was an even affair for the most parts in Dagenham with both setups nullifying the other. The Toffees looked defensively resilient, handling the threat of Kelly Gago and Viviane Asseyi comfortably. Down the other end, West Ham did the same with the visitors’ attack. Both had an equal share of possession, both had similar xGs and both registered just three shots on target. Everton’s ability to finish strongly, however, was the difference maker. Phelan turned to his bench and they were able to ratchet up the pressure with Yuka Momiki providing the delivery for the winner. SD

View image in fullscreen Ruby Mace celebrates after Laia Codina of West Ham United (not pictured) scores an own-goal. Photograph: James Fearn/Getty Images

6 Holdt ignites Spurs on way to rout

Olivia Holdt marked her first start of the season by scoring a hat-trick as Spurs turned a dominant but goalless first half into a 7-0 win at Crystal Palace. Palace’s task was made harder when Fuka Tsunoda was sent off in the seventh minute following a reckless challenge on Cathinka Tandberg, but Spurs initially struggled to break down a side defending deep. “When they got the red card, I was thinking this could actually be tougher for us,” Holdt said. At half-time, the Spurs manager, Martin Ho, asked his players to get more bodies into the box. Holdt had completed her hat-trick by the 73rd minute as Spurs finally found the ruthlessness that had been missing. Mitul Samji

7 Brighton’s lack of clinical edge proves costly

Brighton may have had 25 shots, eight on target and an xG of 3.17, but they were forced to settle for a 1-1 draw against Aston Villa after failing to make their dominance count. Gabby George’s first goal for the club gave them a deserved lead in the 31st minute, but they could not find a second despite creating a total of 15 chances. The result was made all the more frustrating by the manner of Villa’s equaliser in the 89th minute, with Brighton unable to defend a corner. The result leaves the new manager, Arturo Ruiz, still searching for their first win of the season. “Here in our stadium, in these kinds of games we cannot lose two points,” he said. “We need to get three points in 100% of these games.” The performance was encouraging, but the finishing was not. Réshma Rao

Sports.title: Granit Xhaka admits to receiving fake Covid vaccination certificate in 2022
Sports.content:
Granit Xhaka has been withdrawn from Switzerland’s squad after he admitted receiving a fake Covid vaccination certificate in 2022. The Sunderland and Switzerland captain – who was an Arsenal player at the time – has apologised for this “mistake” and will sit out his country’s forthcoming four Nations League matches.

Xhaka is poised to be questioned by the prosecutor’s office in Lucerne next week as it decides whether any criminal proceedings will be initiated regarding the alleged issue of a series of false Covid certificates by a doctor based in the Swiss city during the pandemic. The doctor, who was first investigated in 2023, has denied the allegations.

In a statement issued via Instagram, Xhaka acknowledged he had decided not to be inoculated against the virus. “In recent days there has been much reporting about a matter from my past. I would like to address this personally,” he wrote. “At the time, I was personally very uncertain and had serious concerns regarding the Covid-19 vaccination. I felt deep distrust of the vaccine and was plagued by fear and uncertainty.

“In this turbulent emotional state, I obtained a vaccination certificate instead of clarifying my open questions through the proper channels. Today I clearly see this was not the right course of action. It was a mistake. I am sorry. I take responsibility for this decision, am committed to investigating the matter and am co-operating with the relevant authorities.”

Xhaka tested positive for Covid in September 2022 and the 33-year-old – he turns 34 on Sunday – did not feature in Switzerland’s internationals that month.

A spokesperson for the Lucerne cantonal prosector’s office said: “The aim [of the inquiries] is to clarify whether there has been conduct relevant under criminal law in connection with the possible fraudulent obtaining of a false certification and/or document forgery.”

Should charges be brought, Xhaka could face a heavy fine or, theoretically, a five-year prison sentence. However, the imposition of the latter sanction – or any sort of custodial punishment – is understood to be extremely unlikely.

Given that Xhaka was with Arsenal in 2022, Sunderland have told the Guardian they are not commenting on the matter. The midfielder left north London to join Bayer Leverkusen in 2023 and arrived at the Stadium of Light two years later.
