Sports.title: Ghosts of 2023 surface after Dortmund return to the Bundesliga summit | Andy Brassell
Sports.content:
Borussia Dortmund would probably rather not think about the last time that they topped the Bundesliga. It was in May 2023, just before all their dreams imploded, with black and yellow Deutscher Meister t-shirts – ‘German champions’ – for sale on the approach to Signal Iduna Park and cold beers at the ready. Now, that is no longer the most recent time Dortmund have led the pack.

It’s four games, four wins to start this season and the Niko Kovac workout plan is hitting the spot. Saturday night’s single-goal win at Stuttgart was a game that had the gravitas of a true Topspiel, if not quite the entertainment value of one. Kovac’s fingerprints were all over it. The conversation of whether his view of the game fits with BVB’s swashbuckling image will no doubt continue, but this was a case in point to show just how good Kovac has been for the club, and for the team.

Dortmund had taken four points from the two games against Sebastian Hoeness and his Stuttgart team last season – and just as Kovac will not be oblivious to criticism of his side’s style, nor is Hoeness to whispers about his impressive team’s waning record against direct rivals – but were hardly overwhelmingly impressive either. It had been a huge improvement on the 2024-25 encounters with Stuttgart, in which BVB had been well beaten, twice, once under the short reign of Nuri Sahin and once in Kovac’s first game in charge, at which point he must have realised the mountainous task ahead of him.

Here, in September 2026, was the clearest of markers of how far Dortmund have come under the former Croatia midfielder and how deeply his ideas have taken root. To see a Dortmund patient, poised and defensively competent enough to grind this game out is still a novelty, and they didn’t have a shot on target until Maximilian Beier prodded in the winner from an inviting ball in by substitute Jobe Bellingham. That Dortmund dealt with everything the home side had in response, with street smarts and limited fuss, was laudable. They made a very accomplished attacking forced look ordinary. “In a top match,” Stuttgart’s Hoeness later reflected, “decent and okay aren’t enough.”

That Bellingham and Beier combined for the goal was noteworthy too; the former frequently rubbished for not being the equal of his generationally-talented elder brother and the latter another player who is simply underrated, both were brought in for big money and accordingly viewed with little patience. Their adaptability was striking, with Bellingham impacting off the bench and Beier thriving in a more advanced role. They are both Kovac’s type: young, willing, athletic and adaptable.

View image in fullscreen Niko Kovac has been in charge of Borussia Dortmund since January 2025. Photograph: Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

Should we call Dortmund contenders? That is, perhaps, a bit strong. But there is talk is about reducing the 16-point gap to Bayern that remained at the end of last season, and there were signs here that they may, at least, be capable of that. “It’s about annoying Bayern a bit”, is how Dortmund managing director Lars Ricken framed it, following the win at Stuttgart.

Dortmund were never going to return to relevance and consistency by trying to relive the Jürgen Klopp years, or by trying to ape Bayern (and yes, both of those approaches have been attempted). To get into the position where they can face the hurt (and potential rewards) of 2023 all over again will take a while, and doesn’t just depend on them – it will take Bayern falling down a rung or two. They are at least climbing the right ladder though, slowly, steadily, and diligently.

Quick Guide Bundesliga results Show Bayern Munich 7-0 Union Berlin, Stuttgart 0-1 Borussia Dortmund, Werder Bremen 3-2 Augsburg, Hamburg 2-1 Köln, Eintracht Frankfurt 2-2 Freiburg, Borussia Mönchengladbach 3-4 Mainz, Paderborn 3-1 Hoffenheim, Schalke 0-0 Elversberg, Bayer Leverkusen 2-0 RB Leipzig Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Talking points

It was only a matter of time and it was probably always going to happen against an ailing Union Berlin, who are enduring a horrible start to the season, but Harry Kane reached 100 Bundesliga goals on Friday night in his 98th game, so much faster than anyone in the league’s history. His double was almost a footnote on a night as Michael Olise scored a dazzling hat-trick, with Jamal Musiala and Ismaël Saibari also netting their first league goals of the season in a 7-0 shellacking. It was a good start to the club’s traditional celebration of Oktoberfest weekend.

Bayern later mourned Peter Hermann, Jupp Heynckes’ popular assistant in the 2013 treble-winning season, who passed away on Saturday at the age of 73. Hermann was also emotionally commemorated at Leverkusen before kick-off on Sunday, having played in their 1979 promotion-winning team and having later served as assistant to Klaus Toppmöller at the helm of the celebrated 2002 Champions League finalists. Die Werkself paid fitting tribute on the field too as they beat RB Leipzig 2-0. The margins were fine, with Christopher Nkunku having an opener ruled out for the visitors before Patrik Schick put the home side ahead from a Miguel Gutiérrez cross. Gutiérrez, Álex Grimaldo’s nominal replacement, scored the second himself. Carles Martínez praised his team for “good balance between keeping the ball and playing forward”, while his opposite number Martín Demichelis has plenty to think about after a fourth straight away defeat.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Bayer Leverkusen players and fans hold a minute of silence for Peter Hermann. Photograph: Martin Meissner/AP

Never before had a team scored three times in successive Bundesliga home games and lost both of them but Borussia Mönchengladbach are managing to find a ledge beneath the edge. Gladbach made a bright start against Mainz (who are under interim coach Jan-Moritz Lichte) – with Florian Neuhaus scoring the opener on his return to the line-up, his first since May 2024 – but ended in defeat again, leaving them bottom, without a point. Alexander Blessin, a former St Pauli coach famed for his defensive work, is expected to arrive in an attempt to plug the leaks.

Hamburg had gone into matchday four pointless and goalless but managed to squeeze past a Köln side who dominated them, with Yussuf Poulsen’s second goal for the club since arriving in summer 2025 proving decisive. It was an endorsement of their faith in head coach Merlin Polzin, who signed a contract extension this week despite that bad start and successive 5-0 defeats.

There are comebacks and there are comebacks, and several coincided on the Weser as Werder Bremen continued their surprisingly good start to the season. They trailed 2-0 to Wolfsburg but were level after a Niclas Füllkrug netbuster but even better was around the corner, with Mitchell Weiser rattling in a perfect left-foot winner, deep into stoppage time, in his first home appearance after 16 months out with injury. It brought the former Bayern man to tears and his coach Daniel Thoune described it as “a goosebump moment”.

All three promoted teams now have a win after Paderborn’s shock victory over Hoffenheim in Sunday’s late game, with veteran substitute Steffen Tigges sealing it with a header for his first top-flight goal since 2024. It was a third loss in four for Hoffenheim, who also suffered an embarrassing Europa League reverse at OFI Crete on Thursday.

Sports.title: Champions Inter deny would-be title rivals Roma as Martínez haunts Gasperini | Nicky Bandini
Sports.content:
Gian Piero Gasperini could not keep himself from smiling. His Roma team had just squandered a two-goal lead at home to Inter but as he crossed the Stadio Olimpico pitch to greet the man who had led the visitors’ comeback, his lips formed into a grin.

“He always scores against me”, explained a laughing Gasperini when he was asked what he had said to Lautaro Martínez a short while after. “I told him to stop it! He does it to everyone, though. He’s a great champion, everyone thinks very highly of him, even if he makes all of us suffer.”

The game had finished 2-2, Martínez’s second-half goals cancelling out a pair from Manu Koné. Two points dropped for Gasperini’s Giallorossi, yet also one made in the standings and one to their rivals, to their fans, to themselves. After winning their opening four games, they had stood toe to toe with the champions and landed confident punches, even if they could not find a knockout blow.

At the start of this second season under Gasperini, Roma look more than ever like a team in his image: taking the game to their opponents high up the pitch, engaging man-to-man and seeking opportunity from individual duels.

The risks were evident even in the moments leading up to Koné’s sixth-minute opener, with possession swapping rapidly and the Roma centre-back Leonardo Balerdi staying alert to intercept a through-ball from Yann Bisseck for Martínez. Roma’s rewards were reaped when Paulo Dybala’s cross was headed down by Nahuel Molina for Koné to sweep home.

Koné is an unlikely scoring threat. He has found the net twice in each of his two seasons at Roma but matched that by the 37th minute of this game, arriving at the edge of the six-yard box to convert again from another Dybala delivery, this time after a touch from Gianluca Mancini. The goal was initially disallowed before a VAR review confirmed neither player had been offside.

View image in fullscreen Manu Koné (centre) scores his second goal for Roma against Inter. Photograph: Nicola Ianuale/Shutterstock

Roma had been the better team but also ridden their luck. Not long before Koné’s second, Martínez missed an open goal from point-blank range and Alessandro Bastoni hit the post from a narrow angle. These Inter warnings went unheeded. Less than a minute into the second half, Martínez released Marcus Thuram down the left and the Argentinian sprinted through the middle to receive the return, finishing brilliantly into the bottom corner in between three defenders.

If Roma are establishing their identity in year two under Gasperini, then perhaps the same is true for Inter under Cristian Chivu. They are, to belabour our previous boxing metaphor, Serie A’s Rocky Balboa, a team who can walk – sometimes quite naively – into a flurry of punches, weather all of them and swing back twice as hard.

This was the fourth game in a row that Inter had fallen 2-0 behind and the third of those in which they avoided a defeat. The champions overcame such deficits to beat Napoli and Udinese this month and might have done the same away to Real Madrid in the Champions League if it weren’t for some brilliant goalkeeping by Thibaut Courtois.

Here, Mile Svilar kept Inter at bay. Roma’s goalkeeper made a stunning reflex stop to keep out Thuram’s header at a corner, before Martínez nodded the rebound on to the bar, when Inter’s talisman finally equalised in the 79th minute.

Inter had created more than enough chances to deserve the draw. Yet things could have gone differently still. In the 68th minute, with the score still 2-1, Donyell Malen brought down a Dybala corner and swivelled to fire a rocket into the face of Inter’s keeper Josep Martínez.

It was a thrilling spectacle for the neutral, and a game which both sides might walk away from feeling both encouragement and frustration. Away from home, against one of their most likely challengers for the title, Inter had reminded us once again of their resilience and depth. Owning the best attacker in the league helps a great deal.

Still, it cannot really be a sustainable plan to keep spotting your opponents a two-goal head-start. One Inter player after another was asked why they keep opening games so badly, and all came back with some variation on: “I have no idea.” Chivu started his post-game interview on Dazn by saying: “I’m going to talk about the second half, because the things I had to say about the first will stay between me and the team.”

View image in fullscreen Roma manager Gian Piero Gasperini (left) embraces his Inter counterpart Cristian Chivu before the match. Photograph: Ciro De Luca/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

Roma have the opposite problem, repeatedly starting well only to allow opponents into games. All three times they have failed to keep a clean sheet this season – against Inter, Atalanta and Fenerbahce – they have conceded within three minutes of the second-half restart.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Gasperini had already acknowledged the trend after Roma’s Champions League draw with the Turkish side, nodding to Agatha Christie with his joking assessment that “two coincidences are a proof”. In her original, of course, three is the number required to meet that threshold. A number which has now been reached.

“We need to keep our focus on our own business,” he said when asked whether his team was ready to compete for the Scudetto. “We need to take this awareness that, in the right conditions, we can be a really good, dangerous, team.”

That they most certainly are. Malen might not have scored, but he has six goals already in this Serie A season – two more than Martínez – continuing the prolific form since joining from Aston Villa in January. Dybala has four recorded assists and that does not include either goal against Inter, despite both being the result of his delivery.

Quick Guide Serie A results Show Monza 2-1 Sassuolo, Venezia 0-2 Lazio, Roma 2-2 Internazionale, Udinese 0-1 Cagliari, Bologna 1-1 Torino, Milan 3-0 Lecce, Juventus 2-0 Atalanta, Parma 2-1 Genoa, Frosinone 2-0 Como, Fiorentina 1-1 Napoli Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Gasperini’s three-pronged attack of those two with Matías Soulé, or the 19-year-old Rodrigo Mora, is fast becoming one of the most menacing in Serie A. Meanwhile the recovery speed of Balerdi, signed from Marseille, looks a huge asset to a team playing with such a high defensive line.

The unanswered question is whether this team has the depth to sustain a challenge to Inter – whose strength in that area was on display again. Chivu could bring Petar Sucic off the bench to replace a struggling Curtis Jones, as well as Carlos Augusto for Federico Dimarco. He kept Martínez and Thuram on until the 90th minute, in recognition of how well they were playing, but Francesco Pio Esposito and Ange-Yoan Bonny are extraordinarily strong late replacements.

Roma need to see more from their most expensive summer signing, Santiago Castro, as an alternative in their own attack, but after five games Gasperini’s glass is more than half full. “We played Inter when they are in peak condition,” he added. “Maybe, over the course of a season, it won’t always be that way.”

And perhaps there will even come a day when Martínez doesn’t score against him. Then again, perhaps not. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, the Argentinian is unbeaten in 17 games against teams coached by Gasperini, winning 12 and drawing five, while racking up 11 goals.

“Una sentenza”, as they say in Italy – an inescapable sentence. But Martínez is only one part of the bigger picture. This September clash between defending champions and would-be contenders left us with more intriguing questions than definitive answers.

Sports.title: Manchester United’s engine room runs out of steam as fans voice frustration | Jacob Steinberg
Sports.content:
One of the more damning aspects of Manchester United’s tortured rebuild is their inability to multitask. So much money has been frittered away, pushing United into the ridiculous position of going one position at a time each summer. Last year was all about the attack and the recent window was about central midfield, even though the options at full-back do not look strong enough to cope with a season back in the Champions League.

United remain a listless, drifting operation. The ownership is reviled and the fanbase is becoming increasingly mutinous. It was not just Gary Neville seeing red as he commentated on United’s dismal efforts away to winless Fulham. There was an ominous shift in the mood in the away end at Craven Cottage, summed up by the boos that greeted Michael Carrick substituting Kobbie Mainoo with 10 minutes to go.

Carrick filled in as an emergency centre-back when United last lost this fixture, way back in December 2009. This has been a happy hunting ground since then and there was a sense of inevitability to United saving themselves on Sunday, although that was more to do with Fulham’s nerves at 1-0 up than any great show of defiance from the visitors when a third defeat in the space of a week was on the cards.

The late equaliser was fortunate, Matheus Cunha’s potshot hitting the luckless David Affengruber before going in. Bernd Leno was deceived in the Fulham goal but United did not fool anyone by stirring only after falling behind to Lisandro Martínez’s slapstick own goal. Speaking on Sky Sports, Neville called out the lack of effort during the 15 minutes before Fulham’s goal. Players went through the motions and pulled out of tackles, while the manner of the concession was feeble.

United could not get out of their box and when Cunha melted in a challenge with Calvin Bassey, the Fulham centre-back barrelled forward before testing Senne Lammens, only for Martínez to turn the rebound past his goalkeeper. It was a farcical goal and in keeping with the flow at that stage. United had no control or presence in midfield. Bruno Fernandes was the No 10 and Mainoo was deeper with Youri Tielemans, signed from Aston Villa last summer, but the ease with which Sander Berge and Shea Charles dominated for Fulham was proof that Carrick’s renovation in the engine room remains a work in progress.

It is interesting that United targeted quantity during a summer in which rival clubs were spending so much on midfielders. Andrey Santos, an unused substitute here, joined from Chelsea for £50m but is yet to prove himself in English football. Tielemans was an opportunistic £35m. Manchester City spent £300m on three midfielders, while Arsenal added depth by buying Bruno Guimarães for £75m. Carrick will hope that Carlos Baleba, back from an ankle injury, makes his debut after the international break.

United were outrun by Fulham. They looked unfit and need Baleba to provide oomph. There were times when Fulham ripped through the middle, particularly in transition. Alex Iwobi surged away from Tielemans during the first half. Josh King’s raids down the inside-right channel caught the eye and Fulham repeatedly cut through before half-time, only for poor finishing to let them down.

Carrick raised eyebrows by saying United controlled a lot of the first half. Cunha was close to the mark by saying Fulham “put in more energy than us” at the start of the second half. One worry is that the players are already not following Carrick’s instructions. Another is that the window-by-window rebuild has still left United short of ideas in midfield and attack.

View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes was unable to inspire his teammates to beat Fulham. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

Those areas were meant to have been sorted. Instead, United were ponderous on and off the ball. There were flashes in attack but they did not convince. While allowances have to be made for Benjamin Sesko missing out through injury, leaving United short of an effective target man to introduce, the lack of quality in the final third was stark.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Only a defensive error from Fulham led to Fernandes hitting the post at 0-0. Cunha also clipped the woodwork, albeit via a heavy deflection, and Marcus Rashford wasted two opportunities.

It is odd that the new-look attack still means a start for Rashford, who was up for sale last year. He played on the left and flattered to deceive before being taken off. Yet Rashford is not the only United forward who can look promising before drifting out of games. Bryan Mbeumo almost equalised but had an inconsistent game on the right. Cunha looks uncomfortable playing as the No 9 but Carrick does not appear to trust Sesko.

Carrick is under pressure. United have five points from five games and are already out of the Carabao Cup. The doubts over whether Carrick deserved the job will grow. But he is not the first United manager to struggle because of wider failings and is unlikely to be the last. It was not ideal, after all, that Carrick had to bring Joshua Zirkzee on when United were chasing an equaliser. The Dutch forward has five league goals since joining two years ago. Why has he not been sold? Some rebuild.

Sports.title: Maresca dismisses title talk as ‘too early’ after Manchester City take over at the top
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca dismissed ­Manchester City pulling ahead in the title race after Sunday’s 5-3 win over Sunderland, with the manager stating it is “too early” in the season.

The frantic victory at the Etihad Stadium gave City 15 points from their opening five league matches, three more than Arsenal after the champions lost at Brighton on Saturday. Maresca was asked about his team being top before the three-week international break.

“It’s much better to win games,” he said. “In this moment, it’s better to have three points more than less, no doubt. But at the same time, we know that it’s quite early. The international break is good. We can review what we have done and what we can do better, and at the same time, we can relax a little more.”

Of the victory against Sunderland, Maresca said: “I prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3 but I expected a very difficult game – I knew how good they are, off the ball, very aggressive. I knew it was a difficult game but happy because we found a way to win the game.

“We scored five. We could have scored probably more goals. So that means that we create enough, but at the same time we need to avoid conceding goals like today. We had four clean sheets in a row and today we conceded three goals.”

City twice took the lead in the first half after goals from Enzo Fernández and Rayan Cherki, yet each time Sunderland found equalisers from Brian Brobbey, before Antoine Semenyo’s 43rd-minute strike gave the home team a 3-2 half-time lead.

After the break the winger’s second made it 4-2 before Brobbey completed his hat-trick to make it 4-3 on 59 minutes. While Erling Haaland’s late strike completed the scoring Brobbey became the first player to score three and be on the losing side in the Premier League since Roque Santa Cruz in Blackburn’s 5-3 loss at Wigan in December 2007.

At 3-2 Elliot Anderson appeared to handle in his area but was not penalised and City subsequently launched the attack that created Semenyo’s second.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Régis Le Bris, Sunderland’s manager, said: “It was hard to see that as not a handball. It is what it is and we have to accept the decision. It’s hard to comment. It’s a defeat, but we are proud of the level of the squad. It is really tight at this level against one of the best teams in Europe. A half chance gets punished, and it’s probably the lesson of the day.”

Sports.title: ‘We miss her the same every day’: Olivia Cusack on her late footballer sister Maddy
Sports.content:
Olivia Cusack says her sister, the late Maddy Cusack, is on her mind every single day and she is determined to ensure her “legacy lives on” three years after the former England youth international midfielder’s death.

Olivia, together with family and friends of Maddy, walked 29 miles from Bramall Lane, Sheffield United’s home, to their family’s home in Horsley, near Derby, on Saturday to raise funds and awareness. Maddy’s loved ones are still enduring a “frustrating and confusing” wait for answers about the circumstances surrounding her death on 20 September 2023.

An inquest into the death of the 27-year-old Sheffield United player was adjourned again in July and has been scheduled to resume on 7 December after fresh evidence came to light. Cusack, a former England under-19 international, was the first player to appear in 100 matches for the Sheffield United women’s team.

Olivia says the walk on Saturday, “Bringing Maddy Home”, was motivated by some of the evidence during the inquest. “After the inquest we wanted to bring her home from Bramall Lane, back to our family home,” she says. “Many people know Maddy as the professional football player and the name on the back of her shirt, the number, the colours she wore, the club she was associated with.

“But I felt in the inquest it was lost that she was a person, she wasn’t an object that we were discussing. She’s a person, she’s a family member of ours [and] a person that’s sometimes been lost within the chaos surrounding her death really, so that’s the notion behind the walk. To claim her back, bring her home and protect her.”

A minute’s applause will be held before kick-off on Sunday at the Women’s Super League 2 fixture between Newcastle and Sheffield United. Discussing that anniversary, Olivia says: “We miss her the same every day, as I will on Sunday. The anniversary is always something that creeps up on us. It’s very emotional and it’s a time where we just reflect, but we do so much throughout the year so she really is at the heart of pretty much every single day. Not a day goes by where we don’t think about her.

View image in fullscreen Sheffield United and Maddy Cusack’s family paid tribute at Bramall Lane shortly after her death. Photograph: Richard Callis/MB Media/Getty Images

“There can be days when you just feel absolutely drained and you know you don’t quite know what the right thing to do is, but I think the way that we just get through it is that we remember who she was as a person. She loved her life, she loved trying new things and just enjoying life’s simple pleasures, we try and embody that on every day, not just the anniversary.

“I really do encourage people to, as difficult as it can be sometimes, share the photos, share the memories, bring her up in conversation wherever you can, talk about her, and between all of us, you know her legacy will live on.”

The family have already endured eight full days of evidence, after the hearing began belatedly on 29 June, but the discovery of additional documents led the proceedings to be paused until December. The coroner apologised to the family for yet another delay. The case had been set previously to start being heard on 5 January 2026 after additional postponements in 2025.

“It’s been really difficult,” Olivia said of the delays. “It’s not something that any of us anticipated to happen. It’s very confusing and it can be very frustrating, the length of time it’s taken, it can be difficult to work that out and to know how you should be feeling and the process of it. However, we know that for the right outcome it has to be taken seriously. They need the time to come together and really get an outcome.

View image in fullscreen Maddy Cusack was also remembered during the Premier League match between Sheffield United and Newcastle. Photograph: George Wood/Getty Images

“It feels as though she can’t be at peace until it’s finished. And I do feel that’s quite upsetting to think about and to work through. It needs to come to a conclusion.”

Olivia said she would “channel Maddy’s energy” during the 29-mile walk on Saturday, when a group of about 15 family and friends travelled in the reverse direction to another fundraising walk in February 2024 from Pride Park to Bramall Lane.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

This time they set off from Sheffield at 5.30am. A fundraising page for the walk had surpassed £1,100 as of Saturday afternoon. Olivia described that tally as “incredible – £1,000 is just amazing, it’s more than I ever expected” and said: “Particularly with it being Maddy’s anniversary, it’s going to be very much a mental challenge as well as a physical one, so it gives you that extra motivation to make the people who’ve donated proud.”

The money is being raised for the Maddy Cusack Foundation, which is helping a range of causes targeting women’s and girls’ football and “letting girls be seen within sport”.

“We provided Derby County Community Trust with a series of bursaries for girls and families who struggle with the financial prospects of becoming dedicated to their football. It’s a helping hand for any child that needs that extra sort of funding, taking away the barriers that they might face.”

The foundation has also partnered with the Stockport County left wing-back and former Derby, Sheffield United and Nottingham Forest player defender Ben Osborn’s organisation Elite Football Development, which aims to inspire young people through sport and education.

“They work with girls and boys but we sponsor the girls’ side of things, which is focused around post-16 study, and allows girls to gain qualifications alongside being able to train and live the life of a professional footballer. We were really keen to get involved in this as Maddy was really passionate about education.”

In the UK and Ireland, Samaritans can be contacted on freephone 116 123. In the US, you can call or text the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline on 988, chat on 988lifeline.org, or text HOME to 741741 to connect with a crisis counsellor. In Australia, the crisis support service Lifeline is 13 11 14. Other international helplines can be found at befrienders.org

Sports.title: Andre Villas-Boas finally responds to John Terry’s claim Chelsea legends refused to board plane
Sports.content:
Andre Villas-Boas has hit back at John Terry's claims of a plane dispute that occurred during his time as Chelsea manager.

In 2024, legendary former Blues captain Terry said Villas-Boas had controversially tried to place youth players in first-class and the established players in economy ahead of a pre-season tour.



4 Terry was managed by Villas-Boas at Stamford Bridge during the 2011/12 season Credit: Getty

Villas-Boas endured a difficult eight-month stint at Stamford Bridge after taking charge in the summer of 2011.

His tenure saw his side struggle in a battle to reach the top four in the Premier League, before they went on to win the Champions League and FA Cup in the months that followed his sacking.

In the years since, Villas-Boas has faced claims he struggled with player power whilst at Chelsea, whose team featured a number of strong personalities including club icons Terry, Frank Lampard, Didier Drogba, Ashley Cole and Petr Cech.



Terry's boycott claim

The most telling 'AVB' story has been Terry's, where he claimed senior players turned against him following a controversial decision.

In 2024, he told talkSPORT host Simon Jordan on his Up Front podcast: "When AVB came in, we went to Hong Kong [for pre-season] I think when he was first manager, we got on the plane and I'm sitting on economy on a 13-hour flight.



"And we've got Josh McEachran, Nathaniel Chalobah, a couple of other young players, all in first class.

"And this was part of AVB going, 'No player is bigger than me, everyone's the same.'



"It turns out Lamps [Frank Lampard] is flying out first class and I'm flying back first class, so if you fly out at home in first, you come back in economy.

"But basically it wasn't good enough, so I'm going, 'No no, we're not going anywhere until these young players go back in economy, and the first team players that have built this club to where we are today go back in first'."

Terry insisted he and the other senior stars would not have allowed the plane to take off under these circumstances and said Villas-Boas 'failed instantly' to make a positive first impression.

4 Terry recalled an incident where Villas-Boas lost the Chelsea dressing room on day one Credit: Getty



He added: "This is one of his first things in front of everyone. In the end it spins, so all first team players fly first, younger players go back in economy, that's how it should be.

"These younger players are striving to be where we've got, and he tried to make a statement on day one and he failed instantly.

"Because I promise you, the plane wasn't going, and if it was going, it would have gone without myself, Frank and Didier [Drogba]."

Villas-Boas sets record straight

Now, Villas-Boas has shared his version of events, insisting there was reason for his decision and claiming Terry's story isn't totally true.



Speaking on former Blues star John Obi Mikel's Obi One Podcast, he said: "First of all, we are speaking first class or business class, not economy.

"I have seen the story, it is good you point it out to me, this is me as a principle human being, setting out the rules.

4 Villas-Boas lasted less than a year at Chelsea before being sacked Credit: Getty Images - Getty

"We only had a few free in first class, we couldn't fit all the first team players, you would have to make a selection between say Cech, Drogba, Terry, Lampard, then leave out the rest of the boys.



"The principle was that - instead of creating a problem, let's put the academy boys here and send the rest of them to business class."

Villas-Boas also denied that Terry had complained to him about the seating arrangements at the time.

He continued: "I don't remember John coming to me saying it might have been an issue, I don't remember them changing.

"That was the principle, instead of putting the top guns... we had enough for the captains which was a good excuse, we tested all of the different criteria, appearances, years for the club, the principle was the big guns got together.



"I see it completely different, John sees it the other way round.

4 Chelsea became the first London club to win the Champions League trophy back in 2012 after Villas-Boas' sacking

"I think it had zero influence on pre-season because we were excellent and started the season well.

"It probably has something to do with my principal way of doing, my stubbornness at some stage, or not overseeing the big picture, the big prima donnas. I am not sure if I would do it differently now."

Sports.title: Ally Pally cult hero who made history last year qualifies for 2027 World Championship
Sports.content:
Ally Pally cult hero who made history last year qualifies for 2027 World Championship

David Munyua will grace the Ally Pally once again after booking his 2027 World Championship spot over the weekend.

Munyua claimed a dramatic 8-7 win over Evans Njuguna in the African Dart Group Northern Africa Qualifier on Sunday.

3 Munyua will be back at the Ally Pally for the second year running Credit: Getty

The 30-year-old made history last year as he became the first Kenyan to appear, and win, on the Alexandra Palace stage.

Munyua surprised Belgian Mike De Decker, despite trailing 2-0 early in the match.

Munyua, a veterinarian in Nairobi, pulled the game back to win 3-2 in what has been described as one of the greatest shocks in World Darts Championship history.

'It's amazing'

The Murang'a-born darts star, nicknamed 'Why Not?', will hope for a repeat in London this year.

He was, after all, over the moon with his win over De Decker in December 2025.

"This is great for me," he told talkSPORT.

"I'm very happy and very excited about it. I didn't expect it. It's amazing."

Munyua spoke of the importance of his victory and what it means for the sport in Africa.

"This is massive," Munyua continued. "We have great players back there, good players.

3 Munyua's win over De Decker was one of the biggest upsets in tournament history Credit: Getty

"Now I'm sure they're encouraged that we can do this."

However, Munyua's World Championship dream ended in the second round as he fell to a 3-0 defeat to Kevin Doets.

When does the 2027 World Championship get underway?

The 34th World Championship will start on December 11 2026.

The tournament itself will run until January 3 2027 and has a £5million prize fund, with the winner pocketing £1million.

3 Littler is looking to win the World Championship for the third successive year

Luke Littler, who has threatened to boycott tournaments in the Netherlands, won the World Championship last year, beating Dutchman Gian van Veen 7-1 in the final.

And 'The Nuke' is hoping to go the distance for the third year running.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi compared to Ruben Amorim as Tottenham players told how to fix mentality issue
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi compared to Ruben Amorim as Tottenham players told how to fix mentality issue

Tottenham players have been warned it is up to them to fix their mentality problem amid their ongoing woes.

Roberto De Zerbi's side sit bottom of the Premier League after five matches this season.

3 De Zerbi's woes have continued with Spurs bottom of the Premier League and winless Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Their defeat to Aston Villa on Saturday extended the club's winless start to the new season.

Spurs have taken just two points from five matches, having not scored in the league prior to their 3-2 loss to Villa.

They remain one of just three sides yet to taste victory this term alongside Bournemouth and Fulham.

De Zerbi on Spurs' mentality

Following their latest defeat, De Zerbi claimed his players have the right mentality but are 'fragile' and 'inconsistent'.

The Spurs boss explained: "It’s not mentality. It’s a mental aspect for sure, but they have the right mentality. They work very well. They are good players.

"It’s difficult to explain because in my career, in 14 years as a coach, I’ve never seen one team like us. So fragile, so inconsistent. You are good or you are bad.

"You can’t be very good in the first 40 minutes, 30 minutes and then to concede like this, in this way."

His comments have since been echoed by summer signing Jan Paul van Hecke.

The defender told Dutch outlet AD: "We had imagined it would be different.

"The way we play and concede goals is unacceptable. The way the energy drained away from the team is simply not right."

3 Van Hecke has echoed De Zerbi's comments on the mentality of the Spurs squad Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Deeney addresses Spurs issues

Troy Deeney has now compared De Zerbi's latest remarks to those of former Manchester United manager Ruben Amorim.

The talkSPORT co-host addressed his comments on Monday's White & Jordan in the wake of Spurs' latest setback.

Deeney admitted: "It’s a little bit Amorim-esque, in terms of telling you the truth and telling you what’s going on."

As for how the players can address their issues, he continued: "I think that Spurs need to come together.

"It feels to me like De Zerbi is saying a lot of ‘not me, them’. That’s how I’m taking it and receiving it, if I put my player’s hat on.

"But also from a player’s point of view, if you keep losing I would expect every now and again you have a players-only meeting.

3 Deeney has now compared De Zerbi to former United boss Amorim Credit: Getty

"One where you just say to the manager, ‘stay out of the room, we just need to have a chat’. Especially if it’s been three weeks. Right, let’s air it out, let’s call everyone.

"We’ve got to call them because we’re going to have a few days away from each other and when we get back, we’ve got to get back to business because this is all about the mentality now."

Even with a team meeting during the international break, Deeney doubts Spurs can pull away from trouble with their current home record.

The north London outfit have won just one of their last 14 Premier League matches at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, a run which dates back to December.

Deeney added: "I think they’re going to struggle because when they miss one opportunity, they implode. Where they haven’t made the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium home, they implode.

"So they’re looking for away days. They’re looking to be away from their own troubles because they’re the underdog. It’s easier there."

Spurs, who have finished 17th in each of the last two seasons, return to action away at Manchester United on Saturday, October 10.

Meanwhile, their next home fixture is against Coventry City on Monday, October 19.

Sports.title: EFL club opt not to postpone game despite three international call-ups
Sports.content:
EFL club opt not to postpone game despite three international call-ups

Reading's League One clash against Wycombe Wanderers will go ahead as originally scheduled.

The Royals had the opportunity to postpone the fixture after Andy Rinomhota, Jeriel Dorsett and Charlie Savage received call-ups from Zimbabwe, Montseratt and Wales respectively.

2 Reading won't have to re-shuffle their fixtures around Credit: Getty

What are the EFL's rules regarding international call-ups?

EFL rules stipulate clubs are eligible to request a postponement if three or more of their players are selected for international duty.

Those players must have been named in the team's starting line-up or been a named substitute who came on before the 7th minute in either 50 per cent of a club's first-team games or four of their last five first-team games.

But the Royals have elected to press on with their trip to Wycombe on Saturday as well as their home match against Bradford City on October 3, with both fixtures scheduled for 3pm.

Reading boss Leam Richardson explains decision not to postpone games

“First of all, congratulations to the three lads who received international call-ups," Reading boss Leam Richardson said.

"It’s a fantastic achievement for them and a proud moment for the club.

“We considered the circumstances carefully and, on this occasion, felt it was right to play the game.

"Football is a squad game and we have confidence in the players available to us, while keeping the fixture in place also helps us avoid adding another game to an already busy schedule.

“It’s better for the supporters too. Saturday afternoon is the ideal time to play football whenever circumstances allow, so we were pleased to keep this one in place.”

Of the Reading trio called up, Rinomhota's absence could be the most keenly felt.

The 29-year-old, who plays as a defensive midfielder, has started all six of the Royals' league fixtures.

2 Richardson has been in charge of Reading since October 2025 Credit: Getty

Dorsett has started four times for Reading across all competitions while Savage, the son of ex-Premier League star Robbie Savage, has come off the bench in all of the club's league games.

How have Reading performed this season?

Richardson's side sit eighth in League One after six games, boasting a record of three wins, one draw and two defeats.

Reading's haul of 10 points is five behind league leaders Bradford.

The Royals' latest result was a 2-0 win over Notts County, with Jack Marriott netting both goals.

Marriott's brace took his tally of league goals to eight, three more than any other League One player.

The win also marked Reading's third-straight victory at home in the league.

Sports.title: Harry Wilson out of Wales squad along with Wrexham star as three EFL players called up
Sports.content:
Harry Wilson out of Wales squad along with Wrexham star as three EFL players called up

Harry Wilson has been forced to withdraw from the Wales squad for their opening four Nations League fixtures.

The Leeds United forward is one of three players to pull out of the side.

3 Wilson has withdrawn from the Wales squad to face Portugal, Denmark and Norway Credit: Getty

Craig Bellamy had named a 28-man squad on Tuesday for the matches against Portugal, Denmark and Norway.

However, he has now been forced into a trio of changes ahead of facing Portugal on Thursday.

Wales trio withdraw

Wilson has withdrawn from the squad due to a quad injury, which forced him to miss Leeds' draw with Crystal Palace at the weekend.

Daniel Farke confirmed on Friday that the 29-year-old would likely be out until after the international break.

A return against Arsenal on October 10 is currently being earmarked for Wilson.

He is joined in pulling out of the side by striker Nathan Broadhead and goalkeeper Karl Darlow.

Broadhead had been a doubt as a result of a thigh issue, with the Wrexham man not featuring for his club since August 28.

Meanwhile, Darlow was on the bench for Manchester United away against Fulham on Sunday.

The stopper made his first appearance of the season in the defeat to Brighton in the Carabao Cup last week.

Bellamy has called up League One trio Joe Taylor, Charlie Savage and David Cornell to replace the withdrawals.

3 Darlow has also pulled out of the side despite being on the bench for United on Sunday Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Huddersfield striker Taylor and Leicester City goalkeeper Cornell are both uncapped.

Savage has won two caps to date, with both coming against Gibraltar.

However, the Reading midfielder, who is the son of former Wales international Robbie Savage, had previously not been called up since June 2024.

They join the rest of the Wales squad in preparing to begin their Nations League campaign.

When do Wales play next?

The players arrived at their training camp on Sunday ahead of facing Portugal in Lisbon on Thursday.

A trip to Denmark will follow on September 27 before a home match against Norway on October 1.

Sports.title: Man United told how to fix Marcus Rashford problem after difficult start to season
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford's role is Manchester United's primary problem and the club have been warned about catering to his ego.

Rashford spent 20 months away from Old Trafford during consecutive loan spells at Aston Villa and Barcelona.



3 Rashford hasn't scored in any of his six games this season Credit: Getty

However, the versatile forward has started in three of the Red Devils' four Premier League games following his return, and came off the bench in their first outing.

The reintegration of the England international, though, has disrupted United's starting forward line from the previous campaign.

To accommodate the England international on the left wing, Matheus Cunha has been forced out of position to play as a central striker.



Across six appearances in all competitions, the forward has been unable to register any goals or assists for his boyhood club and has frustrated fans.

On talkSPORT's Premier League All Access podcast following United's 1-1 draw, former Watford captain Troy Deeney said: "There is an elephant in the room, and I don’t want it to seem like another Rashford attack, but they just look better when he comes off. Why keep persisting with it?"



talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook replied: "Because he’s on £350,000 a week.”

Host Sam Matterface, added: " It’s a major issue that they weren’t planning for him to come back. They thought they had a deal with Barcelona in that he would stay at the Camp Nou, even if they had to pay half of his wages, it meant he was out of the team.



"Instead, bringing him back into the group has actually disrupted that front three.

Deeney responded: "With Marcus coming back into the fold, he should be having to do other things. He should be the one playing up front and through the middle, not Cunha.

"We know that the previous setup works so it should be Rashford who has to fix it, but instead they’re pandering to him and his ego, and instead he needs to be the one who is sacrificed."

3 Mbeumo and Cunha scored nearly as many goals as Man United managed as a team in the Premier League last season Credit: Getty



Last season's winning formula

During the 2025/26 campaign, United's primary attacking trident of Benjamin Sesko, Bryan Mbeumo, and Cunha combined for an impressive goal tally across all competitions.

All three players hit double digits in the league alone as both Mbeumo and the Slovenia international finished the season as the club's joint-top goalscorers with 12 goals each in all competitions.

When Sesko is fully recovered from his injury, fans are urging Carrick to start the Slovenia international in the number 9 position and choose Cunha to play deeper.

'A wasted talent'

Barcelona decided not to activate their £26million option to buy Rashford permanently this summer which left him returning to Carrington.



While Carrick inherited a player boasting 87 Premier League goals in 287 appearances, the winger's application continues to divide opinion.

Deeney added: "I get frustrated with him because if you just took the talent package, he’s one of the best talents in the country.

3 Rashford has been at United since 2005 and has grown as a player there at every stage Credit: Getty

"But application, consistency, and the willingness to be the best version of yourself is when I get frustrated.



Matterface agreed: "I want Marcus to really work out because I think there’s talent there, and England should want a player like that.

"But whatever reason, that dynamic has not worked at the beginning of the season and solving that problem is one of the biggest issues for Carrick."

Rashford has often looked to be United's most creative player at times but has struggled to be clinical upon his return.

Simon Jordan added on the White & Jordan show: "I've got no issue with Marcus. I think he's a wasted talent and I think he's shown himself. I think he showed himself with his pathetic podcast that he did a couple of years ago about ‘woe is me’.



"And he's shown himself not being valuable to Barcelona. So why do Man United need him back... I don't know.

"I think they should have made a decision and either bought him out of his contract or let him go on a discounted deal and helped his wages along the way just to clear the decks."

Sports.title: Wrexham buy pub made famous Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac documentary and make statement on its long-term future
Sports.content:
Wrexham buy pub made famous Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac documentary and make statement on its long-term future

Wrexham have confirmed they have acquired the purchase of The Turf from Admiral Taverns.

The pub, which used to overlook the stands of the Racehorse Ground, has since been added to the club's portfolio by the club's owners, which include Hollywood stars Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney.

3 The Turf has become famous in the years since Reynolds and McElhenney acquired Wrexham Credit: Getty Images - Getty

"The ownership group of Wrexham AFC has today exchanged on the purchase of The Turf from Admiral Taverns, the UK’s leading community pub company," a statement read on the club's official website.

"The acquisition allows for the preservation of the history and traditions of the historic public house that is inexorably linked to the Racecourse Ground and Wrexham AFC Football Club since its foundation in 1864.

"The acquisition of The Turf will help protect the historic pub by incorporating the Club, the Racecourse Ground and The Turf under a single ownership, whilst allowing for further investment into the fan experience in and around matchdays.

"This will include opportunities to enhance the current fan zone and other fan-related activities in the area next to The Turf on the Mold Road."

Welcome to Wrexham's impact

The pub itself was made famous having featured frequently on the documentary 'Welcome to Wrexham'.

The docuseries, now in its fifth season, documents the events of the Welsh club as they look to rise the football pyramid and secure a Premier League spot.

The Turf is viewed as an important part of the development plans as Wrexham and has welcomed a number of famous faces in recent years, including Will Ferrell and Hugh Jackman.

And Wayne Jones, the popular landlord made famous in Welcome to Wrexham, will remain in charge of the pub.

"Ever since we invested in Wrexham AFC through Red Dragon Ventures in 2024, the town, the community and the Football Club have become a second home," Eric Allyn, on behalf of minority investors the Allyn family, said.

3 Rob Mac and Ryan Reynolds' documentary brought The Turf into the spotlight Credit: Photo by Jordan Strauss/Invision/AP

"And no place more so than The Turf with Wayne Jones behind the bar and filled with the locals and international fans that visit regularly - they have all become our friends and have welcomed us into the Wrexham family.

"By bringing The Turf into the group, we are securing the long-term future of the pub and with it preserving its history and that of the Club."

'Get their act in order'

The purchase comes after Wrexham were told to "get their act in order" by a local community council.

The Championship side completed the build of a facility without first acquiring proper planning permission, which the club apologised for.

The original application was filed in August, but came after work head already started.

3 Wrexham have come in for criticism from the local council recently Credit: Getty

"I do wish that people [Wrexham] would get their act in order and not put in retrospective applications just because it suits you - which, at the end of the day, [is] what it came down to," Councillor Mike Morris, Gresford community council's planning committee chair, said.

"You wanted to do it in the summer, and you know the fact you've had good results, and you know the football club is doing very well, we all applaud that, but it's no excuse for not following the procedure properly.

"It's no different to any other retrospective application. So it will be a matter for members to consider whether they are going to support it or not, and that will come out in the debate."

Sports.title: Piers Morgan has on air meltdown at Jamie O’Hara and Gabby Agbonlahor for Arsenal jibes
Sports.content:
Piers Morgan has on air meltdown at Jamie O’Hara and Gabby Agbonlahor for Arsenal jibes

Piers Morgan was in no mood to hear Jamie O'Hara and Gabby Agbonlahor poke fun at Arsenal's loss to Brighton.

The Gunners' perfect start to the Premier League campaign came to an end on Saturday as they slipped to a 3-0 loss against the Seagulls.

3 The Gunners took their first stumble of the 2026/27 season Credit: Getty

Mikel Arteta's side never got going and the frustration eventually boiled over right at the end when Declan Rice kicked out at Brighton's Malick Yalcouye.

O'Hara and Agbonlahor took great delight in Arsenal's defeat throughout Monday's edition of talkSPORT Breakfast, prompting passionate Gunners fan Morgan to call up and rip in.

Piers Morgan's reaction to Jamie O'Hara and Gabby Agbonlahor's Arsenal sledging

Morgan was especially keen to poke fun at O'Hara's beloved Spurs, who sit last in the top flight despite a gargantuan summer transfer spend.

"I'm just a little bit bemused this morning," Morgan said.

"I've been listening to you guys mocking my team.

"We had a bad day at the office and we got well-beaten by my second team, Brighton.

"However, the idea that you two clowns are taking the high moral ground about my football club, when I've just looked at the Premier League table.

"Tottenham, who came 17th the last two seasons, you've spent £300million and guess what, you've actually managed to achieve the impossible, you've got worse. You are currently bottom of the Premier League.

"I then moved up a few places to 16th and found Aston Villa, who are having an equally dismal season.

"So the idea that you two are playing mocking clips about my team, who are second in the Premier League, current Premier League champions, is an absolute joke."

3 O'Hara's Spurs are one of three teams yet to win a league game this term Credit: Getty

Piers Morgan offers Jamie O'Hara £1m charity bet

Morgan then decided he'd test O'Hara's love of Spurs by challenging him to a £1m wager that Arsenal would finish above their north London rivals not just this season, but the next five seasons.

After O'Hara turned down the seven-figure bet, Morgan decided he'd stoop to the ex-Spurs midfielder's 'financial level' and stake £1 to a charity of O'Hara's choosing that Arsenal would win the league again.

Agbonlahor then decided he'd take Morgan on, betting £200 that Manchester City would pip Arsenal to the Premier League title.

Unsurprisingly, an agreement was struck between the two.

What bet did Jamie O'Hara agree to with Piers Morgan?

As for O'Hara, Morgan decided to up the stakes but without any financial implications.

"If Arsenal win the league, I demand to come in and host your show," Morgan said.

3 Could Morgan be a surprise guest host on the Sports Bar in May? Credit: Alamy

"And you have to sit there and take all the pelters from me for three hours."

O'Hara, who also believes City will beat Arsenal to the league title, happily agreed to Morgan's offer.

If the Gunners do manage to go back-to-back, a special edition of the Sports Bar with Morgan, O'Hara and Jason Cundy will certainly make for box office viewing.

Sports.title: Declan Rice leads FIVE stars in pulling out of England duty - with just two new players called up - as Thomas Tuchel faces exodus after his stern warning
Sports.content:
Declan Rice is the new big name among a five-man England exodus - days after Thomas Tuchel warned his players of a need to 'step up' to prove their worth after the World Cup. Rice, Cole Palmer, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento have all now pulled out of Tuchel's squad - with Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner of Everton the only replacements. Arsenal midfielder Rice played the full 90 minutes of their defeat by Brighton on Saturday but has been declared unavailable for England. The Gunners are yet to offer any other details on his injury. Chelsea sources say Palmer has a muscular injury, while Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said Rashford had an 'issue' after their weekend draw with Fulham. Mainoo was also assessed over an injury today. Livramento was forced to pull out of the World Cup squad with a calf injury, did not play for Newcastle United at the weekend and is yet to start a game this season. England are due to face 2026 World Cup winners Spain first, before two games against Czechia and another versus Croatia. Tuchel is scheduled to speak this Friday, when he will be able to offer his opinion on losing five players. Declan Rice has been removed from the England squad for their upcoming internationals Cole Palmer has pulled out of the England squad with a small injury and to manage his work load after an injury-hit season last campaign Tuchel previously warned Palmer, who was left at home for the World Cup, that he had a 'point to prove' and needed 'to step up' to 'keep his shirt and justify the nomination'. He added: 'So now it is a new competition. Some players, some positions, have more injuries. Some have less injuries. Cole has his starts that he always had but he has his numbers back - he has his assists back, he has decisive goals back - so that is why he is in the squad.' Gibbs-White, 26, had been on holiday with his family in Dubai after playing in the defeat by Coventry on Saturday but is immediately returning to answer England's call. Everton midfielder Garner is selected ahead of Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton. Tuchel cited having too many attacking midfielders to include them all as the reason for Gibbs-White's initial omission. 'It makes no sense to nominate three, four, five No 10s,' Tuchel said. 'It just does not help anyone. Manchester United duo Kobbie Mainoo (left) and Marcus Rashford (right) have also withdrawn Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White has been called up in place of the midfielder - leaving his family holiday in Dubai to answer his country's call 'We can see the form he is in. He ended the season very strongly and is a key player for Forest. We can see him stepping up now.' Rashford has been battling a hip issue since the World Cup. He started Manchester United's 1-1 draw with Fulham on Sunday but the injury needs management. Mainoo is also struggling with an issue. The 21-year-old was in the squad at the World Cup, but did not play a single minute.
