Sports.title: How to watch the 2026 Azerbaijan GP and why it is being held on a Saturday | TV Times
Sports.content:
There are two significant changes to the usual race weekend format for this weekend’s Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

This is the latest date the race at the Baku City Circuit has ever been held. Formula One Management confirmed it moved the date forward from the usual Sunday slot to Saturday following a request from the government and race promoters “to accommodate a national day”

Azerbaijan’s dictatorial president Ilham Aliyev designated September 27th as a ‘Remembrance Day’ in 2020 to mark the beginning of that year’s war in the Nagorno-Karabakh region. Azerbaijan expelled all ethnic Armenians from the territory in 2023. Aliyev’s ethnic cleansing drove around 100,000 people from their homes.

FOM has agreed all its track sessions will take place a day earlier than usual this weekend. That includes the trio of Formula 2 support races.

The series has added an extra feature race due to the cancellation of its rounds in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia earlier this year due to the Iran war. As it will not accompany F1 to Sepang next week for the ‘Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia’, the F2 drivers have a two-month break until their next event in Qatar, though it remains unclear whether that round or the finale in Abu Dhabi will take place.

Sports.title: Wolff tried to help Masi ‘for the good of the sport, and for us’ in 2021 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has revealed details of his conversations with former race director Michael Masi before his controversial call in the 2021 championship-decider.

Masi lost his job over his mishandling of the 2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. He arranged a final-lap restart in contravention of the rules which led Wolff’s driver Lewis Hamilton to lose the championship to Max Verstappen.

Hamilton and Verstappen were involved in a series of controversial collisions over the course of 2021. Wolff, who previously called Masi “disrespectful” and a “liability”, said he had concerns over how the race director reacted to feedback from the drivers.

“I really tried to speak to Michael and guide him all along the year,” Wolff told High Performance. “I said ‘listen I’ve been in the sport for a long time, listen to the drivers, don’t always be stubborn in your decision making, don’t be arrogant’.”

Wolff admitted his motivation in speaking to the race director was partly to advance Mercedes’ interest.

“I tried that for the good of the sport, and obviously also for us as a team not to be vulnerable to situations that could be totally detrimental,” he said.

Masi contradicted the regulations and his past interpretation of them by arranging a final-lap restart at Yas Marina by removing the lapped cars between Hamilton and Verstappen, but not any of the others. The FIA later ruled this had been an error. Verstappen passed Hamilton immediately after the restart, clinching his first world championship and denying Hamilton a record-breaking eighth.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Wolff said Masi’s actions were “inexcusable.”

“You could say the empathy should make me realise how he feels,” he said. “I realise how it feels.

“And I know that’s not good, and bad, but he could have thought about it all year long, when people, not only me, tried to support him in the right way.

“So sometimes you have to just realise that someone is just doing his own thing or taking his own decisions. So for me, I don’t care about it anymore.”

However he admitted he still reflects on the lost championship “every week”.

“I mainly think about it because I think Lewis deserved to be the greatest of all time with eight world championship titles,” he said. “And you can argue all along about that year.

“I think Max and Lewis were deserving champions. There were instances during the year where Max lost some points that he shouldn’t have lost. You look at the crash in Monza both of them had. So both deserving champions, but on that particular afternoon in Abu Dhabi, it was unfair.”

Following his departure from F1, Masi joined SRO Motorsports Australia last week as head of sporting operations.

Sports.title: Poll: Should F1 change its rules to make Virtual Safety Car periods fairer? | Debates and Polls
Sports.content:
The outcome of last weekend’s Spanish Grand Prix was effectively decided by Lance Stroll’s retirement on lap 15.

The Virtual Safety Car was deployed while the Aston Martin driver parked up in a run-off area. It only lasted

seconds, but as far as Lando Norris was concerned its timing could not have been worse.

Norris was leading when the VSC period began seconds after he passed the pit lane entrance. Andrea Kimi Antonelli, second, was able to pit during the VSC period, gaining a useful advantage by pitting while the race was neutralised.

Every other driver on the track had the same opportunity to pit, with one exception: Norris. The VSC period ended moments before he reached the pit lane entrance.

Afterwards Norris expressed frustration that the race’s only VSC period was timed in such a way that it gave everyone apart from him a chance to make a low-cost pit stop. While it’s certainly the case he was unlucky, should F1 try to prevent a similar situation happening again?

The Virtual Safety Car problem

In F1, like other series such as IndyCar, Safety Car periods can often have a disruptive effect on drivers’ strategies. They may occur at a more advantageous time for some drivers than others (as was the case when Norris scored his first win in Miami two years ago).

However the Virtual Safety Car, which F1 introduced in 2015, created a new kind of problem. During a classic Safety Car period, every driver has the opportunity to make a pit stop. But as a VSC period can be much shorter, it is possible that only some drivers may have the chance to pit.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

This is more likely to happen in certain circumstances. For example, when the track is very long, or if conditions are wet creating longer lap times, or when the field is tightly compressed after a start or restart.

There have only been a few cases of drivers being unable to pit during a VSC period since the rules were introduced. One notable example occured in the 2024 Brazilian Grand Prix, where all but four drivers were able to pit during a VSC period.

Possible solutions

No change

The striking thing about Norris’s misfortune on Sunday was how unusual it is. As these situations are so rare, it is not worth creating special rules to deal with them, which would create further complexity and scope for unintended consequences.

Introduce a minimum duration for VSC periods

It is unusual for VSC periods to last less than a lap in duration. When they do, it is usually only by a few seconds. Introducing a minimum length for VSC periods would ensure no driver suffers the same misfortune as Norris but make little difference to the majority of VSC deployments.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Forbid tyre changes during VSC periods

Other series which have similar mandatory tyre change rules to F1 do not allow drivers to fulfil the requirement to change tyres during a VSC period. This is the case in Formula 2, and F1 could simply adopt the same rule. Closing the pit lane entrance during a VSC period would have the same effect, though this would prevent drivers pitting for damage repairs or other reasons.

Introduce a lower pit lane speed limit during VSC periods

Drivers are able to gain an advantage by pitting during a VSC period because the speed of the cars on track is reduced while the pit lane speed limit stays the same. Reducing the pit lane speed limit could address this, though it would have to be very low, especially at tracks where the lower 60kph speed limit is used by default, and imposing it on cars in the pit lane when the VSC is deployed could be complicated.

Abolish the Virtual Safety Car

Revert to using the classic Safety Car for all interruptions to the race. This would likely result in longer disruptions to races and compress the field more frequently.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

I say

I find the VSC preferable to the regular Safety Car because it does a better job of preserving the competition as it stands, and not significantly altering the gaps between cars. It is unfortunate that in some, limited circumstances, it does create the possibility for some drivers to suffer a significant disadvantage. Introducing a minimum duration for VSC periods would seem the easiest and fairest way to tackle the problem, which is unlikely to add significant extra delays or cause knock-on problems.

Sports.title: Antonelli ‘doing a scarily good job’, ‘beating much more experienced team mate’ – Norris | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Reigning world champion Lando Norris is highly impressed by the performance of the driver who looks set to succeed him.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli scored his eighth grand prix victory last weekend and has pulled 81 points clear of his closest rival – team mate George Russell – at the top of the championship standings.

“He’s leading by 80 points because he’s doing an incredible job,” said Norris. “He’s beating a much more experienced team-mate.”

Antonelli was still a teenager when he scored his first grand prix victory earlier this year. “He’s doing a scarily good job [having] just turned 20,” Norris continued. “Pretty phenomenal.”

Norris closed within 83 points of Antonelli by winning the two rounds either side of the summer break. But his slim hope of retaining his title faded after Antonelli won the last two rounds, leaving the McLaren driver 106 behind.

If Antonelli clinches the championship this year he will break Sebastian Vettel’s record for being the youngest ever world champion. Vettel was 23 when he won the world championship in 2010. “I think it’s cool to see someone so young doing such an incredible job and more than likely go on and win the championship,” said Norris.

“He’s been impressive since the first race this year. [He’s made] very few mistakes. He’s not driving like it’s his second year in F1, that’s for sure.

“It’s cool to see and there’s going to be many, many more years of us battling and I’m excited for more, hopefully this year.”

Sports.title: F1 drivers explain why Madring’s hyped Monumental corner failed to impress | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The Spanish Grand Prix promoters set high expectations of the new Madring ahead of its first Formula 1 race last weekend.

“The adrenaline is at 100% every lap” raved one Formula 3 driver in pre-event material issued by the promoters. They promised turn 12, dubbed Monumental, was “set to become one of Madring’s greatest challenges.”

The reality proved somewhat different. The Madring as a whole produced little action of note and Monumental was no exception, aside from Franco Colapinto’s impressive save during qualifying.

Formula 1 drivers were largely unchallenged by the 24-degree banked corner as they couldn’t tackle it at maximum speed. This was for the same reason so many of F1’s great corners have been neutered this year: their power units weren’t up to it.

“I wanted to go flat [out], but then my battery dies,” explained Max Verstappen, “so you add a lift to have better deployment. So that’s my Monumental experience.”

The original design for the Monumental corner featured a straighter, faster approach. But even with the addition of two more turns before it, drivers had to use the Madring’s much-hyped challenge as an energy-saving opportunity.

This was despite the Madring promoters claiming “the circuit is adapted to the new [F1] regulations” which were introduced for 2026.

Although the corner proved unchallenging for F1 drivers, Verstappen suspects it was more demanding for those in junior categories.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“It’s cool, the banking, but I think they should have done it the other way around,” he said. “Initially more banking and then just flatten it out.

“In an F1 car you have so much downforce. I think it’s more challenging in the other categories because it didn’t look so easy flat in other categories.

“For us, plus because our battery dies towards the end, you already slow down a bit. But I guess for the shots it looks great from the outside.”

Lando Norris agreed “it’s not the biggest challenge because you have to just save the battery through the first part of the corner.”

“It would be better if we just had no battery and more power, so in a few years maybe it’ll be more fun. But it’s still a cool feeling, it’s a different feeling.”

Norris suggested increasing the camber on more corners would improve the racing at the Madring. “Cambered corners normally allow you to follow better,” he said. “So, I think next year more corners should be a bit more cambered.”

“It’s a fun corner,” he added, “it could just be better.”

Sports.title: Hearn Risks Matchroom’s Future for Aging Joshua
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn may have secured Anthony Joshua’s preferred country for the Tyson Fury fight, but Roy Jones Jr. believes the Matchroom promoter has damaged his position with the people controlling boxing’s richest events.

Joshua and Fury had agreed to fight November 20 at Madison Square Garden. Hearn resisted the New York venue because Joshua’s contract required the contest to take place in Britain. The heavyweight clash is now likely to land at Principality Stadium in Cardiff on December 11.

That gives Hearn a victory he can sell to the British public, but the reported 2 a.m. local start removes much of its meaning. Seventy thousand paying spectators may be asked to remain inside the stadium until early morning so Netflix can show the fight during American prime time.

If Jones is correct that American viewers have little interest in Fury–Joshua, the compromise becomes harder to defend. Britain provides the crowd, ticket money and atmosphere while the broadcast schedule caters to an audience that Jones says does not care.

Jones applauded Hearn for resisting the combined pressure from Turki Alalshikh, Sela, Netflix, Dana White, TKO and Team Fury. He also offered a much darker forecast for Matchroom.

“Hearn has won a battle, but he’s gonna lose the war. I just think it’s because Turki has enough money to do whatever he wants to do. Whoever has his ear is gonna win the war, because he’s got the money to keep it going. But my hat goes off to Eddie for fighting, because Eddie knows that war is not the best thing for boxing,” Jones told Parimatch Slots Site, via BoxingScene.

The concern reaches beyond a disagreement over one venue. Alalshikh has the financial resources to outlast any traditional promoter. If he decides TKO and Frank Warren are easier partners, Matchroom can be removed from major cards without leaving the Saudi operation short of alternatives.

Warren has remained aligned with the Riyadh group while showing flexibility over the Fury–Joshua date and location. That may leave Queensberry better placed for future Saudi events as Hearn returns to a far more limited DAZN schedule.

Dana White and TKO present another danger. White wants a more centralized boxing structure with tighter control over fighters and purses. Hearn has built his reputation by securing the largest possible payments for his boxers. The two approaches were always likely to collide, and this dispute may have given TKO another reason to work around Matchroom.

Hearn has made that stand for a 36-year-old Joshua whose career is nearing its conclusion. Joshua helped build Matchroom Boxing into an international company, so the promoter’s loyalty is understandable. However, Jaron Ennis, Diego Pacheco, Conor Benn and Matchroom’s younger fighters will need access to major financial opportunities long after Joshua retires.

It is too early to state that Hearn’s relationship with Alalshikh is finished. Neither side has announced a permanent split. Jones nevertheless sees the imbalance clearly. Hearn enforced Joshua’s contract and preserved the British venue, but he challenged a group with enough money, fighters, and promotional partners to continue without him.

Joshua may receive the home fight he demanded. Matchroom’s younger stable may inherit its cost.

Sports.title: Can David Morrell Recover at Light Heavyweight?
Sports.content:
David Morrell has disappeared from the boxing conversation since Zak Chelli stopped him in the 10th round on May 9. Once presented as a future star at super middleweight, the Cuban now sits at 12-2 with no confirmed return date and serious questions about his future at 175 pounds.

Chelli accepted the fight on two weeks’ notice and was trailing before hurting Morrell in the ninth and finishing him with 36 seconds left in the final round. It was not merely a shocking defeat. It exposed a technical weakness that had followed Morrell throughout his professional career.

When pressured, Morrell retreats in straight lines until his heels reach the edge of the ring. He then squares his upper body, raises both gloves, and waits for the attack to end.

The guard protects parts of his head, but widening his torso gives opponents access to his liver and ribs. He also provides no angle for an escape. Instead of stepping around an orthodox fighter’s lead foot, Morrell remains directly in front of him.

David Benavidez exploited that behavior over 12 rounds in February 2025. Morrell dropped Benavidez in the 11th, but those isolated successes could not erase the long stretches he spent absorbing combinations along the ropes.

Chelli found the same opening. Once Morrell’s legs faded, the guard became a hiding place rather than an active defense.

Morrell remains dangerous when he has room to select his shots. His straight left hand, counter right hook, and short two-punch bursts are fast enough to punish careless entries. The trouble begins when an opponent survives the first attack. Morrell rarely follows with the sustained combinations needed to hold the center of the ring. His style still carries the rhythm of amateur boxing: land the cleaner single shot, reset and wait for another opening. Professional pressure fighters do not always grant that reset.

An opponent willing to walk through one or two hard punches can force Morrell backward and beat him through activity. Morrell does not have a developed inside game that allows him to fight for position once the distance has disappeared.

Elite fighters who become trapped along the ropes usually clinch, pin an arm or turn the attacker before leaving. Morrell does little of that.

He stands behind his forearms and allows opponents to complete their combinations. Even when most of the punches strike his gloves, judges see one fighter attacking and the other merely surviving.

That passivity is more exhausting at light heavyweight. Morrell was physically stronger than most of his opposition at 168 pounds. At 175, naturally larger fighters can drive their weight into him and force his legs to support both bodies.

Holding a turtle guard under that pressure drains the shoulders, back, and thighs. It helps explain why Morrell’s energy vanished so rapidly against Chelli in the ninth and 10th rounds. Morrell reportedly relocated to Orlando and changed his training setup after the Chelli defeat. A new camp will only help if it changes his reactions when another fighter presses him.

He needs lateral escape steps, an offensive clinch, and combinations long enough to make opponents reconsider walking forward. Returning to super middleweight would reduce the physical burden, although making 168 again may no longer be practical.

Matchmaking presents another issue. Morrell remains too powerful to become an easy opponent for a rising prospect, but his two defeats have stripped away much of his bargaining power. A soft return fight will bring criticism, while another aggressive volume puncher may push him farther from the top level. Morrell is only 28, and his speed, power, and amateur background still give him valuable tools.

His future depends on accepting that the defense which carried him through 168 pounds does not work against strong light heavyweights. If he returns with the same straight-line retreat and stationary high guard, Chelli’s victory will no longer look like an isolated upset. It will look like a blueprint.

Sports.title: Moses Itauma Exposed as Three Round Fighter
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma’s explosive offense carried him into an IBF heavyweight title fight at 21, but Filip Hrgovic exposed the costly machinery underneath it. George Groves now describes Itauma as a “three-round fighter,” a label that rings true once the sheer physical toll of that early assault is broken down.

Itauma held the speed advantage, tagging Hrgovic with sharp, clean punches during the initial minutes. Rather than establishing control, he pursued the knockout as if Hrgovic were simply another fragile victim waiting to fold. The Croatian veteran absorbed the initial storm, forced the prospect into sustained manual labor, and closed the show in round nine.

“At the moment, he’s a three-round fighter. That’s the sad fact of it,” Groves told Sky Sports.

Groves saw the deterioration developing long before the stoppage. The tactical failure began with Itauma completely discarding distance management. Instead of flicking out light, probing jabs to displace Hrgovic’s guard, he loaded up on heavy hooks from the opening bell. Dozens of those shots crashed harmlessly against Hrgovic’s gloves, yet Itauma continued torqueing his entire core into every strike as though the target were exposed.

Bludgeoning a tight defense with maximum leverage wrecks the back and shoulders. Itauma made that deficit worse by firing extended combinations at top gear. He was emptying championship-level reserves on leather while Hrgovic waited calmly behind his shells.

Top-tier heavyweights pace their attacks. They dial back the force on four punches to mask the fifth, dislodging a guard to create genuine openings. Itauma approached every swing like an executioner. That blitz dismantles limited gatekeepers, but it burns through the reserve tank when a stubborn veteran stays upright.

His movement created a parallel physical leak. Itauma employed an active, darting bounce to step into range and pull away before Hrgovic could fire back. It caught the eye, but that bounce placed relentless strain on his calves.

The moment that bounce disappeared, his posture came apart. Itauma stood straight up, his head movement vanished, and his jaw drifted onto the center line. He quit pivoting off the ropes, retreating instead in straight lines. Hrgovic stopped having to track a mobile target because Itauma planted himself directly in the path of the right hand.

The most glaring flaw was Itauma’s lack of defensive resting skills. Elite fighters know how to steal breathers. Tyson Fury leans his massive frame into clinches to crush a man’s legs, while Oleksandr Usyk circles just outside reach to run thirty seconds off the clock. Itauma attempted to punch his way through suffocating fatigue. Rather than wrapping Hrgovic up, leaning on him or establishing a break in the action, he kept firing wild salvos.

A mental unraveling accompanied the bodily exhaustion. Having grown accustomed to early knockouts, Itauma looked rattled when Hrgovic absorbed his hardest punches without blinking. Lacking a fallback strategy, his shot selection deteriorated into desperate swings, speeding up his own demise.

Rebuilding Itauma requires a far more precise touch than feeding him a passive punching bag. Another two-minute knockout would decorate the highlight reel while leaving the critical flaws unaddressed. He requires an opponent whose defensive habits punish impatience without offering Hrgovic’s devastating counterpunching.

Hughie Fury provides the ideal stylistic puzzle. He fights ugly, stays elusive, ties up inside and refuses to grant young punchers the firefights they crave. Itauma would have to operate behind a steady jab, trap a retreating target along the ropes, and accept that an immediate finish is off the table.

Muscle fiber composition and cardiovascular ceilings are largely genetic. Fighters who carry dense, explosive, fast-twitch muscle mass do not wake up at 28 with the engine of an endurance athlete. George Foreman was an explosive wrecking ball who blew his tank against Muhammad Ali in Zaire at 25, and he never magically transformed into a high-output distance machine. He solved it later in life by stripping away almost all wasted motion, pacing himself to a crawl, and walking men down behind a heavy, thudding jab.

The hard truth for Itauma is that human physiology does not work backward. As heavyweights move out of their early twenties, their bodies naturally thicken, absolute fast-twitch snap dulls, and carrying 240-plus pounds over twelve rounds becomes more taxing on the heart and lungs, not less. If a fighter is hyperventilating and losing his legs after three hard frames at 21, running more miles on the road will not rewrite his DNA.

Right now, Itauma operates like a sports car redlining in first gear. Every punch is loaded with full hip and shoulder torque, every movement is an explosive leap into range, and he has zero concept of how to make an opponent carry his weight when he gets tired. That is catastrophic fuel economy.

If Itauma remains married to that style, he is permanently locked into being a dangerous three-round frontrunner who will get dragged out into deep water and finished by any durable contender with a pulse and a chin. He only stretches his effectiveness to six or seven rounds if he accepts a radical tactical lobotomy:

Sports.title: Joe Louis Crushes Bob Pastor in Detroit Rematch
Sports.content:
Joe Louis settled an old score on September 20, 1939, knocking out Bob Pastor in the 11th round before 33,868 spectators at Briggs Stadium in Detroit. Pastor had escaped him for 10 rounds two years earlier. Louis made certain that the same tactics would not save him again.

Their first meeting took place at Madison Square Garden on January 29, 1937. Pastor, a former New York University fullback, conceded roughly 25 pounds and was listed as a 10-to-1 underdog. He survived by circling, retreating, and refusing to remain within punching range.

The unanimous decision belonged to Louis, but Pastor celebrated reaching the final bell. Sections of the 18,864 crowd booed the winner and treated the challenger’s survival as a moral victory. Their reaction irritated the future champion, who believed Pastor had reduced the contest to a footrace.

By the rematch, Louis (39-1, 35 KOs) was making his eighth defense of the heavyweight championship. Pastor (38-4-4, 17 KOs) had developed into a leading contender. Both men were 25, though Louis held a 17-pound weight advantage at 200 pounds.

Pastor’s camp requested a 20-round fight, believing the extended distance would test the champion’s stamina. It was a disastrous calculation. Pastor prepared to ration his energy across a marathon. Louis attacked from the opening bell as if the fight had been scheduled for three rounds.

A different pursuit strategy also separated the rematch from their 1937 encounter. Instead of following Pastor around the perimeter, the champion used shorter diagonal steps and moved across his escape lane. Pastor repeatedly found his opponent waiting for him.

The adjustment produced four knockdowns in the opening round and another in the second. Yet that early destruction presented Louis with a test of his own. He had spent heavily trying to force the stoppage, and Pastor’s refusal to fold left the champion less explosive through portions of rounds three through six.

There was no reckless chase for the knockout after the early assault failed to finish Pastor. The champion lowered his output, recovered his breathing, and resumed the methodical work of taking away the challenger’s legs. Body punches during close exchanges reduced Pastor’s lateral bounce without wasting energy on punches aimed at an absent target.

Pastor had trained specifically to avoid Louis’s left hook. Trainer Jack Blackburn turned that preparation against him. The champion showed the left, occupied Pastor’s vision with throwaway jabs and drove his right hand through the opening. Pastor’s habit of slipping outside the left placed his head in the route of the punch he truly needed to avoid.

The challenger produced his strongest work in the eighth. Pastor planted his feet, backed Louis toward the ropes, and connected with jabs and short combinations. The sequence exposed a flaw in the champion’s defense. Louis held a high guard but offered limited upper-body movement, allowing an active jab and quick inside punches to reach him before he regained his punching position.

That success carried a price. To back Louis up, Pastor had to abandon the movement that had protected him. Every planted combination created a stationary target. The champion remained calm, absorbed the surge, and continued attacking the body rather than trying to silence Pastor with one wild counter.

A short right badly staggered Pastor in the tenth. By then, the left hand had become a range finder and visual distraction. Pastor was still reacting to the hook, while Louis was measuring him for the right.

Back in the corner after the tenth, the champion told Blackburn that the next round would be the last.

Pastor opened the 11th by jabbing and attempting to circle left along his familiar escape route. Louis extended the left to obstruct his view and close the lane. Pastor moved to evade the punch he expected, and the right hand came over the top.

He never saw it. Pastor crashed to the canvas and remained there for referee Sam Hennessey’s count. The knockout came 38 seconds into the round, after the challenger had been dropped six times.

The victory paid Louis $118,400 from a gross gate of $347,870, while Pastor received $51,800. More importantly, it erased every complaint left behind by their first fight. Pastor had survived by making him chase in New York. In Detroit, the champion cut off the ring, attacked the challenger’s habits, and used the punch Pastor had spent the entire night helping him find.

Sports.title: Terence Crawford Overlooks Ryan Garcia’s Final Golden Boy Fight
Sports.content:
Terence Crawford is mocking Ryan Garcia for choosing Isaac “Pitbull” Cruz after discussing Teofimo Lopez and the winner of Devin Haney’s proposed fight with Jack Catterall or Liam Paro. His criticism ignores the promotional and championship obligations controlling Ryan’s December choice.

“What happened to all the other people you was talking about fighting? You just be talking and putting on a show,” Crawford posted on X.

December is expected to be Ryan’s final fight under his Golden Boy contract. It would be financial lunacy for him to use that obligation on Teofimo when the same matchup may earn him far more as a free agent.

Crawford understands that calculation. He spent years dealing with Bob Arum and Top Rank before gaining control of his career and securing the Errol Spence Jr. fight on favorable terms. Acting as though Ryan should ignore his contract, broadcast rights, and future negotiating power creates an obvious double standard.

Ryan can fight Cruz, complete his Golden Boy deal, and negotiate with Teofimo without his current promoter controlling the event. If Ryan signs with Zuffa Boxing, his purse and share of the event may be considerably larger on Paramount.

Cruz stopped Nestor Bravo on September 19 and would receive little recovery time before moving from light welterweight to 147 pounds. His short, forward-charging attacks also place him directly in range of Ryan’s check left hook. Ryan would hold major advantages in height, reach, and natural size.

Crawford is correct that Ryan uses famous names to control boxing headlines. He is wrong to treat Cruz as proof that Ryan abandoned Teofimo. Ryan is completing his Golden Boy contract against a marketable opponent while saving his best payday for free agency.

Golden Boy also has little incentive to spend months assembling a Teofimo blockbuster for a fighter preparing to leave. Cruz supplies a recognizable opponent and a sellable December event without using the premier matchup Ryan wants for his promotional future. Teofimo may not be available in December anyway. If the WBA orders him to defend his welterweight title against mandatory challenger Catterall, Lopez must accept the fight or surrender the belt. Catterall has already said he will not step aside.

Vacating would hurt Teofimo’s commercial value. His title is a major part of the sales pitch for a Ryan fight. Facing Catterall is dangerous as well. The British southpaw has the timing, patience, and defensive discipline to beat Lopez over twelve rounds. A loss would remove Teofimo from Ryan’s Cinco de Mayo plans.

Teofimo is trapped in a classic no-win situation. The entire justification for him jumping past 140 to grab the WBA welterweight belt was to establish championship leverage at 147. If he vacates to wait around for Ryan, he instantly surrenders the high ground. Fans and media would torch him for ducking a difficult southpaw in Catterall. Without that belt, Teofimo walks into negotiations with Ryan as an ex-champion coming off an avoidance maneuver, stripping him of the primary bargaining chip that makes a Cinco de Mayo pay-per-view event feel essential.

Taking the Catterall fight is just as risky for Teofimo. Catterall has made a career out of defeating explosive counterpunchers with subtle upper body movement and jabs. Teofimo struggles when opponents refuse to engage on his terms or bite on his athletic traps. If Catterall outpoints him, the Ryan fight disappears overnight. Ryan would have zero incentive to fight a beaten, beltless Lopez when other options exist

If Ryan gets caught or worn down by Pitbull, his leverage for free agency plummets, and the May super fight disintegrates before it even reaches the negotiation table.

Crawford’s other suggested opponents are no more realistic for December. Haney’s legal and promotional issues remain unresolved, while fights involving Catterall or Paro would require separate negotiations and television agreements. Three months is not enough time to clear every obstacle and stage an event of that size.

The gamble is not Ryan’s choice of Cruz. It is trusting Teofimo to keep his WBA belt and survive Catterall before Cinco de Mayo arrives.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Delay Leaves Teofimo No Catterall Excuse
Sports.content:
Teofimo Lopez wants Ryan Garcia, but Ryan will not be available for several months. That gives Lopez time to satisfy his WBA obligation against Jack Catterall instead of protecting his position while Ryan takes another fight.

Ryan discussed returning against Isaac Cruz or Angel Fierro in December or January before targeting Teofimo around Cinco de Mayo. Teofimo does not need to spend that entire period waiting.

WBA president Gilberto Mendoza stated in July that the winner of the bout between Rolly Romero and Teofimo must face Catterall next. Catterall now wants that commitment enforced.

“I expect the WBA and Gilberto Mendoza to stand on business, keep their word and honour what was agreed. Like I say, I don’t ask for favours, just what was agreed and what I deserve,” Catterall posted on X.

The WBA may clarify Catterall’s position Monday. President Gilberto Mendoza announced that the championship committee’s decisions will be released then, although he did not identify the divisions involved. With Mendoza already committed publicly to making the Romero-Teofimo winner fight Catterall next, the welterweight ruling will receive immediate scrutiny.

The sporting argument is simple. Ryan can take his winter tune-up while Teofimo defends against Catterall. If both win, the May date between Ryan and Teofimo remains intact.

The business calculation explains the hesitation from Teofimo. Catterall is a southpaw who refuses to provide easy counterpunching opportunities. Teofimo looked erratic against Sandor Martin and Jamaine Ortiz when those southpaws denied him clean exchanges.

Catterall offers another difficult tactical night without delivering the massive financial return of a Ryan event

Avoiding Catterall brings problems. Teofimo would reach May after a long absence while Ryan arrives sharp from a recent winter outing. A dominant victory over Catterall proves Teofimo belongs at the top of the division and makes the bout with Ryan much easier to sell on pay-per-view. Sitting on the shelf also hands Ryan total leverage over purse splits, ring location, and weight terms. Ryan draws massive numbers regardless of who holds the belts. Teofimo needs Ryan to secure the biggest payday of his career.

If the WBA allows Lopez to stay idle while Catterall waits, the organization confirms its mandatory rules mean very little. Teofimo has ample time to make the defense. The only genuine obstacle is the fear that Catterall ruins the entire plan. If Matchroom and Catterall legally corner the WBA and demand an immediate purse bid, the chance of Teofimo vacating the belt is extremely high.

Teofimo knows by now the belt is secondary in this equation. Ryan draws massive gate receipts and pay-per-view buys whether a sanctioning body strap hangs over his shoulder or not. Ryan proved that against Gervonta Davis and Devin Haney, generating elite commercial numbers without needing sanctioning body validation.

For Teofimo, holding the WBA title is useful for billing, but holding onto it becomes reckless if defending it requires facing Catterall. Catterall’s ring movement and refusal to trade invite the exact difficulties that caused Teofimo problems against Jamaine Ortiz and Sandor Martin. A spoiler-style decision loss to Catterall destroys Teofimo’s leverage, ruins the Cinco de Mayo payday, and drops him completely out of the conversation.

Vacating the belt would be a calculated business move rather than a surrender. If Teofimo drops the WBA strap, he removes the obligation, avoids the stylistic trap Catterall presents, and walks straight into negotiations with Ryan based purely on his own name and promotional profile. Dropping the belt costs him sanctioning fees and a piece of hardware, but risking it against Catterall could cost him tens of millions of dollars. If the WBA genuinely threatens to strip him, expect Teofimo to drop the belt first and claim he outgrew sanctioning body politics.

Sports.title: Chris Eubank Jr. Trains With Paydays Waiting
Sports.content:
Chris Eubank Jr. is back on the heavy bag, flashing training clips that signal plans for another massive payday before 2026 closes out. While no deal is signed, Conor Benn and Hamzah Sheeraz sit as the two prime British pay-per-view options waiting for him at 168 pounds.

That gut on Eubank is not muscle. That is pure luxury padding bought by British pay-per-view receipts. To step into a ring with Benn, Hamzah Sheeraz, or any opponent dug up to face him, he will need to burn off significant excess baggage.

The immediate problem is whether Zuffa Boxing has any genuine desire to fund a third clash between Eubank and Benn. Zuffa invested heavily to stage Benn against Ryan in Las Vegas on September 12, only to watch Benn blown out in under two rounds. That defeat shattered the myth that Benn could hold his own against elite world punchers. Paying eight-figure sums to finance a third installment of a domestic soap opera makes zero business sense for Dana White and Zuffa.

Public interest in a third meeting is dead in the water. Hardcore and casual fans would recognize it immediately as a shameless cash grab between two celebrity fighters who operate on famous surnames rather than world-level achievements. Neither Eubank nor Benn has proven they can beat prime, dangerous opposition at the elite tier.

Writing another massive check for Benn to face an out-of-shape, 37-year-old Eubank produces zero return on investment outside of local UK curiosity. Zuffa targets global streaming metrics and brand dominance, not funding bloated purses for domestic nostalgia acts coming off bad losses. If Benn and Eubank demand the kind of money they made in their first two stadium meetings, White and Zuffa will tell them to go pound sand.

Matching Eubank with Hamzah Sheeraz brings its own commercial headaches. Sheeraz destroyed his standing with boxing fans when he gave up his WBO super middleweight belt rather than face Janibek Alimkhanuly. Abdicating a world title to protect a record leaves a terrible stain, removing any argument that Sheeraz is an elite attraction.

Sheeraz is not a pay-per-view needle-mover. He has shown zero natural charisma, no edge in interviews, and lacks the personality required to play a theatrical heel. Eubank can talk all day, but one man cannot carry a press tour if the other guy stands there like a statue giving generic media training answers. In the UK, you might scrape together a modest gate at an arena based purely on Eubank’s notoriety, but globally the event will do terrible business.

If Zuffa shuts the vault on a Benn trilogy, both men are trapped. Benn holds zero leverage, Eubank is carrying ring rust and visible weight, and Sheeraz brings minimal commercial draw outside the UK. The easy money built on family dynasties has run out, leaving both camps staring at cold market realities.

Chris Eubank Jr’s recent social media activity suggests a return could be near 🍿 pic.twitter.com/Tnr9QQhPQA — Ring Magazine (@ringmagazine) September 20, 2026

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua Won’t Stay With Usyk For Fury Camp
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua turning to Ben Davison to crack the Tyson Fury code is a flawed strategy built on outdated history. While Joshua balances visits to Oleksandr Usyk’s team in Spain and Derrick James in Texas, Davison’s presence in camp is being sold as an inside track on Fury. In reality, Davison’s playbook offers nothing useful against the Kronk fighter Fury became years ago.

Joshua recently spent time in Spain working around Team Usyk, yet he has returned to Davison’s gym in Essex while keeping ties with Derrick James open. Eddie Hearn has refrained from naming a single head trainer or confirming a permanent camp base, although he took steps to remove doubt surrounding Davison’s presence.

“I think in some capacity he’ll stay close to them,” Hearn stated regarding Joshua’s ties to Usyk’s team. “He’s always been, even when Ben wasn’t his principal trainer, working with him strategically, talking all the time. I think he respects Ben a lot. Obviously, there’s probably a feeling that Ben Davison knows Tyson Fury extremely well. I don’t know AJ’s final decision to where he’s going to locate his training camp, but Ben Davison will definitely be involved in that camp and that process.”

Davison’s familiarity with Fury cuts both ways. Fury knows how Davison schemes, how he sequences combinations, and how he reacts when a fight slips away from the whiteboard. Any blueprint reliant on years past will run into a fighter who knows the playbook just as well.

The bigger problem is that Davison worked with a completely different fighter. Davison guided the elusive version of Fury who completed a comeback and survived Deontay Wilder across twelve rounds in 2018. That fighter was a survival project built on light jabs, lateral evasion, and snatching rounds from the outside. Fury realized the limitations of that safety-first approach, parted ways with Davison in late 2019, and went to SugarHill Steward to resurrect the Kronk style.

Under Steward, Fury abandoned the backfoot bouncing, added twenty pounds of solid bulk, and committed to walking opponents down. He uses heavyweight bullying to control the ring: collar ties, framing with the forearms, turning opponents in the clinch, and dropping his upper body weight over their neck and shoulders. Davison never coached that style, never cornered Fury while he executed it, and was abandoned because Fury outgrew the light-hitting system Davison specializes in.

Preparing Joshua for the 2018 iteration of Fury is a trap. The modern Fury will not waste energy trying to outbox Joshua cleanly from the outside. He will lean his massive frame on Joshua, tie up his arms, and make every round an exhausting physical grind.

Consulting Team Usyk brings its own tactical contradictions. Usyk neutralized Fury using rapid lateral escapes, constant rhythm disruption, and cruiserweight agility. Joshua is a muscular, upright heavyweight who moves in straight lines. Forcing Joshua to mimic Usyk’s fluid footwork while executing Davison’s mechanical combinations will only leave him disjointed.

Trainer hopping has defined Joshua’s post-McCracken career. Moving through Robert Garcia, Derrick James, Davison, and Team Usyk points to a fighter looking for external solutions to internal doubts. When Joshua faces adversity, conflicting philosophies will paralyze him.

Joshua does not need a committee of trainers offering polite suggestions. He needs a single corner authority with absolute control over the strategy. If Joshua carries multiple voices into the ring, the hesitation will give Fury all the openings he needs.

The recent disaster with Moses Itauma against Filip Hrgovic exposed the exact same systemic flaws that showed up when Daniel Dubois ran right through Joshua at Wembley. Davison builds intricate, lab-tested game plans for the opening bell, but the moment a heavyweight fight turns into an ugly, grueling dogfight, his system breaks down.

Against Hrgovic, Itauma had everything going his way early, scored a knockdown, and swept rounds, yet the tank emptied completely because the conditioning foundation was not built for deep waters. When the crisis hit, Davison had no Plan B, telling a gassed 21-year-old to take deep breaths instead of giving him a practical survival strategy.

That identical corner paralysis was on full display against Dubois. Joshua walked out stiff, mechanical, and completely unprepared for a fighter charging forward with bad intentions. When Dubois clipped him in the first round, Davison looked lost. There were no adjustments to clinch, buy time, or change the target. Joshua was left wandering into right hands until the fifth-round finish.

The fact that Joshua kept Davison after the Dubois demolition shows a fighter desperately clinging to the comfort of Davison’s praise rather than demanding hard-nosed accountability. Joshua believes Davison holds the secret blueprint to beat Fury because Davison was in Fury’s corner years ago.

Relying on Davison to outscheme Fury is a massive tactical error. Fury knows Davison’s limitations better than anyone, which is why Fury left him for SugarHill Steward in the first place. If Joshua walks into a fight against Fury depending on Davison’s whiteboard tactics, he is walking into the exact same trap that cost Itauma his undefeated record and left Joshua flat on his back against Dubois.

Ghana News.title: Black Stars: Thomas-Asante receives late call-up for September-October games
Ghana News.content:
Coventry City forward Brandon Thomas-Asante has been handed a late call-up to the Black Stars team for the upcoming international break following his injury over the weekend.

The forward is expected to join the national team for the upcoming games against Côte d’Ivoire, Gambia and Morocco.

Thomas-Asante has been drafted in to as one of two replacements with Mohammed Kudus dropping out and Prince Adu Kwabena’s head injury over the weekend.

The forward was part of the Black Stars squad at the 2026 FIFA World Cup in Mexico, Canada and USA, where the team got knocked out in the Round of 32.

Thomas-Asante set up Caleb Yirenkyi for the only goal of the game in the win over Panama in Ghana’s first game.

He was initially left out of the 24-man squad named by Carlos Queiroz for the upcoming assignments but gets a late invitation to be a part of the team.

Ghana will open their international break campaign with a game against Côte d’Ivoire in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers before hosting Gambia at the Accra Sports Stadium five days later.

The Black Stars then wrap up the window with a friendly against Morocco on October 4.

Ghana News.title: NPP Techiman South demands immediate release of detained Nurse Salomey Awiti Baffoe
Ghana News.content:
The New Patriotic Party (NPP) Techiman South Constituency has issued a strong condemnation of the arrest and continued remand of Madam Salomey Awiti Bafoh, a senior nursing officer and mother of three, demanding her immediate release or the granting of reasonable bail.

The press briefing, held at the Techiman South Constituency Office and addressed by Communications Officer Mohammad Mukarram Abdallah, drew a large crowd of party faithfuls clad in red bands, chanting for the release of the detained nurse.



The emotionally charged atmosphere underscored the constituency's deep concern over what they describe as a troubling abuse of state power.

The Arrest and Detention

According to reports, Madam Salomey was taken from her home in Hansua, near Techiman, late at night on September 13. Her family reportedly struggled for days to establish her whereabouts and the precise reason for her arrest. Conflicting accounts regarding the date and circumstances of her detention have further heightened tensions.

The Police have alleged that Madam Salomey was involved in the publication and circulation of false news and allegedly assisted in redistributing content associated with the "Ghana Jollof" account. She has pleaded not guilty to all charges.

Despite her lawyers' application for bail, she was remanded in police custody until September 30 while investigations continue. She was taken to the Adentan Circuit Court, far from her home constituency—a move the NPP describes as deeply questionable.

Party Leaders Demand Answers

The press conference featured passionate appeals from key party figures. Women's Organizer Nana Akosua Sakyiwaa questioned why "a mother of three was snatched away from her children for days without proper charges." Lawyer Amadu Berma Sulemana raised pointed questions about the arrest procedure and the specific charges outlined on the charge sheet.

The NPP Communications Directorate joined calls by Flagbearer Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia and Member of Parliament for Techiman South, Hon. Martin Adjei-Mensah Korsah, for Madam Salomey's immediate release.

"This matter is no longer only about one nurse. It is about the protection of constitutional rights, the limits of state power, and the future of democracy in Ghana," Mr. Abdallah declared.

Nine Demands for Government

The constituency directorate issued nine pointed questions demanding answers from the government:

Who authorised Madam Salomey's arrest? Which agency carried out the operation? Under what legal authority was she taken from her home? Why was the arrest conducted at night? Why was she taken to the Adentan Circuit Court? Why did her family reportedly struggle to locate her? What specific evidence requires her continued detention? Why can she not be granted reasonable bail while investigations continue? Who will take responsibility if it is established that her rights were violated?

A Warning for All Ghanaians

The NPP Communications Officer framed the case as a warning sign for all citizens, regardless of political affiliation.

"Today, it is Madam Salomey. Tomorrow, it could be any journalist, nurse, teacher, trader, student, religious leader, or ordinary citizen who expresses an opinion that those in power find uncomfortable," he warned.

The party rejected any suggestion that it supports violence, incitement, or the deliberate publication of false information. However, it equally rejected "the abuse of state power, selective enforcement, intimidation, and the use of security agencies to silence citizens."

Calls for Proportionality and Due Process

The NPP emphasized that it is not seeking special treatment for Madam Salomey but rather demanding equal treatment under the law.

"Remand is not punishment. Arrest is not conviction. Allegation is not proof," the statement read. "The continued detention of a working mother, without a demonstrated need to keep her in custody, raises serious questions about proportionality, fairness, and the government's respect for due process."

The party called on the Attorney-General, the Inspector-General of Police, the National Security Minister, and all relevant authorities to intervene immediately, demanding:

· Immediate review of Madam Salomey's continued detention

· Granting of reasonable bail, subject to lawful conditions

· Full explanation of the circumstances surrounding her arrest

· Transparency regarding the role of National Security in the matter

· Respect for her constitutional rights and dignity

· Assurance that no citizen will be intimidated for expressing a lawful opinion

"We Will Not Be Silent"

The press briefing concluded with a defiant message from the constituency directorate:

"The NPP Techiman South Constituency will not remain silent while the rights and dignity of a constituent are placed at risk. We will not allow the people of Techiman South to be treated as though they have no voice."

"We will resist the oppressor's rule with all our will and might," Mr. Abdallah declared to thunderous applause.

The party vowed to continue standing with Madam Salomey and her family, demanding transparency, accountability, and the defense of constitutional freedoms.

As the case continues, all eyes remain on the government's next move—and on whether the calls for justice for Madam Salomey will be heeded.

Ghana News.title: ‘Let’s stop the politics’ — Dafeamekpor calls for united fight against drug trafficking
Ghana News.content:
Majority Leader and MP for South Dayi, Rockson-Nelson Dafeamekpor, has waded into the ongoing debate over drug trafficking in Ghana, arguing that the issue should not be reduced to partisan politics.

In a post on X, formerly known as Twitter, Mr Dafeamekpor listed a series of drug seizures and arrests recorded in Ghana and involving Ghanaians or foreign nationals between 2017 and 2024.

He cited cases involving cocaine and heroin seizures at the Kotoka International Airport (KIA), Ghana Post and other locations, as well as a major cocaine seizure in Nsawam in 2008.

Mr Dafeamekpor also referenced a January 2009 US Department of State report which described Ghana as a transshipment point for illegal drugs, particularly cocaine from South America and heroin from Afghanistan and Pakistan.

He said the report noted that drugs transited through Accra’s Kotoka International Airport to Europe and the United States, while also contributing to domestic drug consumption.

The South Dayi MP used the cases to argue that drug trafficking is a longstanding national challenge that predates the current administration.

He called for a national approach to tackling the menace rather than partisan exchanges.

“So let’s stop the politics and support Govt efforts to fight the drug menace as a Nation.”

He added: “We were declared a drug trafficking hub under an NPP Govt in 2008.”

Ghana News.title: Chief Justice Baffoe-Bonnie leads new 11-member Council for Legal Education and Training Board
Ghana News.content:
The Council for Legal Education and Training (CLET) has unveiled its new 11-member Board of Members, chaired by Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie.

The board brings together senior members of the judiciary, government officials, and academics from some of Ghana’s leading law schools and tertiary institutions.

The members are:

Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie – Chief Justice of the Republic of Ghana

– Chief Justice of the Republic of Ghana Justice Gabriel Scott Pwamang – Justice of the Supreme Court

– Justice of the Supreme Court Justice Jennifer Abena Dadzie – Justice of the Court of Appeal

– Justice of the Court of Appeal Her Honour Siran Mahama – Circuit Court Judge

– Circuit Court Judge Dr Justice Srem-Sai – Deputy Attorney-General and Minister for Justice

– Deputy Attorney-General and Minister for Justice Dr Clement Abas Apaak – Deputy Minister for Education

– Deputy Minister for Education Prof Augustine Ocloo – Deputy Director-General, Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC)

– Deputy Director-General, Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) Prof Kofi Abotsi – Dean, University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA) Law School

– Dean, University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA) Law School Prof Peter Atudiwe Atupare – Dean, University of Ghana School of Law

– Dean, University of Ghana School of Law Prof Cynthia Forson – Deputy Provost, Lancaster University

– Deputy Provost, Lancaster University Prof Raymond Atuguba – Director-General for Legal Education

The composition gives the board representation from the judiciary, the ministries responsible for justice and education, the tertiary education regulator and major law faculties.

CLET is responsible for overseeing aspects of legal education and professional legal training in Ghana, including the administration of the Ghana School of Law and related regulatory functions.

The new board comes as Ghana continues efforts to implement reforms in legal education following the passage of the Legal Education Act.

The Ghana Bar Association has previously called for the operationalisation of the legislation and the establishment of its governing structures, arguing that this would provide the institutional framework needed to advance reforms in legal education.

The inclusion of senior judicial officers, government representatives and academics on the new board is expected to provide oversight across the different areas involved in legal education and professional training.

The board will now be expected to take forward its responsibilities under the legal education framework, including providing oversight for the development and administration of legal education and training in Ghana.

Ghana News.title: Decades of silent diplomacy: Baba Issifu Kamara at 70
Ghana News.content:
He is a silent and consequential player in security and the geopolitics of West Africa and beyond. He is a geopolitical bridge builder and a quiet broker of peace and security between and among major geopolitical actors!

His conviction that regional stability prerequisite for development has taken him far and near, playing important roles in Africa. Recently, ECOWAS renewed his term of office as ECOWAS Special Envoy on Counter-Terrorism.

Happy 70th Birthday to H.E. Ambassador Baba Issifu Kamara, an indefatigable leader, a master organizer, astute statesman, detribalised Ghanaian, father, kingmaker, dependable ally, a perfect gentleman, philanthropist, and a role model par excellence.

Today, we celebrate not just your age, but a life of service, leadership, wisdom and impact. We celebrate you, and we celebrate with you on this milestone.

May the years ahead bring you greater fulfilment, sound health, enduring grace, and even more opportunities for humanity to continue to benefit from your extraordinary pedigree of service with dignity. You have touched many souls.

70 years old is a milestone that honors a lifetime of your leadership, patriotism, and impactful service to the nation and the Globe as an Outstanding Statesman.

Today, we celebrate your seven decades of a life entirely dedicated to the progress, unity, and upliftment of West Africa and the World. Your visionary leadership has not only shaped our nation’s history but has also deeply touched and transformed many souls.

As you join the revered club of septuagenarians, we honour your unwavering integrity, your wisdom, and the enduring legacy you continue to build. A Ghana that is richer because of your service.

May your days ahead be filled with good health and joy! Reaching this milestone is a testament to Allah’s grace upon your life.

Beyond the policies and the political milestones, your greatest legacy is the countless lives you have touched along the way. Your kindness, mentorship, and love for the people have left an indelible mark on our hearts.

We pray that this new decade brings you abundant strength, happiness, and fulfillment.

Happy 70th Birthday to a phenomenal statesman who has spent his life building people and building nations. You have touched so many souls with your wisdom and leadership.

The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) recently appointed you, Ambassador Baba Kamara, as Head of Mission for its Election Observation Mission (EOM) to the Republic of Guinea-Bissau ahead of the country’s general elections scheduled for 23rd November 2025.

Ambassador Kamara, you have been recognized extensively for your diplomatic and security expertise, spanning more than four decades of public service to Ghana and West Africa.

A former National Security Advisor, you served in several high-level roles, including Ghana’s High Commissioner to Nigeria (with concurrent accreditation to Cameroon, Chad, and São Tomé & Príncipe) and Ghana’s Permanent Representative to the ECOWAS Commission from 2009–2012.

You also diligently served as Senior Presidential Advisor before assuming the role of National Security Advisor between 2013 and 2017.

Ambassador Kamara, you are widely recognised as a respected statesman with deep insight into peace, security, democracy, and governance across West Africa. We are proud of you. Your experience in elections tells it all. Serving as Deputy Head of the ECOWAS Observation Mission for Nigeria’s 2023 Presidential Elections, as well as participating in election monitoring exercises in Togo and Côte d’Ivoire.

At 70, Ambassador Kamara's position of Special Envoy for Counterterrorism for ECOWAS, a role to which he was appointed in July 2023 by the Authority of Heads of State and Government in recognition of his depth of experience in regional security and diplomacy, is commendable.

BABA KAMARA REFUSES TO LEAVE GUINEA

EXEMPLARY LEADERSHIP

Ambassador Baba Kamara chose to stay in Guinea-Bissau—not Guinea—during the November 2025 political turmoil to ensure the safety of all 130+ ECOWAS election observers under his command.

Here are the key details of what happened:

The Situation: As the Head of the ECOWAS Election Observation Mission for Guinea-Bissau’s November elections, Ambassador Kamara faced a sudden military takeover and political unrest in Bissau.

The Decision: While former Nigerian President Goodluck Jonathan and other officials departed on special flights, Kamara declined early evacuation.

The Resolution: He insisted on remaining behind until a chartered ASKY Airlines flight was successfully arranged to safely evacuate every single member of the observation team home.

Welcome to the 7th floor. Africa salutes you, Sir. We are proud of you. Your name will be written in the sands of time on the Globe. Happy Birthday, ECOWAS CITIZEN BABA KAMARA.

From Maxwell Okamafo Addo, a young person who has drunk and benefited from your foundation and Fountain of Wisdom.Eid Milad Sa'eed - عيد ميلاد عيد ميلاد سعيد

Ghana News.title: 30% transport fare hike still on the table, talks resume Tuesday – GPRTU
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Private Road Transport Union (GPRTU) has rejected claims by the National Petroleum Authority (NPA) that its proposed 30% increase in transport fares has been put on hold.

The union says no agreement has been reached with government to suspend the proposed adjustment, insisting that negotiations with the Ministry of Transport remain inconclusive.

Speaking on Joynews, deputy Public Relations Officer of the GPRTU, Samuel Amoah, said the two sides were still negotiating the proposed increase at their last meeting on Friday, September 18.

“There has never been any agreement with the government that we are suspending our proposed increment. The last meeting we had with the minister was last Friday, and we were still negotiating the 30 percent increase, but there wasn’t any conclusion,” he said.

His comments contradict an earlier position by NPA Chief Executive, Godwin Edudzi Tamakloe, who said engagements with transport operators had helped put the planned fare increase “on ice.”

Mr Tamakloe said government and transport operators had been discussing how to manage the impact of rising fuel prices and other operating costs without immediately passing the full burden on to commuters.

Mr Amoah said the GPRTU remains committed to its proposed 30% adjustment, although the union is prepared to negotiate.

He said the union had indicated during Friday’s meeting that any reduction from the proposed 30% would not take the figure below 25%.

“We are pushing for 30% increment. That is what was on the table at the last Friday negotiation. And we made the ministry understand that if we have to come down, we still come anything less than 25%. And that is where we ended it,” he said.

The GPRTU had earlier submitted a proposal for a fare review to the Ministry of Transport, with a joint team comprising the ministry, the GPRTU and the Ghana Road Transport Coordinating Council (GRTCC) tasked with reviewing the various cost inputs before a final decision is taken.

The union had also previously stated that existing approved fares remained in force while the review process was ongoing.

Mr Amoah cited rising fuel prices, spare parts, insurance and vehicle maintenance among the factors behind the proposed adjustment.

The development comes after the NPA raised the price floor for petrol and diesel from September 16, with the authority setting the floors at GH¢16 per litre for petrol and GH¢16.77 for diesel. Some Oil Marketing Companies subsequently adjusted their pump prices.

The GPRTU has argued that the higher fuel costs have compounded existing pressures from other inputs required to operate commercial vehicles.

According to Mr Amoah, the GPRTU and the Ministry of Transport are expected to resume discussions on Tuesday, September 22.

He said the parties had agreed to postpone their meeting because Monday, September 21, was a public holiday.

“We all agreed that tomorrow morning we’ll go back to the transport ministry again to conclude the percentage increment,” he said.

The outcome of that engagement will determine whether the proposed adjustment is maintained, reduced or otherwise revised.

Meanwhile, Mr Amoah said GPRTU members have been directed not to participate in a sit-down strike announced by the Progressive Transport Owners Association (PROTOA) over the rising cost of vehicle maintenance.

The directive comes amid broader concerns among commercial transport operators about the cost of keeping vehicles on the road.

For now, however, the GPRTU’s proposed fare adjustment remains subject to negotiations with government, with no new fare officially approved.

Ghana News.title: KATH marks 70th anniversary with inter-directorate games
Ghana News.content:
The Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital (KATH) has marked its 70th anniversary with an inter-directorate fun games event aimed at strengthening staff bonds, promoting teamwork and encouraging healthy lifestyles among employees.

The event, held at Paa Joe Stadium, KNUST, brought together staff from various directorates, members of management and families for a day of sporting and recreational activities.

The programme featured football, athletics, table tennis, volleyball, basketball and indoor games, providing staff with an opportunity to interact outside their usual work environments.

Speaking at the event, Dr. Yaw Opare Larbi, Deputy Medical Director and Chairman of the KATH 70th Anniversary Operational Committee, said the games were organised to bring staff together and foster stronger relationships across the hospital.

“Activities such as this bring us together and we get to make new friends. And this is important for teamwork. It’s important for cohesion,” he said.

He said the event was particularly significant because it formed part of the hospital’s celebrations to mark seven decades of service.

According to Dr. Larbi, KATH has more than 6,000 staff, making activities that encourage interaction important to building unity and improving teamwork.

He also said the games had a health-promotion component, giving staff an opportunity to exercise while encouraging them to become more conscious of their physical wellbeing.

Anniversary activities

Dr. Larbi said KATH’s 70th anniversary celebrations were launched in December 2025, following the hospital’s attainment of 70 years in 2025, with activities scheduled throughout the anniversary year.

One of the activities already undertaken was an outreach in Nkoranza in the Bono East Region, where a multidisciplinary team of about 50 KATH health professionals joined local health workers during the installation of a new chief and queen mother.

The team conducted health education and screening exercises and engaged the public through radio programmes as part of the hospital’s contribution to the community.

Dr. Larbi said other activities lined up include community outreach programmes involving health screening, health education and blood donation, as well as a public lecture focusing on the history and development of KATH.

The public lecture will also feature research dissemination, allowing the hospital to showcase research conducted by its professionals and its contribution to healthcare knowledge.

The anniversary programme is expected to culminate in a Thanksgiving Service and Grand Durbar, where outstanding workers will be recognised, followed by a dinner dance.

Dr. Larbi said the celebrations provide an opportunity for the hospital to reflect on its history while positioning itself for the future.

KATH’s contribution to healthcare

KATH Chief Executive Officer, Dr. Paa Kwesi Baidoo, said the inclusion of sports in the anniversary programme was consistent with the hospital’s broader health mandate.

“You know, Komfo Anokye is a health institution. We provide healthcare services. And exercise or sports goes with health,” he said.

Dr. Baidoo said the hospital’s contribution over the past 70 years extended beyond treating patients to supporting medical education, research and the broader healthcare system.

He disclosed that KATH attended to more than 364,000 patients in 2025, highlighting the scale of services provided by the institution.

He said the hospital serves people from different backgrounds and continues to fulfil its mandate as a tertiary healthcare institution.

Preparing for the next 70 years

Dr. Baidoo also highlighted ongoing infrastructure projects intended to expand the hospital’s capacity and improve service delivery.

These include a Cardiac Catheterization/Intervention Centre being undertaken through the Ghana Medical Trust Fund, the redevelopment of an abandoned office complex and the construction of a multi-floor pharmacy complex.

He said the developments were part of efforts to ensure that KATH could provide expanded services as it looks towards the next 70 years.

For Dr. Larbi, KATH’s contribution over its seven decades has centred on four key areas: advanced clinical care, undergraduate and postgraduate training, research, and support for lower-level healthcare institutions.

He said the hospital’s research activities continue to inform healthcare practice, while professionals trained at KATH have gone on to serve in different parts of the world.

As the anniversary celebrations continue, KATH is expected to use the remaining activities to celebrate its history, recognise the contribution of its staff and communities, and set the stage for its next chapter.

Ghana News.title: Black Stars: Godwin Attram replaces Desmond Ofei as assistant coach
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Football Association (GFA) has confirmed the appointment of former Ghana international Godwin Attram as assistant coach of the Black Stars.

Attram joins the Black Stars technical team replacing Desmond Ofei, who will now concentrate fully on his role as head coach of the Black Meteors, Ghana's U23 national team.

The appointment forms part of the GFA's technical restructuring as the Black Stars prepare for the upcoming 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers and other international assignments.

Attram, a former Black Stars midfielder, brings a wealth of experience as both a player and a coach.

The ex-PSV Eindhoven and Silkeborg IF playmaker previously served as Head Coach of Great Olympics and has been involved in various national youth team structures. He is highly regarded for his work in player development and his modern approach to the game.

Desmond Ofei, who combined his role with the Black Stars with his duties as head coach of the Black Satellites and later the Black Meteors, will now focus exclusively on leading Ghana's U23 side as they prepare for the next Olympic Games qualifiers.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
