Send your identity number to at a cost of R1 per SMS. This option is for voting-station special votes only IEC office: Visit your local IEC office and submit a completed special vote application form

Manual applications must be hand-delivered to the local IEC office. The completed form may be delivered by another person on the applicant’s behalf.

Important reminder for voters

A special vote is not automatically granted simply because an application has been submitted. The IEC must receive and approve the application.



Voters approved for a home visit will cast their ballot at their approved address within their registered voting district.

Those approved for a voting-station special vote will vote at the voting station where they are registered.

The IEC has urged eligible voters not to wait until the deadline to submit their applications as preparations are required to facilitate the special voting process.



The opening of applications marks another step in preparations for the 4 November 2026 Local Government Elections.

World.title: Wallabies not ‘scared’ of Springboks
World.content:
As it stands on the current World Rugby rankings, the Springboks have a healthy lead in the No 1 spot, while the Wallabies are dwelling down in seventh place.

However, similarly to the All Blacks, Australia do seem to be enjoying what is referred to in football as a ‘new manager bounce’.

With new coach Les Kiss at the helm, the Wallabies have produced consecutive victories over Japan (35–32 in Tokyo, 56–17 in Townsville) and an away win over Argentina (27–21 in Mendoza), although that three-game winning streak recently ended in a hard-fought 28–28 draw against Argentina.



There is now set to be a whole new challenge as the Wallabies take on the high-flying Springboks, who also won 30-12 on their last visit to Perth in 2024.

Wallabies talking a good game ahead of Springboks’ Test

In the lead up to this Sunday’s clash, wing Max Jorgensen says the Wallabies will not be daunted by the prospect of facing the Springboks.

“They’re all human, they’re just a rugby team, so we’re not scared,” he told Code Sports.



Meanwhile, loose forward Carlo Tizzano echoed these sentiments.

“South Africa are the best team in the world, so what better way to test what we’ve been doing and everything we’ve been working on than doing it against the best?” he said in the build-up to the one-off meeting at Optus Stadium.

“To get the win will be unreal,” Tizzano added. “I think we’ve grown a lot since we last played them in Perth.



“But it’s all about making sure we do all the things we’ve been talking about during the week. And if we do that, then we should get a good result.

“We’re obviously going to have to lift a lot, and there’s a lot to work on, but I feel like we’ve made some awesome strides as a team, not only on the field but off the field as well.

“I think everyone’s really proud of each other and how we’ve handled our business, and obviously there’s a lot more to work on as well, so that’s really exciting.”



The Boks, meanwhile, cannot gain any ranking points by beating the Wallabies, but the world champions will remain No 1 even if they lose on Sunday.

World.title: One of South Africa’s safest golf estates is selling plots for R90 000
World.content:
For many South Africans, living on a golf estate is the ideal.

But building a dream home on a plot is often out of reach.

In one small town, the golf estate offers safety and an affordable way to enjoy the relaxed lifestyle.



South Africa’s Safest Golf Estate

The Katberg Eco Golf Estate on the outskirts of Balfour could be the country’s safest golf estate.

Katberg in Seymour is in the Amathole region of the Eastern Cape.

The town has a population of 4 536 and a crime rate of 3.09%.

In the three months ending June 2026, the town reported 22 crimes, down from the same period last year when 33 crimes were reported.

The most common crime in Balfour is residential burglary; in the first quarter, 6 such crimes were reported.

Property in Katberg

The Katberg golf estate is a 400-hectare estate set in the Winterberg mountains.



The estate overlooks the 18-hole championship golf course and adjoining hotel.

Property in the Katberg golf estate starts at R40 000. But a handful of properties are on sale for R90 000.

So far this year, 15 sales were registered with the deeds office. The average sale price among these is R66 000.

All of these sales have been plots. However, a rare listing for a fully furnished 4-bedroom home is on the market for R2 million.

Life in Balfour

Buyers should prepare for life away from city amenities.

The Katberg Eco Golf Estate is very remote.

It’s a 2-hour 30-minute drive from Ko Gumpo City (East London) on the R351. Large portions of the road leading to the estate are untarred.

It’s roughly a 3-hour drive from Port Elizabeth.

The nearest city is Qonce (King William’s Town), 2 hours away, where residents can find amenities like malls and medical facilities.

Of course, closer to home, residents can spend their time at the Katberg Manor golf clubhouse, which has tennis courts, a pool, and a restaurant.

In the vicinity, residents can go trout fishing or explore the hiking and mountain biking trails.

World.title: Ferrari Amalfi and Purosangue tamed on SA roads
World.content:
When you receive an invitation from Scuderia Ferrari South Africa to sample their two newest thoroughbreds, best to not overthink it. You simply RSVP “yes”, even as wonder if you received the invite in error. Because, of all the automotive objects out there, anything wearing the infamous Cavallino Rampante, or Prancing Horse, is probably the most admired by car lovers and laypeople alike.

A Ferrari is more than a means of transport. It is a cultural symbol of Italy, a manifestation of artistic flair and engineering prowess. And for one day only, we were given access to the new Amalfi – a front-engine, V8-powered 2+2 grand tourer. And the marque’s opinion-dividing SUV – the naturally aspirated V12, four-wheel-drive Purosangue.

FERRARI AMALFI

The new Amalfi continues the naming trend of places you’d love to drive it to on a summer grand tour. Image: Ray Leathern

The day’s proceedings dictate we’ll drive the Ferrari Amalfi first. As far as styling is concerned, it breathes new life into the marque’s front-engined configuration. All smooth, simple, stretched surfaces, it’s pretty in pictures but even more arresting in the metal. Like a 365 GTB Daytona for the present day.



Power and torque from the wonderful twin-turbo V8 now hits a clavicle-crushing 470 kW and 760 Nm. Zero to 100 km/h is dispatched in a claimed 3.3 seconds. And as I carefully nose that long bonnet out the parking lot into Paarl main road, I’m immediately relieved by how easy it is to pilot at mundane speeds. The nose isn’t so low enough it requires a lift function (although one is optionally available).

There’s freedom to move in the cockpit, see out and place the car on the road between dawdling Ubers. The steering is eager, throttle response well tamed (for now) and it rides firmly but smoothly over road imperfections. On the inside, I have enough time to note the fit and finish, which treads a fine line between sophisticated and sporty. Many of the haptic feedback buttons of the Roma have been done away with in the Amalfi. Owners say they prefer hard buttons.

UNLEASH THE STALLIONS

The Manettino-festooned steering wheel of any Ferrari is technical work of art. A must have with the rev-indicator lights up top. Image: Ray Leathern

Every new Ferrari is basically tailormade to the buyer’s specification. And this Amalfi was specified with a Manettino-festooned steering wheel, with F1-style shift lights that match the engine revs. The marque calls the steering wheel the ‘man/machine interface.’ Virtually every function from ignition, headlamps, wipers, suspension, driving modes and indicators is all controlled on the wheel. In particular, the indicators are thumb-operated buttons on either side. And why no other manufacturer has attempted to copy these, we’ll never know, because they make indicating as involving as changing gear with the paddle shifters.



The engine up front is Ferrari’s multiple Engine of the Year-winning twin-turbo V8. And like all turbo Prancing Horses, it follows a zero-lag concept. Its vocal range is characterised by boost and turbo spool low down, but once you press on to higher speed ranges, it’s got all the charisma of a naturally aspirated V8. The absolute key to this accomplishment is Variable Boost Management. A clever system that adjusts torque delivery to suit the gear selected, with more twisting force available as you climb the gears.

As a result, you have confidence at low rpm that you won’t overwhelm the rear tyres with torque demand. And engine pick-up increases as the revs and noise rise, encouraging you to keep chasing maximum kilowatts. This is a routine I take to with relish as we scythe up and down the stunningly beautiful mountain roads beyond Paarl. A truly memorable, spine-tingling driving experience.

FERRARI PUROSANGUE

The marque calls it a Ferrari Utility Vehicle (FUV) rather than a full-on SUV. Spend time with it and that makes perfect sense. Image: Ray Leathern

Then at the halfway stop, I swap cars to the Ferrari Purosangue. The brand insists this isn’t an SUV but rather a Ferrari Utility Vehicle (FUV). And credit to Maranello, because as semantically challenging as this is, it’s also a pretty apt description. Everything about the Ferrari Purosangue plays into contradiction. Step inside and you’re not so much sharing a cabin as occupying four individually sculpted cockpits, for the driver and three passengers.



Unlike the elegant Amalfi, at the helm of this you’re never allowed to forget you’re driving a rolling showcase of Ferrari’s F1-derived electronic wizardry. We’re talking latest-generation Side Slip Control, which integrates an E-Diff, F1-Traction Control and Ferrari Dynamic Enhancer (FDE) into one lateral-control symphony. This vehicle, like the old FF, has part-time four-wheel drive that quietly disengages the front axle once you’ve bypassed lower gears. Once up to speed, you’re back piloting a rear-wheel drive stallion.

In brief our time behind the wheel, the FDE system felt the standout. It reaches into the hydraulic brake pressure mid-corner and trims your line as it sees fit, correcting you before you register you even need correcting. Even more impressive is none of it feels synthetic in this two-tonne-plus family hauler. You simply marvel at how a semi-high-riding SUV can punish a mountain road so effectively. All with a wailing naturally aspirated V12 as your sonic backdrop.

THE VERDICT

Don’t let the svelte facade fool you, the Ferrari Amalfi is a thoroughbred Prancing Horse. Image: Ray Leathern

Forgive us, it is uncouth to discuss Rands and Cents when it comes to such one-of-a-kind items. However, the Ferrari Amalfi will set buyers back in the region of R6.15 million, give or take a few hundred thousand on extras. And the Purosangue FUV nearly double that at R11.7 million. Not that it’s a comparison, but the sleek and wantonly elegant Amalfi is the vehicle that really captured our imagination on the day. The twin-turbo punch is brutal off the line. And you lose nothing in the way of thrills as you chase speed all the way to the redline.



Much like the old FF, and perhaps oddly for a ‘utility vehicle’ aimed at everyday use, we see the appeal of Purosangue being more narrowly focused somehow. But full of thrilling, double-edged contradictions all the same. Nevertheless, at the end of the day, being given the chance to drive two thoroughbred Ferrari models for the day is something to be savored and celebrated.

World.title: Jabulile Ntimba murder: Ramaphosa vows action amid love-triangle probe
World.content:
Police and forensic teams work at an open field in Villa Liza, near Dawn Park in Boksburg, where Jabulile Ntimba’s body was found as investigators probe a possible relationship-related motive in her murder. Facebook/Nabeelah Shaik

Police are probing whether a relationship dispute, including a possible love triangle, led to the murder of Jabulile Ntimba in Boksburg.

Ntimba’s partially clothed body lay face down in an open area in Villa Liza near Dawn Park when authorities discovered her on Thursday, 17 September.

Deputy National Police Commissioner for Policing Lieutenant General Tebello Mosikili revealed on Monday that investigators had uncovered information pointing to a possible relationship-related motive.



The development gives police a clearer line of inquiry in Ntimba’s case as detectives continue investigating the deaths of women across Ekurhuleni.

Police probe possible relationship motive

Mosikili said investigators were examining whether a relationship dispute played a role in Ntimba’s murder, including what police have described as a possible love triangle.

However, she declined to reveal further details because the case has already entered the court process.

“We will leave it to the courts to unpack the evidence and, ultimately, the motive behind her killing,” Mosikili said.

Investigators are treating Ntimba’s murder separately from the other eight Ekurhuleni cases.

Police have also ruled out a possible serial-killer link in her death but continue examining whether any of the other cases share connections.



Three arrested over Ntimba’s murder

The Gauteng Murder and Robbery Unit arrested two women and a man over the weekend in connection with Ntimba’s killing.

The trio appeared in the Boksburg Magistrate’s Court on Monday.

Their arrests marked a significant breakthrough in one of the nine cases that have gripped Ekurhuleni over the past two months.

Acting National Police Commissioner Lieutenant General Puleng Dimpane said detectives were treating all nine investigations as priority cases.

Teams of detectives, forensic experts, fingerprint specialists and other policing units continue to follow evidence and leads in each investigation.

Authorities initially identified Ntimba incorrectly as 24-year-old Tebello Monamodi from Vosloorus.

Monamodi later returned home alive, and police subsequently confirmed Ntimba as the woman found dead in Villa Liza.

The deaths have sparked growing concern about women’s safety in Gauteng and intensified calls for authorities to act.

Police also widened their investigation after another young woman’s body turned up in Soweto over the weekend.

Authorities found the woman, believed to be in her 20s, wrapped in a duvet in a dam in Moroka on Sunday, 20 September.

Investigators have not established a link between the Soweto case and the deaths in Ekurhuleni.

Ramaphosa: GBV is a national crisis

In light of this, President Cyril Ramaphosa called on men to take greater responsibility for ending violence against women.

“And the message must also go to men. Men must continue respecting women, honouring women,” Ramaphosa said in Johannesburg on Monday.

“The women of our country are the builders of the nation. They carry this nation on their shoulders.”

Ramaphosa said the abuse and killing of women represented “a real blight against all of us”.

“Gender-based violence is not only a problem for women. It’s a national crisis, and we need to be treating it with exactly that.”

He said government would strengthen its response as fear over violence against women continued to grow.

More money, resources and technology

Ramaphosa pledged additional state resources to tackle gender-based violence and femicide.

“We’re going to even be deploying more money, more resources, more technology to ensure that we deal with the fear that women are now subjected to,” he said.

He said government’s Inter-Ministerial Committee on Gender-Based Violence and Femicide would introduce further initiatives.

Ramaphosa also said government had a duty to protect women.

“Government is there to protect the people of South Africa, plain and simple. So when things like these happen, government should take responsibility.”

He said women deserved to walk South Africa’s streets without fearing men.

“We are taking this very seriously. I have always spoken against gender-based violence throughout the years, and will continue spreading the message that as the government of South Africa we are committed to protecting women.

“We are committed to ensuring that the lives of our women are safe.”

World.title: Abdeslam Ouaddou rewrites Orlando Pirates PSL history books
World.content:
Abdeslam Ouaddou has made Orlando Pirates history after extending the club’s remarkable unbeaten run in the Betway Premiership. Image: CAF website

Abdeslam Ouaddou has made Orlando Pirates history after extending the club’s remarkable unbeaten run in the Betway Premiership.

The Soweto giant’s head coach has now overseen 20 consecutive league matches without defeat, becoming the first coach in the club’s PSL history to achieve the feat.

Orlando Pirates’ unbeaten run stretches back to February 2026, with Ouaddou’s side recording 15 wins and five draws during the remarkable sequence.



The achievement moves Ouaddou clear of some of the club’s most successful coaches when it comes to extended unbeaten league runs.

Abdeslam Ouaddou breaks Orlando Pirates record

Ouaddou’s 20-match unbeaten run is now the longest in Orlando Pirates’ PSL history.

The previous record was held by Dutch coach Ruud Krol, who guided Orlando Pirates through a 19-match unbeaten league run in 2009.



Ted Dumitru and Kosta Papic are next on the list, having each overseen 17-match unbeaten league runs.

The top four longest unbeaten league runs at Orlando Pirates are:

20 – Abdeslam Ouaddou

19 – Ruud Krol (2009)

17 – Ted Dumitru (1999)

17 – Kosta Papic (2005)

Ouaddou’s record comes during an impressive period for the Buccaneers, who have established themselves as one of the leading forces in South African football.



The unbeaten sequence has also strengthened Orlando Pirates’ away credentials, with the club continuing to avoid defeat on the road.

The achievement adds another notable milestone to Ouaddou’s tenure and comes as the Buccaneers continue their push at the top end of the Betway Premiership.

Standings

Following their 2-0 win over Marumo Gallants on Sunday, the Buccaneers are now second in the standings with 19 points, one point behind log leaders Mamelodi Sundowns, but will a game in hand.



Due to the upcoming FIFA international break, Orlando Pirates’ next Betway Premiership match is only scheduled for Sunday, 18 October at the Orlando Amstel Arena against TS Galaxy.

Kick-off is at 18:00.

World.title: Missing in Nepal | Search for Terricia Govender moves to Tibet
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - After their search in Nepal yielded no results, the family of 33-year-old Terricia Govender is turning its attention to neighbouring Tibet.

Govender is among thousands of people still missing after devastating floods hit Nepal 28 days ago.

Flooding and landslides along the Nepal-Tibet border unleashed water and debris, killing hundreds and leaving thousands missing.

Govender was part of a pilgrimage group that, according to her friend Sashin Maharaj, allegedly never made it across the border into Nepal.

Govender’s mother, Linda, and Maharaj travelled to Nepal to seek assistance in the search for her.

Maharaj says they engaged with immigration officials and reviewed information provided during their search.

World.title: New Zealanders pick endangered black robin as Bird of the Year
World.content:
WELLINGTON - A record number of New Zealanders turned out at the polls this month, not for national elections but to vote for their Bird of the Year -- the critically endangered black robin.

The diminutive native lives on the remote Chatham Islands, 800 kilometres off the South Island's east coast.

In the 1980s only five of the birds remained, including one reproductive female. Now, there are about 350 black robins living in two protected populations.

The black robin topped the pecking order ahead of the famed flightless parrot, the kakapo, and the native karearea falcon, which came in second and third.

The annual Bird of the Year competition is run by independent conservation organisation Forest and Bird, and has been the subject of significant controversy in the past decade.

In 2019 there were accusations of Russian interference after hundreds of votes were registered from IP addresses in the country.

Forest and Bird deemed most of the votes were legitimate, and said it did not affect the victory of the hoiho, or yellow-eyed penguin.

In 2023 the puteketeke won the title after receiving the celebrity backing of Last Week Tonight comedian John Oliver, who urged his viewers to vote for the lake dweller.

Forest and Bird's Rebecca Hatch said voter numbers had soared this year, but not due to foreign interference.

"This year has seen record numbers of votes with 105,000 people choosing their favourite," Hatch said.

"New Zealanders have really shown up for nature. Roughly one in every 50 Kiwis voted," she said, referring to the country's people and not the native, flightless birds.

The black robin received more than 26,000 votes.

The Chatham Islands Landscape Restoration Trust ran the campaign for the black robin and is seeking to create a third habitat for the birds to expand their biodiversity.

World.title: Malaysia's 'elephant whisperer' fights to save Borneo's endangered giants
World.content:
SUKAU - Deep in Malaysia's Borneo jungle, wild shouts fill the air as a Bornean elephant is darted and her angry herd rallies to protect her.

The downed elephant is one of only around 1,000 Bornean elephants left in the wild, and the team that darted her is working to protect the endangered species by minimising growing conflict between the animals and local communities.

Once the herd has been chased off, conservationist Farina Othman and her team move in to attach a tracking collar to the animal.

The collar allows them to alert villagers if the elephant strays too near.

World.title: Bridgeman wins PGA Biltmore title with sizzling 61
World.content:
ASHEVILLE - Jacob Bridgeman birdied four of the last six holes on Sunday to hold off fellow American Ben James and win the PGA Biltmore Championship by two strokes.

Bridgeman fired a 10-under-par 61 with eight birdies and an eagle to finish 72 holes on 26-under 258 at The Cliffs at Walnut Cove in Asheville, North Carolina.

"When I was over the putt I knew where it was going to go. It was just magical," Bridgeman said. "I just made so many putts."

It was the second career PGA crown for 26-year-old Bridgeman, a native of nearby Inman, South Carolina, playing in front of family and friends who captured his first in February at Riviera.

"It was super cool," Bridgeman said. "It was awesome. I felt like I had all my family and friends cheering for me.

"It was pretty neat. It's super cool to perform in front of them. I'm super pumped."

Bridgeman will play for the United States in next week's Presidents Cup at Medinah.

"It's a dream come true," he said. "Being able to play as a team for the United States, I'm really pumped."

James matched his career-low PGA round with a 61 to finish second on 260, one stroke ahead of fellow Americans Ricky Castillo and Neal Shipley with Americans J.T. Poston and Jackson Koivun sharing fifth on 263.

Bridgeman birdied three of the first four holes, added a 10-foot eagle putt at the par-five eighth and sank a five-foot birdie putt at the 10th for a one-stroke lead.

James grabbed a share of the lead with a birdie at the par-five 15th but Bridgeman answered with a birdie from just outside five feet at the 13th.

When James made a 26-foot birdie putt at 16, Bridgeman responded with a 12-foot birdie putt at the par-three 14th to regain the solo lead.

Bridgeman tapped in for birdie at 15 and James did the same at the par-five 17th to stay on his heels.

A closing par by James left him needing a mistake by Bridgeman in the last two holes but the leader added a tap-in birdie at 17 and parred 18 to secure the $900,000 top prize.

Poston began the day 11 strokes adrift but fired a 60 and nearly had the PGA's 17th sub-60 round.

"It was pretty special," Poston said. "It was just cool to have a round like that."

Poston, this year's Memorial winner who grew up in nearby Hickory, was in the first group off the back nine after a fog delay and reached 18 needing a birdie for 59. He parred after missing a putt from just beyond 26 feet.

"I was rolling it really well," Poston said. "Just wanted to give myself a putt and I did that. Hit a good putt and it just missed."

The $5-million event marked the start of the PGA Tour's fall series, which offers golfers who missed the playoffs a chance to improve their status for next year's tour.

World.title: LIVE | Joe 'Ferrari' Sibanyoni faces Madlanga Commission again
World.content:
PRETORIA - Businessman and taxi boss Joe “Ferrari” Sibanyoni is expected to return to the Madlanga Commission on Monday.

During his first appearance before the commission, Sibanyoni was questioned about the taxi industry and alleged links to the so-called Big Five cartel.

Sibanyoni and three co-accused face charges of extortion and money laundering in connection with allegations of a protection racket in Mpumalanga.

He and his co-accused are currently out on bail.

World.title: KZN premier raises alarm over serial rapists
World.content:
DURBAN - KwaZulu-Natal is dealing with a growing number of suspected serial rapists.

That's according to the province's premier, Thami Ntuli.

Police arrested a 36-year-old man linked to the rape of 14 women in KZN and Gauteng.

Ntuli says authorities are working to link other cases and bring serial offenders to court.

"It's unfortunate that we've learned that there are a number of serial rapists in the province of KwaZulu-Natal," he said.

World.title: US has deported 25,000 to third countries under secretive deals: report
World.content:
WASHINGTON - The United States has deported more than 25,000 people under secretive agreements with 35 countries to take migrants with no ties to those nations, according to an investigation published on Monday.

Since US President Donald Trump took office in January 2025, Washington has been signing deals with developing countries to take migrants who cannot legally be sent home.

The investigation by Forbidden Stories found the administration has earmarked $410-million to be paid directly to the receiving countries, or to UN agencies to facilitate the returns.

At least 25,447 people had already been deported to third countries by 31 August 2026, according to data compiled by Forbidden Stories with a consortium of international journalists.

The vast majority -- around 20,000 -- were sent to Mexico, but the rest were dispersed to 27 other countries across Latin America, Africa, and the Pacific, and agreements have been finalised with seven more.

The deals vary, including over which nationalities can be deported and whether people with criminal records can be accepted.

An AFP investigation earlier this year found Washington is using visa bans and restrictions on African countries to strong-arm them into accepting deportees.

Lawyers told AFP that deportees were being thrown into a "legal black hole", held without charge in countries where they have no ties and few if any rights.

Forbidden Stories said 49 of Africa's 54 countries had been approached about accepting third-country deportees.

A little-known State Department division called the Office of Remigration, created in May 2025, has handled most of the negotiations and payments, according to Forbidden Stories.

The office is headed by Christian Jove Ehrhardt, a 41-year-old diplomat who previously worked as a security officer.

The report details his visits to Cameroon, which signed a memorandum of understanding with the US in December on accepting deportees. A week later, it also signed a five-year health assistance programme worth nearly $400-million.

The following month, the State Department said it would provide a further $30-million to the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) in Cameroon to "facilitate the voluntary return of refugees and combat illegal immigration."

The first plane carrying deportees arrived in Cameroon on January 14.

- Payments -

Other agreements have involved direct payments to governments.

Palau, a small Pacific island nation with a population of under 18,000, signed an agreement in December 2025 to accept up to 75 third-country nationals in return for $7.5 million.

However, only three people have so far been sent under the agreement.

In Eswatini, 32 people have arrived since July 2025 out of a possible 160 under an agreement worth more than $5-million. It has accepted deportees with criminal records, the investigation found.

Of the $410-million planned for the agreements, internal State Department records showed that $81-million was earmarked for signatory governments.

The rest was intended for aid organisations, including more than $178-million for the UN's International Organisation for Migration, and $123-million for UNHCR.

The agencies have faced criticism over their involvement, although UNHCR told Forbidden Stories that it was not party to the bilateral agreements and that US funding was being used in line with its mandate to strengthen asylum systems.

An IOM spokesperson told Forbidden Stories that the agency's decisions to accept funding rested "on a single question: whether our engagement will improve the lives of the migrants affected. In these instances, we believe strongly it does."

World.title: Devi | African Pro | 20 September 2026
World.content:
In a country where millions are desperate for work, a job offer can feel like a lifeline.

So, when Dudu Radebe promised to build the “Amazon of Africa”, nearly 100 people signed offer letters and got to work — many using their own money, data and equipment to help build African Pro Supply Chain Solutions.

But when payday arrived, their salaries did not. Instead came delays, broken promises and, eventually, termination letters.

When the Devi Show confronts the woman behind the business, forget an apology — Dudu turns our cameras into a call for investors.

World.title: Families given 21 days to claim 443 Shakahola victims' bodies
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCI detectives after exhuming bodies in Shakahola Forest, Kilifi County. [File, Standard]

The Kilifi County Government has given the families of victims of the Shakahola massacre 21 days to identify and collect the 443 bodies preserved at the Malindi Sub County Hospital for burial by December 2026.

Kilifi County Executive Committee Member in charge of Health Peter Mwarogo said that investigations by the Directorate of Criminal Investigations had been completed, allowing the county to begin the process of interring the remains of the unclaimed bodies.

Mwarogo who spoke during a visit by the Joint Senate Committees on Health and Public Investments and Special Funds at the Malindi Sub County Hospital on Monday, said that the County Government might be compelled to seek a court order to dispose of the unclaimed bodies.

“The Directorate of Criminal Investigations officers have concluded investigations on the bodies and we have embalmed the 443 bodies which are at the Malindi Sub County Hospital Mortuary. We have been given permission for the burial of the bodies,” said Mwarogo.

Mwarogo told the joint committees led by Nominated Senators Mariam Omar and Betty Syengo that the 443 bodies would be buried in a manner that allows them to be identified in future, with the DCI expected to guide the process.

The Kilifi County Government had identified land near the Shakahola Forest, where the unclaimed remains will be interred in a manner that they can be identified even several years later if somebody comes to identify the burial site of their relatives.

The proclamation by the Kilifi County Government comes more than three years after discovery of mass graves in Shakahola, where hundreds of suspected followers of controversial preacher Paul Mackenzie died after being subjected to extreme starvation and other forms of abuse.

“Only 14 out of the 443 bodies currently held at the Malindi Sub County Hospital have so far been identified by relatives through DNA matching, some families had been traced but declined to collect the remains because of the stigma associated with the tragedy,” said Mwarogo.

The County Health Executive told Senators that the Directorate of Criminal Investigation retained records of the DNA matching and identification process for purposes of the ongoing legal proceedings.

Mwarogo said that the County Governnment had published a Gazette notice giving relatives 21 days to come forward. If the period expires without the bodies being claimed and that the county will approach the courts for authority to inter the remains.

Elgeyo Marakwet Senator William Kisang asked the county to go beyond the gazette notice, stating that reliance on the gazette notice alone would leave some families unaware of the deadline leading to the burial of their relatives without their knowledge.

“It should be known that not all Kenyans would read the Gazette notice. The information should have been put in the various media channels by now because I know some people are still tracing the bodies of their relatives,” said Kisang.

The Elgeyo Marakwet Senator said that the county should consider wider publicity to ensure families who may still be searching for their relatives are informed before the remains are buried since the matter was very emotive and shocked the entire country.

Mwarogo told Senators that the 443 remains include complete bodies as well as body parts, which were recovered in difficult circumstances during the exhumation process with some already eaten by wild animals.

The County Health Executive told Senators that the remains have been stored in a container at the hospital after being released from the custody of investigators following completion of the forensic investigations.

“The Kilifi County Government wanted the matter concluded by December, partly because the temporary storage facility was taking up space needed by the hospital, that is why we informing the affected families to avail themselves or else we dispose the bodies,” said Mwarogo.

Mwarogo told Senators that the Shakahola remains are being held separately from the hospital's normal mortuary, which has a capacity for 25 bodies and currently has 22.

The County Health Executive told Senators that to ease the pressure, the county is constructing a new mortuary at the back of the hospital, which he said was about 90 per cent complete.

Mwarogo said that the new facility is expected to be operational in the coming months, allowing the county to relocate mortuary services away from the front of the facility.

World.title: Ndindi Nyoro, Kinangop MP clash over alleged threatening message
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro arrives at St Paul ACK church in Engineer Town for the service on September 20, 2026. [James Munyeki, Standard]

There was drama at St Paul ACK church in Engineer Town during service on Sunday after Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro clashed with Kinangop MP Zachary Kwenya Thuku over an alleged threatening message.

Thuku, who is allied to the Kenya Kwanza government led by President William Ruto, is said to have warned Nyoro against attending the service.

"Yesterday, I received a message from the MP for Kinangop, Kwenya Thuku, warning me not to attend the church service. If I am lying, let him come here and read the message he sent me," Nyoro said.

He challenged the Kinangop MP to read the message aloud to the congregation.

"If anything happens to me today, Kenyans will judge whoever will be responsible," said Nyoro.

The Kiharu MP challenged Thuku to face him at a public rally at Engineer Trading Centre.

When he rose to speak, the Kinangop MP said he would not address the matter in church.

Instead, he said this was a political issue that the leaders would resolve.

"Let us solve this matter amicably. We are all brothers in this political journey," he said amid cheers from the congregation.

Recently, Nyoro added his voice to the growing political realignment in Mt Kenya, openly acknowledging the political tightrope he now walks as he distances himself from his former allies in the ruling party.

In a candid interview, he admitted that his previous close ties with President William Ruto and the Kenya Kwanza administration have left him vulnerable to suspicion from both sides of the political divide but insisted his decision to abandon the ruling party, United Democratic Alliance (UDA) was deliberate, difficult, and necessary.

World.title: Ruto leaves for New York ahead of UN General Assembly
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Ruto leaves for New York ahead of 81st UN General Assembly. [PCS]

President William Ruto has departed for New York, United States, to attend the 81st United Nations General Assembly.

Ruto is expected to push Kenya’s investment agenda and advocate for increased financing for Africa.

According to a statement from State House, Ruto will use the global gathering to seek partnerships in energy, infrastructure, manufacturing, health, agriculture and technology.

He will also advance Kenya’s agenda on artificial intelligence and Africa’s participation in the global digital economy.

Ruto is expected to co-chair roundtables hosted by the Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) and Global Africa Business Initiative (GABI), alongside industrialist Aliko Dangote.

A key focus will be the planned Sh2.2 trillion East Africa Refinery in Lamu, which the government says will have a capacity of 700,000 barrels per day and create more than 60,000 jobs. The project is scheduled to break ground on September 30, 2026.

On artificial intelligence, Ruto and Finland President Alexander Stubb will co-lead the AI Middle Powers Initiative, which seeks to enable countries to pool computing resources, data and talent to build AI capabilities.

Kenya will also advance the Africa Development Bank-backed AI 10 billion initiative, which aims to mobilise up to 10 billion dollars by 2035 for investment in Africa’s artificial intelligence sector.

The President is further expected to sign a global declaration and roadmap on child online AI safety alongside leaders from Spain, the United Kingdom, Canada and Australia.

He will also launch an Africa Resilience Compact that will use artificial intelligence, satellite earth observation and predictive technologies to strengthen preparedness for El Niño and other climate shocks.

During his address to the UN General Assembly, Ruto is expected to champion an Africa-financing-Africa approach, calling for reforms and international guarantees to unlock more African capital for infrastructure and enterprise.

Ruto will also highlight Kenya’s National Infrastructure Fund, which the government says is designed to mobilise up to 40 billion dollars without adding to public debt.

On the sidelines of the General Assembly, the President is expected to hold meetings with heads of state and government, multilateral institutions and global corporations to discuss trade, investment and diplomatic cooperation.

He will also engage Kenyans living in the United States as the government advances a Diaspora Investment Platform intended to channel diaspora capital into productive investment in Kenya.

World.title: Inside Parliament's probe into secondary school fees and capitation
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Pangani Girls School Chief Principal Dr Millicent Odhiambo before the National Assembly Public Investments Committee on Governance and Education. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

Parliament’s scrutiny of the Auditor-General’s report on public secondary schools has exposed inconsistencies in capitation funding, student enrolment figures and the National Education Management Information System (NEMIS).

The National Assembly Public Investments Committee on Governance and Education has raised concerns over the impact of funding shortfalls on school operations and called for discussions with Ministry of Education officials to address the challenges.

The committee is also exploring whether the secondary school fee structure should be reviewed amid concerns that current capitation is insufficient to meet rising operational costs.

Chaired by Luanda MP Dick Maungu, the committee raised the concerns after the Auditor-General’s report showed that several national schools (C1) had sought additional fees from parents above the approved Sh53,000 annual amount, citing rising costs and inflation.

MPs also questioned disparities between capitation disbursements and the actual number of students in schools, which principals said had contributed to underfunding.

For the first time, administrators of national schools appeared before a parliamentary committee to respond to audit queries, with several saying discrepancies between NEMIS figures and actual school records had affected the amount of capitation they received.

Chief principals from Alliance High School, Alliance Girls, Bishop Gatimu Ngandu Girls, Limuru Girls, Mang’u High, Kenya High School, Pangani Girls and Kabare Girls, among others, said they had experienced difficulties validating learner data on NEMIS.

They said capitation received by their schools did not cover all students, with principals reporting that they receive less than the Sh22,244 expected per learner annually. The amount, they said, averages about Sh15,000.

Schools defend additional fees

During the committee’s examination of Alliance High School’s audit report, the Auditor-General flagged the irregular increase in school fees, including Sh17.6 million collected from parents.

“The school charged fees of Sh68,554 whereas the fees as per the Ministry’s guideline is Sh53,554 and the school thus raised fees by Sh15,000 per student annually contrary to Regulation 44 of Basic Education Regulation 2015, which states that no public school or institution shall issue alternative fee structure other than that approved by the Cabinet Secretary,” the auditor read. ‎Alliance High School's Principal David Kamau before the National Assembly Public Investments Committee on Governance and Education. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

Alliance High School Chief Principal David Kamau admitted that the school had sought alternative funding but said the initiative came from parents.

He said the approved Sh53,000 fee was insufficient to sustain the school’s budget amid rising costs and expectations of maintaining the institution’s standards.

“We have a certain lifestyle we have to maintain and that is why parents came in – in fact it was their idea – and asked us to maintain that. They came in and suggested they can do a budget support so that we maintain the same standards. For us, to acquire the results, we have to do a lot of activities to make sure we give a holistic education associated with the school over the years,” he explained.

“Parents approve that at an Annual General Meeting and we write to the Ministry but that letter of authority has never been granted. We have followed the process to the letter in terms of seeking approval for extra levies from parents,” he added.

The audit also flagged fee arrears in almost all the schools, with Alliance High School reporting arrears amounting to Sh36 million.

Kenya High School Chief Principal Rev Edith Koech was also required to respond to an audit query over unapproved fees under the parents’ association support programme, through which parents were charged Sh25,000 above the set amount per student without approval from the county education board.

Koech said the school had written to the Ministry seeking approval and, although it did not expressly receive authorisation at the time, it had since obtained it.

She said additional funds were approved during annual general meetings, where two budgets were presented — one based on Ministry guidelines and another reflecting what parents felt should be covered.

“Kenya High has its standards, for instance we have tea three times a day and they eat githeri once, they will burn the school if we change,” Koech explained.

Kiminini MP Kakai Bisau said the issue of additional levies had emerged in many schools, with principals arguing that the funds were necessary for students’ wellbeing.

“Looks like this issue is conflicting the law yet public participation is conducted among parents of respective schools. This is something we need guidance on and embedded in policy,” he said.

Other MPs questioned what happens to students from poor backgrounds who cannot afford the additional charges.

Lungalunga MP Chiforomondo Munga said principals had been entrusted with following the law, which states that public schools should not issue alternative fee structures without approval.

“I was a parent of Alliance but all said and done, you have done contrary to the law because approvals must come from the CS and I can assure you there is nobody who will approve that because they know they will be breaking the law and will be held accountable,” he said.

He said the situation presented a dilemma because schools were expected to maintain certain standards while operating within existing regulations.

Embakasi West MP Mark Mwenje said the issue of additional fees had existed for years, noting that he had paid about Sh40,000 while he was an Alliance High School student about two decades ago.

“We just need to sit down with the Ministry because it is becoming obvious that this money is no longer sufficient but we need to inform the principal that whenever such things are happening, there should be concurrence of the Principal Secretary but when we meet with the CS that issue should come out because we can no longer bury our heads in the sand,” Mwenje said.

Igembe Central MP Daniel Karitho described the issue as a “tricky” one, given rising inflation and the need to comply with the law.

“We cannot allow parents from any institution to just sit down and agree because there are those who are voiceless. This is an issue that needs to be discussed even in the House on the fees structure and if there is something that needs to be done, even on the basic regulation so that we can have a level,” Karitho said.

Alliance principal, however, maintained that the school’s process was transparent, with parents being provided with budget documents during annual general meetings and informed why additional funds were required.

“We tell the parents that is their decision to make and if they want to stick to the Sh53,000 but what we can offer as a school will reduce. I can assure we are conscious of the needy and we do not send anyone away because of the fees, either for statutory or additional,” he explained.

Kenya High echoed similar sentiments, saying additional contributions were based on public participation among parents and that no child was sent home over fees. The school also has endowment funds, it said.

NEMIS discrepancies

In another case, MPs questioned how Limuru Girls High School received an additional Sh785,946 in capitation after discrepancies emerged between its student enrolment records and figures captured in NEMIS.

The committee noted variances in Limuru Girls’ records and those of other national schools for the financial years 2020/2021 to 2024/2025.

The Auditor-General’s report for the year ended June 2024 showed that NEMIS recorded 2,099 students at the school in September 2023, 2,300 in January 2024 and 2,354 in May 2024.

However, records presented by the school showed enrolment of 2,062 students in September 2023 and 2,253 students in both January and May 2024.

The difference resulted in Sh785,946 in excess funding, raising concerns over whether the variance affected service delivery in other schools that did not receive capitation and made it difficult to confirm value for money.

Limuru Girls Chief Principal Susan Kariuki acknowledged the discrepancies but attributed them to differences between physical enrolment records and learner information captured in NEMIS.

“The difference arose from variations between the school’s physical enrolment records and the learner information captured in NEMIS at the respective reporting periods. The school did not intentionally provide inflated enrolment figures,” Kariuki said.

“So, because you are given more money, where do you take it?” Maungu posed.

Kariuki, however, said the school had not received the full amount of capitation due per learner and therefore did not consider itself overfunded in the ordinary sense. She said the Government was expected to provide Sh22,244 per learner but the school had been receiving about Sh15,000.

Narok Woman Representative Rebecca Tonkei questioned how Limuru Girls received higher funding for learners who were not captured in NEMIS, noting that other schools appearing before the committee had complained of underfunding caused by incomplete NEMIS records.

Maungu questioned the reliability of NEMIS, saying a system used to determine public funding should be predictable, consistent and dependable.

“This is not a good system. A good system should be predictable, consistent and dependable. But this system gives some people less and others more, sometimes the data is missing,” Maungu noted.

Starehe Girls raises fresh questions

Starehe Girls presented a different case that the committee said contained several grey areas after it emerged that 70 per cent of the school’s 776 learners are fully sponsored while the remaining 30 per cent are self-sponsored.

The school explained that all learners receive about Sh16,000 in Government capitation. For the 70 per cent, their upkeep is sourced through the board of trustees, while self-sponsored learners cover their own costs.

“Being a C1 school, by law it should pay Sh53,000. Instead, some are paying Sh150,000 meaning Sh96,000 extra to take care of the vulnerable. On this other side, you are saying they have a sponsor who take care...are you seeing the kind of confusion because they are already sponsored?” posed Maungu.

Despite the school’s unique funding arrangement, the committee said Starehe Girls remained a public institution and should therefore be audited.

The committee noted that not all financial years had been covered in the audit, unlike other C1 schools, and directed the institution to present all relevant documents for review.

Meanwhile, Mang’u High School surprised the committee when its administration said the school also faced challenges posed by snakes and hyenas that sometimes invade the institution.

World.title: Ruto faults Uhuru for undermining his government
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto join traditional dancers in Homa Bay on September 17, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has renewed his public criticism of former President Uhuru Kenyatta, accusing his predecessor of undermining the government and urging him to withdraw from active political mobilisation.

Ruto said he had supported Uhuru throughout their political partnership and expected reciprocal support when he sought the presidency.

“I stood by you through four elections; I stood by you, helped you, took care of you, and worked for you.”

Ruto claimed the two had discussed an arrangement in which each would serve as president for ten years. He accused Uhuru of failing to honour that understanding, saying:

“When the time came for you to help me, after you said ‘ten years for you, ten years for me,’ not even for a single day did you support me.”

Ruto also appealed to Uhuru to respect the position of former President and withdraw from political activities that he said were aimed at destabilising his administration.

“A former president! Surely, my brother, you are lowering the dignity of the office of the former president. You are a retired president respect your office, go and relax. Let us plan for this country of ours, Kenya,” Ruto said.

Ruto made the remarks on Thursday, September 17, 2026, in Sindo, Homa Bay County, as he concluded a four-day development tour of Nyanza.

The tour covered Kisumu, Siaya, Migori and Homa Bay and focused largely on roads, markets, housing, water and other development projects. The Star+1

The latest confrontation adds another chapter to the complicated political relationship between the two leaders.

Ruto served as Uhuru's deputy from 2013 to 2022, after the two politicians formed a political alliance that won the 2013 and 2017 presidential elections.

Contemporary accounts describe their original arrangement as involving support for Kenyatta for two terms, followed by support for Ruto's presidential ambitions. The Washington Post

The President nevertheless acknowledged Uhuru's democratic right to oppose his government but urged the former president to respect the office he once held.

“You are running schemes to sabotage the government. You are a retired president respect your office, go and relax. Let us plan for this country of ours, Kenya,” he said.

His criticism centred instead on what he described as continued political mobilisation against his administration.

He said his administration had stabilised the economy and pointed to investments in education, housing, markets and infrastructure. During the Homa Bay leg alone, the government highlighted a Sh3.5 billion plan for 21 modern markets.

World.title: Five killed as bandits ambush police search team in Isiolo
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Five people, including two police officers killed by bandits at the troubled grazing field of Gotu in Isiolo County on Wednesday.

The victims are a senior police officer, a police constable who was the driver of the vehicle that was ambushed by bandits, a livestock farmer and two National Police Reservists (NPR). The police officers were attached to an Anti-Stock Theft Unit (ASTU) located near Gotu trading centre.

The victims were part of a search team that was looking for an elderly man who reportedly went missing within the Gotu area and was last seen around Madho Gurba Huka, a grazing area in Chari Ward in Merti sub-county.

Isiolo County Police Commander Isaac Sang said the mentally challenged man from Barambate sub-location, Kulamawe location was reported missing a day ago.

The Isiolo camel keeper, reported to be related to the man who went missing, had requested police to search for him.

The mission turned tragic when the group was ambushed by armed bandits, killing all five on the spot.

The incident took place near the junction of Lososia-Merti road and Gotu-Merti route.

Mr Sang said the bodies of the officers and other victims were removed to Isiolo County Teaching and Referral Hospital awaiting postmortem.

"A reinforcement (of security personnel) had been sent to the area which includes an armoured vehicle to pursue the attackers," said the police chief.

The police boss called for calm and cooperation from the residents while police pursue the suspects.

He said that investigation into the incident had commenced.

On Wednesday afternoon, a gunfight was reported between police reservists and the bandits on the western bank of the river.

"The reservists in the area pursued the attackers minutes after reports of the killings that led to an exchange of gunfire. We are told an unknown number of people have been injured," said a herdsman from Gotu who sought anonymity for security reasons.

A source from Isiolo County and Teaching and Referral Hospital revealed that two ambulances had been sent to Gotu to attend to the injured persons.

Gotu, along with Kom in Merti sub-county is a bandit hotspot in Isiolo that is attributed to competition over scarce pasture by rival herders from Isiolo, Samburu East and parts of Marsabit with local leaders calling for eviction of pastoralists from outside the County. Several people have been killed in the two locations since last year and hundreds of livestock stolen.

On August 1, two people were killed in the Garse Dabata area in Gotu and nearly 700 goats and sheep were stolen. Nearly all the stolen animals were recovered in operation undertaken by a multi-agency security team stationed in various locations along the Isiolo-Meru border.

Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen on two occasions called for an operation in parts of Isiolo, Laikipia, Samburu and Meru Counties that had experienced frequent cases of banditry and rustling.

However, leaders fault the CS for failure to take decisive action on insecurity that keeps on recurring in parts of Isiolo and Meru Counties. The leaders including Governor Abdi Guyo want herders from outside Isiolo who are in Kom and Gotu areas to be evicted.

World.title: Muthaiga Golf Club restores access after KFS standoff
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Muthaiga Golf Club has restored access to a section of its course that was temporarily taken over by the Kenya Forest Service (KFS), hours after the agency moved into the area, claiming it forms part of Karura Forest.

The disruption affected the Front Nine, covering Holes Two to Nine, before the club’s board intervened to restore normal operations.

In a statement issued Tuesday, Muthaiga Golf Club Chairman Dennis Mwirigi said the board had taken the necessary steps to facilitate the resumption of activities after the temporary disruption.

“We are pleased to confirm that access to the affected part of the course has been restored and members may proceed with their scheduled activities as usual,” Mwirigi said.

He said the board remained committed to protecting the club’s interests, assets and members while addressing the matter through the appropriate channels.

The development follows an earlier communication to members informing them that KFS had taken over access to the affected section, claiming it was part of Karura Forest.

The club had initially said the Front Nine would not be accessible until further notice as it sought to resolve the matter. The driving range and parking areas were not affected.

The incident sparked criticism over the manner in which KFS handled the dispute, with Prof Karanja, Chairperson of Friends of Karura Forest, urging the agency to pursue dialogue and legal channels.

Prof Karanja said KFS should have first engaged the club’s management and clearly explained its claim over the disputed land instead of deploying dogs, guns and heavy security.

“If they don't agree that it was your land, go to court. The court will determine,” he said.

He questioned whether KFS had adequately demonstrated that the disputed section was forest land or explained how it was allegedly acquired by Muthaiga Golf Club.

“They should have come publicly and said, look, Muthaiga, that area and that area belong to the forest,” Prof Karanja said.

He said KFS should identify the specific portion of land it claims belongs to the forest and explain the basis of its claim before taking further action.

Prof Karanja argued that the dispute should be resolved through established legal procedures rather than force. “Trees are not protected by guns,” he said.

He described the deployment of armed personnel as the wrong way of resolving a land dispute and called for engagement between KFS and the golf club.

Prof Karanja also warned that actions by government agencies could have wider implications for the administration of President William Ruto, saying confrontational conduct could lead members of the public to associate such actions directly with the government.

“When government departments behave like this, everybody now starts thinking, oh, it's Ruto's whatever,” he said.

He further recalled a previous dispute involving Friends of Karura Forest, where he said armed personnel were deployed and the group removed from an area before senior government officials intervened.

According to Prof Karanja, officials from the Treasury and forestry departments eventually intervened and encouraged dialogue to resolve the matter.

He urged KFS to adopt a similar approach in the Muthaiga dispute, saying the agency and the club should present their respective claims and seek a court determination if they cannot agree.

For now, the restoration of access means members can resume their scheduled activities, while the underlying dispute over the contested section remains subject to further engagement between KFS and the club.

World.title: Juja couple's surprise blessing of five babies
World.content:
Mercy Kanini, 28, from Juja, Kiambu County, gave birth to five children at Thika Level Five Hospital. [Gitau Wanyoike, Standard]

A couple from Juja, Kiambu County, is celebrating the unexpected arrival of five babies after scans during pregnancy showed they were expecting quadruplets.

Mercy Kanini, 28, delivered four girls and a boy through normal delivery at Thika Level Five Hospital, in a rare case believed to be among only a handful of quintuplet births recorded in Kenya.

World.title: Ruling pro-Putin party set to win Russia’s tightly controlled wartime parliamentary election
World.content:
The United Russia party is easily on track to win Sunday’s tightly controlled Russian parliamentary elections, with President Vladimir Putin once again set to cement his dominance over domestic politics.

Final election results will not be tallied before September 25, but according to initial data from the Central Election Commission the United Russia party – which backs Putin – is in the lead with 57.8% of votes and 95% of the ballots processed.

The vote came as Kyiv launching one of its largest attacks against Moscow overnight into Sunday, the final day of the three-day election. More than 1,900 drones were launched, killing at least three people and damaging a major oil refinery.

Although the result of the election was not in doubt, voter participation could be seen as a test of support for the war in Ukraine.

The commission said that overall turnout across Russia topped 59%, a new record high for parliamentary election.

If confirmed, the result will get United Russia 355 of the 450 seats in the Duma, the lower house of the Russian parliament. That is the highest number of seats the party has ever secured and 31 more than it got in the last election in 2021 – before Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine – United Russia took 324

Putin is not a member of the party, although he served as its leader between 2008 and 2012.

As the sitting president, Putin was not on the ballot. He is not up for election until 2030, having won the most recent presidential election in 2024 with just under 88.5% of the vote.

No real opposition

Meaningful opposition is effectively nonexistent in Russia, with critics either barred, in jail or exiled abroad. According to the independent human rights monitor OVD-Info, more than 2,000 people are currently in prison for political reasons.

Russia’s only registered anti-war party, Yabloko – “Apple” in Russian – was briefly allowed to take part before being barred by the Supreme Court last month from the federal party-lists election.

Some individual Yabloko candidates were allowed to run in single-seat local districts, even though the Supreme Court banned the party’s main national list. But these candidates faced significant restrictions and pressures. Two of the party’s deputy leaders were recently imprisoned on charges related to their anti-war stances and social media posts. No Yabloko candidates were elected, according to the preliminary results announced by the commission.

Yabloko said on Saturday that one of its election observers “lost consciousness” while being detained at a polling station in St. Petersburg. It said numerous other Yabloko observers were barred from polling stations elsewhere.

The outcome of the election is likely to be used by the Kremlin to claim a stronger mandate, saying it illustrates Russians’ support for Putin and what the Kremlin calls its “special military operation” in Ukraine.

Ahead of the vote, Putin signaled in a televised speech to the nation that the election results will show Russians are united behind the army.

“Your choice and determination will show once again that millions of people are backing our fighters and that we stand together, united by shared values, our historical memory, love for our Motherland,” Putin said.

Rather than the actual results, observers will likely look at turnout as an indicator of how Russians are feeling about the war and Russia’s political trajectory.

Electronic voting questions

Polls closed on Sunday after three days of voting across Russia’s 11 time zones and at Russian embassies and consulates abroad.

People living in areas of Ukraine that are currently occupied by Russia were also asked to vote, with new constituencies added for Moscow-controlled parts of Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions.

Related article MOSCOW, RUSSIA – SEPTEMBER 2: A billboard advertising the upcoming parliamentary elections is seen in Moscow, Russia, on September 2, 2026. Parliamentary elections in Russia are scheduled to take place from September 18 to 20, 2026. (Photo by Natalia Kolesnikova/Anadolu via Getty Images) Natalia Kolesnikova/Anadolu/Getty Images Empty podiums, prizes for e-voting, no opposition: Russians head to the polls amid intensifying war in Ukraine 7 min read

Ukraine rejected the elections taking place in its territory, calling them a “farce.”

The European Union condemned Russia for holding what it called “sham elections” in the occupied territories and said it would sanction those who facilitated them.

“The so-called Duma elections marked another major setback for Russian democracy. Their outcome was never in doubt. The Kremlin silenced dissent, barred the only registered party that opposed its war in Ukraine, and shut out international election monitors,” the EU’s foreign representative Kaja Kallas said in a statement.

Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Norway and the UK issued a joint statement condemning the voting in occupied Ukraine, saying it breached Ukraine’s sovereignty.

As the elections unfolded, Russia continued to attack its neighbor. According to Kyiv, Moscow fired hundreds of drones and several missiles against Ukrainian cities over the election period.

People vote in Russia’s parliamentary election as a Russian serviceman secures a polling station in Donetsk, Russian-controlled Ukraine, on September 18. Stringer/AFP/Getty Images

After debuting the option during the last election in 2021, online and electronic voting was widely available – and encouraged – this time around. Moscow went as far as offering its residents incentives in the form of points for prizes, if they chose to vote electronically instead of casting a paper ballot.

Some voters in Moscow told the independent Russian news outlet SotaVision they weren’t issued paper ballots because of “malfunctions” and were encouraged to vote via an electronic terminal instead. “They did this on purpose, the b****rds,” one voter told SotaVision.

Critics have long been suspicious of the Kremlin’s introduction of electronic voting because they argue it’s less transparent. Russian authorities reject criticism of their electoral processes and insist elections are held in accordance with the law.

Putin himself opted to vote online, with the Kremlin releasing a video showing him navigating the online system and casting his vote.

Russian state news agency TASS reported outages and malfunctions of the electronic voting system in Moscow on Friday into Saturday, quoting Central Election Commission chair Ella Pamfilova as saying this was due to a “very large-scale and intense” attack.

During the elections, more than 3,000 waves of Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks on election infrastructure were recorded, according to Pamfilova.

In 10 regions, 74 buildings housing election commissions were damaged or destroyed during the voting days, Pamfilova said.

The remote electronic voting system was attacked 135 times, Rostelecom’s networks 420 times, and electronic government infrastructure nearly 2,000 times, the commission said.

World.title: Is Germany’s leader Friedrich Merz doomed as far right wins again?
World.content:
Berlin — “It is a disaster.”

Those were the words of a forlorn-looking German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Sunday evening as he addressed his party in the seconds after regional elections handed his center-right Christian Democrats (CDU) their second and third electoral drubbings in a month.

The elections in the north-eastern region of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and the city of Berlin not only reopen the barely healed wounds from the Saxony-Anhalt election on September 6, but have plunged the party to new depths of unpopularity.

Voters are abandoning the CDU –– the party of Angela Merkel and Konrad Adenauer –– in their droves, for the far-right, pro-Russia and anti-migration Alternative for Germany (AfD).

The AfD has once again demonstrated it is a major political force in this country.

On Sunday, Merz ruled out stepping down, saying Germany requires “courage, steadfastness and patience. I will demonstrate these qualities as Chairman of the CDU and, above all, as Chancellor of our country.”

Before Sunday speculation was rife about Merz’s survival. In the aftermath, he is now fighting for his political life.

In Mecklenberg-Vorpommern, the CDU’s prospects of making it into the parliament are hanging by a thread. Needing 5 percent to reach the threshold, they currently sit at 4.9 percent on projections.

The party’s previous worst regional election performance in 75 years was 9 percent in Bremen in 1951.

The AfD is projected to win the election with 38.3 percent of the vote, in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, although it fell far short of a majority. In Berlin it came in third, but saw a 7 percent increase in its vote share.

AfD co-leader Tino Chrupalla and lead candidate Leif-Erik Holm react to preliminary results in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania state elections, in Schwerin, Germany. Sean Gallup/Getty Images AfD party top candidate Berlin Kristin Brinker and AfD co-leader Alice Weidel react to the first exit poll results on public television in Berlin on September 20. Ralf Hirschberger/AFP/Getty Images

The CDU was the incumbent party in the German capital but has lost its grip on power there to the far-left Die Linke party, which is projected to come out on top. The CDU fell into second place.

Sunday’s results, coupled with the trouncing in Saxony-Anhalt earlier this month, heap misery on an already beleaguered Merz. A situation that, some believe, means only one outcome is possible –– a ‘chancellor-swap.”

“This is the worst possible result for Merz and the CDU,” Jana Puglierin, head of the European Council on Foreign Relations’ Berlin office, told CNN as the results were announced.

She said she saw no viable option for Merz to continue to lead the government, adding: “He has definitely lost control over his own party, and he has lost authority big time… and there is no way to reinstall it.”

Following the AfD’s election victory in Saxony-Anhalt, the party’s co-leader, Alice Weidel, declared there would be national elections in Germany before the end of the year. She doubled down on Sunday, saying “the CDU cannot continue with Friedrich Merz, with a weak chancellor.”

With two more elections going against the CDU, and Merz’s popularity plunging, that assessment seems less speculative.

“It’s not like Merz can just throw in the towel, nor does he want to,” Sudha David-Wilp, vice-president and senior fellow at the German Marshall Fund, a think tank, told CNN. “He’s still hanging on, but he’s not out of the woods yet.”

Any such upheaval would have reverberations around Europe. Germany, the EU’s most populous and economically powerful nation, has long stood as a rock of political stability and is a key backer of Ukraine as it fights Russia.

Tanking poll numbers

The Christian Democrats have long been the dominant political force in Germany. Of the 10 chancellors since World War II, the party has held the post six times – including a mammoth 16 years under the Angela Merkel.

An opinion poll from September encapsulates Merz’s woes. Levels of dissatisfaction across the country are eye-wateringly bad. Only 13 percent of Germans are happy with the job he is doing, according to a poll for ARD public television released earlier this month.

David-Wilp told CNN that AfD victories in the elections had been “baked” into the CDU’s political calculus, but the magnitudes of the outcomes were worse than expected.

“There is a feeling in the CDU that something has to happen in order to change the dynamic, because the AfD is on the march and threatening the very existence of the CDU,” she said.

A person casts his ballot in Berlin state elections on September 20, in Berlin, Germany. Michele Tantussi/Getty Images

Whilst the regions that make up the former East Germany are AfD strongholds, Merz’s problem lies in the party’s rise in popularity across the country. In two other state elections this year the AfD doubled its percentage share of the vote, while winning neither.

Nationally, too, opinion polling suggests the AfD would be Germany’s biggest political party were a snap general election to be held now.

Merz arrived in office in May last year promising to halve the AfD’s vote share –– so far the opposite has been true.

Turmoil in Germany

Such was the pressure on the chancellor last week that the other CDU state premiers felt it necessary to rally around him. They issued a joint statement Wednesday saying public support comes from “listening” and “political action” not “through personnel debates,” but failed to mention him by name.

Replacing a chancellor mid-term is not uncommon, but a removal under these circumstances is. It would also make Merz the shortest-serving chancellor since reunification. His conservatives and their grand coalition partner, the Social Democratic Party (SPD), would have to agree on his successor, no easy feat.

For David-Wilp, replacing Merz would “really leave a crisis of leadership when everybody is looking to Berlin for it.”

The members of the Bundesrat, the upper house of the German parliament, sit in session on June 12, in Berlin. Michael Kappeler/picture-alliance/dpa/AP

Puglierin said that Merz’s ascension to power had been accompanied by hope across Europe that he would restore stability after the disastrous previous coalition led by Olaf Scholz, and would “keep the club together” at a time when the United States under President Donald Trump was ripping up the “Pax Americana” that had underpinned international relations since World War II.

Those hopes could end in disappointment, Puglierin said, “because the country is looking inward… We are struggling with our political system that is no longer functioning the way it has done since the Federal Republic was founded in 1949.”

Merz’s problems – some his own, others not

Merz’s issues began before he even formally had the keys to the chancellery.

It took him two attempts to be officially confirmed as chancellor, an unprecedented scenario. Then he reneged on an election promise not to increase Germany’s borrowing, by unlocking half a trillion dollars of spending for defense and infrastructure.

Puglierin said personal characteristics –– poor communication skills, impulsiveness and a lack of emotional control –– “have put people off him.”

In April, Merz made questionable remarks about Trump’s war in Iran. The chancellor said the US president was being “humiliated” by Iran in efforts to end the war.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz reacts as he gives a statement after the exit polls of the Berlin and Mecklenburg Western Pomerania state elections were announced. Christian Mang/Reuters US President Donald Trump speaks in the Oval Office of the White House in Washington, DC, on August 10. Jim Watson/AFP/Getty Images

The comments drew the ire of the president, and upended the charm offensive by Berlin toward the White House. Before Merz’s comments, one official had remarked to CNN that they were pleased to have remained one of the few allies who had not been lashed by the sharp-tongue of the US president.

Yet there is also little denying that factors outside of Merz’s control have combined to create roadblocks to progress.

“The geopolitical backdrop of challenges that Germany is facing –– the war against Ukraine, inflation in Germany and energy costs –– all mean the economic model has been overturned in Germany,” said David-Wilp.

“Merz was never a beloved figure, or the first choice to be chancellor,” she added, but outside factors and his “inability to communicate has created a crisis for Berlin.”

Merz may still be saved by the lack of an obvious successor as chancellor and the dire situation his removal would leave the government in.

Neither member of Germany’s two-party coalition government wants it to collapse, said Puglierin, given polling numbers are not in their favor. A new coalition would likely mean a return to a three-party government, a formula which failed spectacularly in recent memory under Olaf Scholz. A repeat of that “won’t solve Merz’s problem(s),” said Puglierin.

The other challenge lies in finding a competent candidate who is ready to take the reins. The name on many people’s lips is that of the 51-year-old governor of North Rhine-Westphalia, Hendrik Wüst.

“He is viewed as the heir apparent in the CDU. He is not a seasoned politician, but he may have to stand up earlier than anticipated,” said David-Wilp.

Wüst, formerly a lawyer, has led North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany’s most populous state and an industrial powerhouse, since 2021. One of the few remaining regions where the CDU has a stable majority, it has its own state election in early 2027.

Hendrik Wüst, governor of North Rhine-Westphalia, speaks onstage during the 2026 Digital X at Rheinauhafen on September 8, in Cologne, Germany. Thomas Lohnes/Getty Images

Wüst “would be eager to be chancellor one day, but not under these circumstances,” said Puglierin, adding that the election in North Rhine-Westphalia is crucial for the CDU.

“To change horses (in the election) on such short notice is a risky game,” Puglierin said, but added that she believes Wüst is the only candidate the SPD would agree to work with were Merz to be out of the picture.

Wüst, though, has said he wants to focus on winning the state election, and that Merz has his full support.

World.title: What to expect at the UN General Assembly, the biggest event in world diplomacy
World.content:
Fear not, world leaders — the UN’s notorious escalator has been fixed in time for diplomacy’s biggest event of the year.

That’s what outgoing United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres told reporters at his last press conference ahead of this week’s General Assembly, which will bring hundreds of diplomats and world leaders to the UN’s New York headquarters.

Last year, US President Donald Trump accused the UN of sabotage after the escalator he was riding malfunctioned while he made his way to the General Assembly Hall. “I can tell you that we took additional measures in order to make sure that whoever goes around does not interact negatively with the escalator,” Guterres said Wednesday.
