World.title: Russia imposes temporary movement restrictions on other side of Estonian border
World.content:
Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) has imposed temporary movement restrictions in two districts across the border from Estonia.

The border directorate of the FSB's St. Petersburg and Leningrad Oblast branch said measures would be in place in border areas of the Slantsy and Kingisepp districts from September 16–26 to "prevent violations of border and migration regulations" and "protect aquatic biological resources."

During this period, small vessels are prohibited from traveling on the section of the Narva River between the Bolshaya Cheryomukha and Kryusha (Krivasoo) rivers.

A nighttime movement ban has also been imposed outside populated areas within a five-kilometer-wide strip along the state border in the Kingisepp and Slantsy districts. Hunting and carrying firearms are also prohibited in the area.

Andris Viltsin, Estonia's border representative on the Estonian-Russian border, said the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) had previously been aware that Russia would impose movement restrictions for a certain period in several areas bordering Estonia. The Russian border authorities did not themselves notify the PPA of the restrictions in advance.

The PPA does not consider such restrictions extraordinary.

Viltsin explained that the Russian side has occasionally imposed various movement restrictions as a preventive measure or in connection with exercises and that even under normal circumstances, movement in Russia's border zone is more restricted than elsewhere.

"Russia has significantly stricter measures in place on a daily basis within a five-kilometer-wide area adjoining the border than Estonia does. For example, not everyone can enter Ivangorod (Jaanilinn — ed.) — you need an invitation to do so," Viltsin said.

"The Russian side has imposed measures like these from time to time depending on the situation. It is not routine, but neither is it anything particularly extraordinary," he added.

According to the PPA representative, the Russian side may have been seeking to prevent incidents during the elections.

It recently emerged that Russia is fortifying the bank of the Narva River, although there is no clear link between the two developments.

"It is clearly apparent that the Russian side is increasingly devoting measures and resources to guarding the border in order to make that work more effective and ensure access for a response if necessary. I think this needs to be viewed in the broader context, together with everything else. They are increasing their readiness and capabilities and it seems they have no shortage of resources on that side," Viltsin said.

Russia held sham elections over the weekend, which were won, as expected, by the ruling United Russia party. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has previously warned that Russia plans to mobilize around 300,000 people following the State Duma elections in September.

Interior Minister Igor Taro (Eesti 200) did not rule out the possibility that the restrictions could be connected to a planned mobilization.

"There have certainly been various theories about another round of forced mobilization, and considering the difficulties they have faced in staging their election spectacle, how severe the restrictions they have had to impose have been in order to produce the result they wanted and the kinds of actions they have had to contend with, naturally nothing can be ruled out," he said.

The interior minister noted that not many Russians want to go to war and die and said the measure could be connected to an attempt to prevent citizens from fleeing the country. He also stressed that evading military service is not in itself grounds for receiving international protection.

"Russia itself knows why it is implementing these measures," Taro said. "In any case, they have always had a special regime for the border zone; the area has never simply been freely accessible."

World.title: Estonian households throw away €117 million worth of food a year
World.content:
Estonian households generated nearly 69,200 metric tons of food waste in 2025, with avoidable waste accounting for almost 38 percent of the total, Delfi reports based a new study.

Estonian households generated nearly 69,200 metric tons of food waste in 2025 of which 25,337 metric tons or nearly 38 percent was food loss — food thrown away that could still have been eaten if it had been consumed sooner or stored or handled differently.

This means that nearly 18.5 kilograms of food per person was thrown away over the course of the year. The value of food wasted in households totaled €116.7 million. For an average two-person household, this amounts to a loss of approximately €179 a year, according to a new study on food waste.

Vegetables, prepared foods, dairy products and baked goods accounted for the largest share of food wasted in households. The main causes of avoidable food loss were insufficient planning, a lack of awareness of what was in the refrigerator and preparing excessively large quantities of food.

At the same time, food waste has declined compared with previous years.

Estonia's entire food supply chain generated approximately 139,000 metric tons of food waste in both 2024 and 2025, which amounts to an average of 102 kilograms per person per year. Households accounted for nearly half of the total, but significant amounts of waste were also generated by the food industry, retail, food service and agriculture.

The study was commissioned by the Environmental Investment Center and the Ministry of Climate with support from the EU Cohesion Fund and conducted by Levellab and Roheline Rada.

World.title: Outgoing president awards office chief €11,000 bonus
World.content:
President Alar Karis awarded Krista Zibo, director of the Office of the President, an €11,200 bonus for strong job performance in 2026. Zibo has also received a large bonus in the past.

On January 29 this year, Karis issued a directive setting Zibo's base salary at €6,010 per month. Her previous salary was €5,500. When she took up the post on September 2, 2024, it was €5,000.

On November 24, 2025, Karis decided to award Zibo a bonus of €10,500 for strong job performance.

Zibo also spent nearly two years as director of the Office of the President on a fixed-term arrangement, having been temporarily transferred from the Government Office. As of July 1 this year, just a few months before the new president takes office, she has held the position on a permanent basis.

When ERR asked in early September why the arrangement had only now been changed, the Office of the President said Zibo was needed to ensure stable management and day-to-day operations through the end of Karis' term and during the presidential transition. The response did not explain why this could not have been done under the temporary transfer arrangement.

13 layoffs in 2 years

As of early September, Zibo had laid off 13 employees from the Office of the President over the previous two years. Two employees had their last day at work just about a month before President-elect Ülle Madise was due to take office. One had worked at the office for 26 years and the other for nearly 19 years.

Zibo said the changes were necessary to save money and improve the organization of work.

However, eight people have been hired by the Office of the President over the past two years. The office attributed the new hires to changes in job roles and work processes.

President-elect Ülle Madise has offered the position of director of the Office of the President to longtime senior executive Paavo Nõgene.

World.title: The Estonian helping put a small US town on the art map
World.content:
One of the United States' major art events this summer was the inaugural Medina Art Triennial in New York state where nearly 100 works of art were installed across a town roughly the size of Elva. Karin Laansoo served as the triennial's artistic director.

The broader goal of the event is to revitalize the area around the historic Erie Canal. Completed in 1825, the nearly 600-kilometer-long canal was considered a major feat of engineering at the time. Today, many communities along the canal have fallen into obscurity.

Medina Art Triennial artistic director Karin Laansoo told ETV cultural affairs program "OP" that one of America's largest energy companies was behind the triennial, seeing contemporary art as a way to support the regional economy and attract more tourists.

"Looking back now, we really had no idea just how big, ambitious and complicated this project would become. Nobody knew anything about Medina. I'm not just talking about international artists; I'm talking about people who live an hour away from here. Of the 39 artists, only one had ever been to Medina before because he was born in Buffalo and visited Medina with his father as a child," she said.

Medina's heyday came around the turn of the 20th century. Its prosperity was driven by local sandstone whose quarrying and transportation employed thousands of people, many of them immigrants from Europe.

History teacher Todd Bensley said the triennial is helping put Medina back on the map.

"We have two larger cities around us, Rochester and Buffalo. People may not think about us that much, but when they come here, they enjoy what they see. It's a typical 19th-century American town. Our Main Street is well preserved. There are a lot of great businesses in town. We just have to get people here and they'll fall in love with Medina," he said.

Two buildings more than a century old were restored for the Medina Art Triennial. A former hotel was turned into a visitor center, while an elementary school building that had stood empty for the past 30 years became the main exhibition venue. The latter also features scented works by Estonian artist Kärt Ojavee that seek to convey what Medina smells like.

"Kärt came to Medina last year on a research visit. She spent a week here trying to find the scent that best characterizes Medina. She settled on a particular variety of apple called Honeycrisp. Kärt began extracting different scents from apple blossoms, soil and seeds," Laansoo said.

Susanna Rosenstock, deputy director of the Toronto Biennial of Art, praised the triennial organizers' initiative and said the team had done incredible work.

"It was a major undertaking to bring the exhibits to a small town that perhaps doesn't have the infrastructure needed for exhibitions that would be readily available in a big city. Even though I've only been here for one day, the people and volunteers were very excited and grateful to have this exhibition here. It's unique to Medina and showcases the town's distinctive character. It's different from any other exhibition because it allows you to see the place where you live differently from the way you do in everyday life," she said.

Laansoo said feedback from visitors has been overwhelmingly positive. "The words people use are phenomenal, incredible, life-changing, inspiring," she said, adding that critics have also praised the initiative. "Critics said this new initiative is among the 20 most important art events of 2026."

World.title: Iraq urges US firms to accelerate project implementation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Finance Minister Faleh Sari urged on Saturday US companies operating in the oil and energy sectors to accelerate the implementation of their projects in the country.

Sari remarks took place during his meeting in Baghdad with US Charge d’Affaires to Iraq Steven Fagin to review bilateral relations and discuss approaches to enhance economic and financial cooperation.

The Iraqi minister’s call aims to boost foreign investment and support the development of vital sectors.

Sari said in a statement that Iraq’s relations with other countries are driven by the country’s supreme interests. He emphasized the Iraqi government’s commitment to maintaining a balanced relationship with the United States based on shared interests.

Fagin described the Iraqi government delegation’s visit to Washington last July as highly successful. He emphasized the importance of building upon the visit’s outcomes to strengthen cooperation between the United States and Iraq.

On July 13, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi paid a five-day visit to the United States, where he signed 48 agreements and memoranda of understanding, as well as announced cooperation between Iraqi and US organizations.

The agreements totaled over $60 billion and encompassed industries such as oil, energy, industry, technology, telecommunications, finance, agriculture, education, and health.

World.title: Spain coach De la Fuente gets new deal after World Cup success
World.content:
Madrid – Spain’s World Cup-winning coach Luis de la Fuente is to sign a new contract keeping him in the role until 2032, the Spanish football federation (RFEF) announced on Monday.

“Luis de la Fuente will extend his contract through the next two European Championships, in 2028 and 2032, as well as the 2030 World Cup,” the RFEF said in a statement.

The 65-year-old, who took charge of Spain in 2022 after replacing Luis Enrique, has since led the national team to World Cup success, Euro 2024 glory and the 2023 UEFA Nations League title.

De la Fuente spent a decade working with Spain’s youth teams before stepping up to the senior role.

“We’re talking about the most successful head coach in the history of the national team, and after fourteen years with us, this is something Luis de la Fuente deserves, a long-term future at the RFEF,” said Rafael Louzan, chair of the Spanish FA’s board of directors.

Spain travel to England on September 26 in their first game since lifting the World Cup in July before hosting Croatia three days later in Seville, to start their Nations League campaign.

They return home to play the Czech Republic in Oviedo on October 3 and end the international window by heading to Croatia three days later.

World.title: EU proposes energy rating for data centres
World.content:
Brussels – Data centres in Europe will be rated on energy and water consumption under an EU proposal put forward Monday to pre-empt possible public discontent as the bloc pushes to boost its computing capacity.

The European Union is aiming to triple its data centre capacity over the next seven years as it plays catch up with the United States and China on artificial intelligence.

“Tripling our data centre capacity cannot mean tripling the pressure on our grids, our water and our energy bills,” said European Commission vice president for clean transition Teresa Ribera.

Data centre construction has sparked backlash across the United States, with local residents often complaining about the power-hungry engines of AI driving up electricity costs — a hot political issue ahead of November’s midterm elections.

The EU said its scheme would provide the public with information about the water and energy consumption of sites with capacity above 500 kW, which already have to report key performance metrics to the EU.

Similarly to that already in use for home appliances, the rating will rank data centres on a coloured scale where A/Green is the most efficient and G/red the least efficient, according to a commission presentation.

To encourage good practices, the score will take into account data centres’ contribution to the grid, such as the reuse of waste heat and the addition of clean energy generation capacities, the commission said.

“Efficient, flexible, powered by additional clean energy and reusing waste heat, this is how data centres become an asset for (the) EU’s energy transition,” Ribera added.

Data centres are yet to become a flashpoint political issue in the 27-nation EU, as the bloc lags well behind the United States on AI development.

The slower growth is in part due to already-high-energy costs, which weigh on European businesses and families alike.

But the International Energy Agency estimates the fast expanding sector will account for more than three percent of overall electricity demand in the EU by 2030.

“To ensure that the digital transformation truly works for our society, we must address the growing energy demand of data centres,” said the EU’s energy commissioner Dan Jorgensen.

“Understanding their energy and resource consumption is the essential first step towards integrating them sustainably into our energy system.”

The labels will be automatically generated by the EU based on companies’ reporting and will be accessible on an EU database, with the first expected to appear in 2027, Brussels said.

The commission said it was also looking into setting minimum performance standards for data centres.

World.title: Putin’s party secures record score in Russia election
World.content:
Moscow – Vladimir Putin’s United Russia party won a record supermajority in the Duma, authorities announced Monday after a tightly controlled three-day election without parties critical of the Kremlin or the war in Ukraine.

Electoral chief Ella Pamfilova said preliminary results showed United Russia — which has dominated Russian politics for 25 years — won 355 of the Duma’s 450 seats.

The result handed Putin’s party an increased supermajority and beat its previous record of 343 seats. The supermajority means it can change the constitution, if it needs to.

The Kremlin said the result of the first parliamentary election since Moscow sent troops to Ukraine in 2022 showed Russians were united around Putin, who has been in power since New Year’s Eve 1999.

The conflict has killed hundreds of thousands, displaced millions and hit ordinary lives in Russia more than ever this year. Moscow has banned criticism of its military campaign and the only party that called for an end to the war was removed from the election.

“These indicators, of course, point to the highest level of consolidation within Russian society around the head of state,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told a briefing with journalists.

Elections under Putin are tightly controlled and few in Russia doubted United Russia would win.

Putin had encouraged Russians to vote in support of troops in Ukraine and Moscow also organised voting in occupied Ukraine.

Pamfilova said turnout was over 59 percent, thanking Russians for voting despite what she called “psychological pressure on Russia.”

Russia’s Ukraine campaign broke its ties with the West. Kyiv hit Moscow with its biggest drone attack of the war Sunday, the last day of voting, killing two people and setting an oil refinery ablaze.

“Despite the extreme situation, we were successful in ensuring the maximum security of these elections,” Pamfilova told a Moscow press conference, thanking security services for ensuring the vote went ahead.

– Fifth year of war –

The election result is expected to further tighten Putin’s grip on power.

Some fear a new military mobilisation in Russia. Putin has denied this is in the works, while Kyiv accuses Moscow of planning a callup in coming weeks.

Russia’s Communist party came second in the vote, winning 40 seats. The nationalist LDPR party took 25 seats and the New People party won 20.

The election took place amid the escalation of the Ukraine war in recent months, with no diplomatic solution in sight.

For the Kremlin, it served as a barometer on the mood of Russians towards the war.

In some regions, voting also took place for the heads of regions.

In Chechnya, Ramzan Kadyrov — known for ruling the Muslim-majority republic with an iron fist — won 99.85 percent of the vote, the electoral commission said.

Opposing Kadyrov is hugely dangerous in Chechnya, which is known for extra-judicial killings.

Putin’s political opponents are in exile, prison or dead — such as his main opponents Alexei Navalny who died in an Arctic prison in 2024.

The EU’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas dismissed Russia’s “so-called” election.

“The Kremlin silenced dissent, barred the only registered party that opposed its war in Ukraine, and shut out international election monitors. The veneer of democracy is all that remains in Russia,” Kallas said.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports hit 35% of shipments leaving Hormuz last week
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Data from Kpler, a leading data platform that tracks commodity flows and maritime shipping, indicates a decline in shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz over the past week, with the number of vessels traversing this vital waterway remaining low.

13 oil tankers departed the Strait of Hormuz during the week that started on September 13, carrying a total of approximately 34 million barrels of crude oil.

Saudi Arabia accounted for approximately half of the exports, while Iraq contributed 35 percent of the total crude oil shipments that left the Strait of Hormuz that week.

Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains significantly lower than pre-war levels; prior to the outbreak of the war on February 28, the vital waterway typically handled around 125 large commercial vessels daily.oil,

Over the weekend, 12 commodity vessels passed through the Strait of Hormuz, compared to 35 the previous weekend, amid ongoing tensions in the Gulf region and a disagreement between the United States and Iran.

Visible shipping traffic through the strait, which previously served as a conduit for one-fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas supplies, has decreased significantly. However, Middle Eastern producers continue to export oil on tankers with their transponders switched off.

World.title: Spanish PM says unregulated AI could be ‘devastating’
World.content:
Madrid – Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Monday joined a chorus of calls to regulate AI as safety fears around the technology escalate, warning of potentially “devastating” consequences.

The debate over the risks from artificial intelligence has intensified this month, with many of the industry’s leading lights voicing support for more cooperation, regulation and slower development of the technology.

Former employees of major AI companies have resigned warning of the technology’s risks, even pointing to an existential threat to humanity.

“If artificial intelligence is concentrated among a few companies and a handful of countries, its impact on shared prosperity, and therefore on the idea of democracy, will be very negative, if not devastating,” Sanchez told an AI-focused event in Madrid.

“We must act urgently, because unregulated, opaque artificial intelligence running wild… and in very few hands is the perfect recipe for disaster,” added the Socialist leader.

US President Donald Trump — with whom Sanchez has repeatedly clashed — has dismissed fears that AI could wipe out humanity and rejected calls to put greater controls around the fast-moving technology.

Sanchez, an outspoken critic of the power of big tech companies and their bosses, on Monday renewed his criticism of “techno-oligarchs” and urged international coordination on AI.

“Self-regulation does not work”, said Sanchez, calling for an AI “focused on well-being and collective prosperity that enables the building of fairer societies”.

He presented a 12-month plan aiming for “a new social contract for artificial intelligence” in Spain in cooperation with civil society.

This agreement would have to offer “security to people in the face of the changes in work and in life that this technology will entail”, he said.

In February, Sanchez announced a plan to ban social media for under-16s, sparking a spat with X owner Elon Musk and Telegram founder Pavel Durov.

His government has also asked the Spanish prosecutors to investigate X, Meta and TikTok for possible offences related to AI-generated child pornography.

World.title: Merz vows to keep ruling coalition together for ‘democratic future’ of Germany
World.content:
Berlin – Chancellor Friedrich Merz vowed Monday to keep his ruling coalition together for the sake of Germany’s “democratic future” after crushing defeats in two regional elections fuelled speculation about his future.

“We are determined to live up to the historic responsibilities our country is facing,” said Merz about the coalition between his centre-right CDU and the centre-left SPD.

“It is about nothing less, and nothing more, than the democratic future of our country.”

The SPD also vowed to remain in the coalition despite the centre-right party suffering heavy losses in Sunday’s votes, while hinting it would push for changes to planned reforms.

The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) came first in the northeastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, where the CDU crashed out of the local parliament after its worst ever election result since the party’s founding in 1945.

Merz described the result as a “heavy blow”, adding: “This election is a profound turning point. It is a dramatic, unprecedented result for the CDU in Germany.”

In the other vote, in the city-state of Berlin, the CDU was pushed into second place by the far-left Die Linke party while the AfD also made strong gains.

Despite calls for him to step down from the AfD after just 16 months in office, Merz repeated he would remain in office and seek to push through hard-fought economic and social welfare reforms.

“But we know that we owe people answers to their worries, to their fears,” he said.

Merz pushed back at criticism that his own low popularity ratings were behind the election defeats.

“The reasons for these election results go far beyond my own person,” he said.

“We are witnessing a profound transformation of the political party system in Germany as well as in many other countries around the world.”

World.title: Iraq launches 6th International Health Exhibition and Conference in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Health officially launched the Sixth Annual International Health Exhibition and Conference on Monday, September 21, 2026, establishing a collaborative platform to advance national medical capabilities, modernize hospital infrastructure, and stimulate domestic pharmaceutical and medical device manufacturing.

Speaking at a press briefing, Technical Deputy Minister of Health Hani Al-Oqabi announced that the international summit will take place from October 28 to October 31, 2026, at the Baghdad International Fairgrounds under the direct supervision and sponsorship of the Ministry of Health.

Al-Oqabi outlined the ministry’s operational strategy, emphasizing on-the-ground administrative oversight, institutional readiness, and direct engagement with hospital cadres to enhance clinical responsiveness and restore public trust in the state healthcare ecosystem.

Extending an official invitation to international, regional, and domestic medical enterprises, academic bodies, and healthcare organizations, the deputy minister highlighted that the four-day convention aims to facilitate cross-border technology transfer, introduce innovative healthcare solutions tailored to Iraq’s specific needs, and accelerate the localization of essential healthcare industries.

The summit announcement coincides with ongoing structural reforms within Iraq’s public health network, including the progressive expansion of the National Health Insurance scheme across additional governorates, improving centralized procurement lines for specialized pharmaceuticals, and fostering public-private healthcare partnerships.

Al-Oqabi stressed that the ministry’s strategic vision prioritizes clinical safety, patient-centered care standards, and bilateral institutional cooperation, anticipating that the upcoming Baghdad summit will yield actionable partnerships and open channels to integrate advanced medical technology into the nation’s medical facilities.

World.title: ‘PM Modi assured me’: OP Rajbhar’s claim on UP division revives decades-old debate
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh minister Om Prakash Rajbhar has claimed that Prime Minister

assured him that the state would be divided into four parts, reviving a nearly two-decade-old debate over dividing the country's most populous state.

Rajbhar, who heads

ally Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP), claimed that PM Modi told him Uttar Pradesh could be divided after the caste census.

âWe want to assure you regarding the 27% reservation. I spoke with the prime minister about this,â he told the audience at an SBSP programme in Deoria on Sunday.

âHe (PM Modi) said, âOm Prakash ji, your point is justified, but some people are opposing it.â I asked him how we could move forward, and he replied, âI will conduct a caste census, and once we have counted the castes, there will be no difficulty.â

The state will be divided into four parts. And on the day the Purvanchal is formed, if the chief minister is to be from any caste, then a Rajbharâs son will become the chief minister,â he added.

However, another UP minister and BJP ally, Sanjay Nishad, dismissed Rajbharâs remarks as âmisleadingâ, saying the Nishad Party was not in favour of a reorganisation.

âThere had been a demand to divide UP earlier, but now the state is progressing rapidly in all spheres.





Further, special development funds have been allocated for regions like Bundelkhand and Purvanchal that needed handholding,â Nishad told PTI.

Rajbhar has advocated the division of Uttar Pradesh in the past as well,

that the âstate can be developed only after it is divided into four parts.â

When Mayawati proposed carving out four states from UP

With the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections due in early 2027, Rajbharâs remarks have revived the long-running political debate over dividing the state.

Ahead of the 2012 UP assembly elections, then chief minister Mayawati revived the demand, with the state assembly passing a resolution to split Uttar Pradesh into Avadh Pradesh, Purvanchal, Bundelkhand and Paschim Pradesh.

In 2011, her government had sent a proposal to the Congress-led Centre seeking the creation of the four states.

Before that, in 2008, Mayawati had proposed dividing Uttar Pradesh into three parts.

Several parties, including the Rashtriya Lok Dal and Congress, have also backed demands for dividing the state at various points. There have additionally been calls for a separate Bundelkhand comprising parts of Uttar Pradesh and neighbouring Madhya Pradesh.

Uttar Pradesh was last divided in 2000, when the BJP-led central government carved out Uttarakhand, then known as Uttaranchal.

Why Uttar Pradesh matters

With a population of around 25 crore, Uttar Pradesh is Indiaâs most populous state.

If it were an independent country, its population would make it the fifth- or sixth-most populous country in the world.

Geographically, Uttar Pradesh is the fourth-largest state in India.

It sends 80 members to the 543-seat Lok Sabha, the highest representation of any state or Union territory. Its legislative assembly has 403 members.

Six prime ministers were born in Uttar Pradesh, while several others, including Narendra Modi, have represented the state in Parliament.

World.title: The 'rebel' hit by rebellion: How Mamata Banerjee's TMC journey has come full circle
World.content:
's political journey in West Bengal has come almost full circle.

In 1998, Mamata walked out of the Congress after years of differences with its leadership and formed the

. She believed the Congress was not doing enough to challenge the Left Front, which had been ruling West Bengal for decades.

28 years later, Didi, as she is fondly called, is now herself a step away from losing control of her party to a rebellion. Her

Congress has split, and rivals in the party, who once worked under her are now challenging her control. The Election Commission has temporarily frozen the party's original name and its well-known 'Jora Ghash Phul' (flowers and grass) symbol while it decides which faction has the ârealâ claim.

And what's more! In an interesting turn of events, Mamata is now desperately banking on the Congressâs support to survive the BJPâs political offensive against her in West Bengal.

The change comes at a difficult moment for her.

The BJP recently ended Trinamoolâs 15-year rule in West Bengal in May, crossing 200 seats and forming its first government in the state. Mamataâs party, which had been in power for 15 years, fell below 100 seats.

Mamata's troubles have only grown since then.

The defeat was followed by a rebellion within the

TMC

and finally a battle over who has the right to use the partyâs name and symbol.





For a leader who built her career as a rebel, Mamata is now facing a rebellion of her own.

Mamata on TMC symbol row

Congress: From bitter rival to 'sister party'

At the peak of her power-packed 15 years as chief minister of West Bengal, Mamata refused to acknowledge the presence of Congress in West Bengal. In fact, for Mamata, both the Congress and the Left were bitter political rivals and she would often accuse them of being the B-team of the BJP in the state. But that changed in the aftermath of her crushing defeat in May this year as the BJP swept the stateâs political landscape and formed its first government.

The shift in power dynamics was on display when Mamata announced support for the Congress candidate in the Nandigram bypoll to be held on October 6. "We are extending our support to Congress in Nandigram. We are doing this for the greater interest of the nation,â Mamata Banerjee announced. But what really surprised was her reference to the Congress as a ânatural allianceâ and a âsister partyâ. Words that would sound almost alien to those who have followed Mamataâs politics, especially the Congress leaders in the state.

While the Congress has strongly backed her fight against the Election Commission, with Rahul Gandhi leading the charge, the help is unlikely to transform into a greater alliance, at least for now. The West Bengal Congress unit, which was at the receiving end of Mamataâs political aggression for many years, is very clear and categorical that it does not want any alliance with her party.

Rahul Gandhi backs Mamata Banerjee

Vendetta politics

Since losing power, Mamata has repeatedly accused the BJP of targeting her and trying to weaken her party.

The irony is that Mamata herself faced similar accusations after she came to power in 2011, ending 34 years of Left rule. Both the Left and the Congress had accused the Trinamool of using political pressure and defections to weaken its rivals.

The circumstances may be different, but the roles have now reversed. What is happening today to her is what she did to her opponents in the past in West Bengal.

Mamata's beginning in politics

Mamata started her political career with the Congress in the 1970s.

The first glimpse of her aggressive political style was on display during Emergency days when she made headlines for her protest against Jay Prakash Narayan.

She quickly rose through the Congress ranks and, in 1984, emerged as the giant killer when she defeated veteran Communist politician Somnath Chatterjee, to win the Jadavpur parliamentary Constituency in West Bengal. She was also among the youngest MPs elected that year.

There has been no looking back since then. She lost in 1989, but came back strongly in 1991 from the Calcutta South constituency and retained the seat in 1996, 1998, 1999, 2004 and 2009 Lok Sabha elections.

From Congress activist and street fighter to TMC founder and three-term West Bengal chief minister

The protest politics and the birth of Trinamool Congress

Mamata's differences with the Congress grew through the 1990s. She believed the party was not aggressive enough in taking on the Left government in West Bengal.

Her politics was built around street protests and agitations against the Left government.

One of the most prominent moments of her political career came in 1993, as state Youth Congress chief, when she led a march to Writersâ Building demanding voter ID cards to prevent alleged electoral malpractice.

Police opened fire during the protest, killing 13 Congress workers. By 1997, her differences with the Congress leadership had reached a breaking point. In 1998, Mamata walked out and formed the Trinamool Congress.

Years later, the Singur and Nandigram movements turned that protest politics into a force strong enough to bring her to power for a good 15 years.

Nandigram challenge, once again

Nandigram has always had a special place in Mamata's political career. The land protests here in 2007 helped turn her into the strongest challenger to the Left. Four years later, she came to power.

But Nandigram also became one of her biggest electoral setbacks. In the 2021 assembly election, Mamata chose to contest from the seat against her former aide Suvendu Adhikari, who had joined the BJP.

Nandigram was Suvenduâs bastion and Mamata wanted to prove a point. That did not happen as she lost to Suvendu by around 2,000 votes. But her Trinamool Congress returned to power in the state with a thumping majority.

Five years later, in 2026, it was Suvenduâs turn to challenge Mamata in her bastion of Bhabanipur, while also contesting from Nandigram. Suvendu not just reinforced his dominance in Nandigram but also humiliated Mamata in Bhabanipur.

Suvendu retained Bhabanipur and vacated Nandigram, necessitating a bypoll. But this time around Mamata faced a setback even before the contest could begin. Her candidate for the October 6 bypoll in Nandigram withdrew from the contest after meeting chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, leaving Mamata without a candidate of her own. She then announced support for Congress candidate Milan Pradhan.

For Mamata, Nandigram has now seen almost every phase of her politics.

It helped her rise, handed her a personal defeat, and is now showing the challenges she faces after losing power.

The road ahead ...

For Mamata, the road ahead is not just about fighting the BJP. The former chief minister has a larger issue at hand at the moment. She has to hold her party together, fight for control of the Trinamool name and symbol, and rebuild her position as the main opposition force in Bengal.

Congress support could help her on some issues, especially at the national level, but a wider alliance in Bengal seems unlikely, at least for now.

Congress leaders in West Bengal remain wary of Mamata after years of on-and-off rivalry and large-scale defections from their party to the Trinamool under Mamataâs watch.

That leaves Mamata at the junction of perhaps the most difficult phase of her political career.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

She began as a Congress leader, broke away in rebellion, built a party of her own and eventually ruled Bengal for 15 years. Now, with rebels challenging that very party and she being forced to return to Congress for help, Mamata's journey has indeed come almost full circle.

The future and fate of the original Trinamool Congress is now in the hands of the Election Commission. Mamata will be keeping her fingers crossed. And rightly so. Precedents from recent past in Maharashtra would worry her. Sharad Pawar lost control of the Nationalist Congress Party and Uddhav Thackeray of Shiv Sena, after the ECI ruled in favour of rebels who had split the two parties. So, will Mamata be lucky, or will she now be left with a âfootball playerâ to try another round of âkhelaâ in West Bengal? Can Mamata once again fight adversity for a much-needed comeback? Well, we will have to wait and watch.

World.title: 'Deeply ashamed, Bihar in grips of gunda-raj': Tejashwi targets BJP govt over Jamui harassment case
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Bihar Assembly Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav on Monday condemned the alleged harassment of a boy and a girl in Jamui, describing the incident as "truly tragic" and expressing concern over the safety of women in the state.

"We are deeply ashamed. The government, however, seems to have lost all sense of shame or decency regarding such events," Yadav said, referring to the viral video of the incident.

While talking to the reporters he questioned the safety of girls in Bihar, alleging that incidents of atrocities against women were increasing across the state.

World.title: Nandigram bypoll: Congress candidate Milan Pradhan sent to judicial custody till October 5 in 2007 agitation case
World.content:
Congress nominee Milan Pradhan sent to judicial custody till October 5

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Congress' Nandigram bypoll nominee Milan Pradhan was on Monday remanded to judicial custody till October 5 in connection with a case registered at Khejuri Police Station 19 years ago, dealing a setback to his campaign for the October 6 assembly bypoll.Pradhan was sent to judicial custody by a Contai court in West Bengal's Purba Medinipur district, his counsel Ayan Bhattacharjee said. He added that the order would be challenged before the Calcutta high court.The development came two days after a Haldia court had remanded Pradhan to judicial custody till October 3, following his arrest on September 18 on multiple charges, including murder, linked to the 2007 Nandigram land agitation.The latest order effectively prevents Pradhan from campaigning during the final days of the bypoll campaign, which ends on October 4.The Nandigram seat was vacated by chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, who resigned in May and chose to retain Bhabanipur after defeating Mamata Banerjee in the assembly election held earlier this year.Meanwhile, Banerjee's decision to support Pradhan has marked a significant political shift between the Trinamool Congress and Congress in Bengal.Banerjee backed the Congress candidate after her faction's nominee, Sanchita Pradhan Dey, withdrew from the October 6 contest following a meeting with Adhikari in Kolkata.Announcing her support on September 18, Banerjee described Congress as a "sister party" and a "natural ally", saying the decision was taken in the larger interest of the country and to strengthen the INDIA bloc.Banerjee also said she wanted to send a message about the future of the opposition alliance beginning from Bengal.The move follows a series of political developments involving the TMC. The Election Commission had frozen the Trinamool Congress' traditional name and âJora Ghash Phulâ symbol amid an internal party dispute, assigning separate names and symbols to Banerjee's faction and its dissidents for the upcoming bypolls in Nandigram and Rejinagar.The Congress-TMC relationship has previously seen periods of cooperation. The parties contested the 2001 Bengal assembly election together and later joined hands in the 2009 Lok Sabha polls. In 2011, their alliance helped end the Left Front's 34-year rule in Bengal.

World.title: Ram Temple donations 'theft' case: SIT to file first chargesheet on or before September 25
World.content:
A four-member SIT is probing the alleged theft of donations

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court-appointed Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the alleged theft of donations at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya will file its first chargesheet in the case on or before September 25, a CJI-led bench was informed on Monday.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta told the bench that the chargesheet would have to be filed as the statutory 90-day period from the first arrest in the case would lapse soon.âNinety days from the date of the first arrest are going to be over on September 25, so we will have to file the chargesheet, otherwise, they (the accused) will get default bail,â Mehta said.The bench, comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, also perused a detailed status report submitted by the SIT in a sealed cover.Under Section 167(2) of the CrPC, an accused becomes entitled to statutory bail if the investigating agency fails to file a chargesheet in the trial court within the stipulated period of 60 or 90 days.The bench had earlier directed the probe team to complete its investigation expeditiously and take it to its logical conclusion. It had also asked the SIT to file a status report in a sealed cover on the progress of the probe into the alleged theft of donations.The Supreme court had taken note of the formation of a four-member SIT headed by IGP Kiran S to investigate the alleged embezzlement of donations and directed the Uttar Pradesh government to include a forensic auditor in the probe team.Observing that âremedial actions will have to be takenâ, the bench had said steps would be taken to âensure transparencyâ and directed the SIT to submit a status report.The court's directions came after allegations of irregularities surfaced in the management of donations at the Ram Temple. Several petitioners approached the Supreme Court seeking a CBI probe and a forensic audit of the temple trustâs finances.

NEW DELHI: The National Commission for Women (NCW) on Monday took suo motu cognizance of harassment and assault of a young woman and her male companion in Biharâs Jamui district, after a video of the incident surfaced on social media.NCW chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar wrote to Bihar director general of police, calling for the immediate registration of an FIR, identification and arrest of all those involved, and a time-bound and impartial investigation.The commission has specifically asked authorities to use the video footage to identify the alleged perpetrators and take action against them.The incident reportedly took place on the evening of September 19. World.title: 'Non-application of mind': Court sets aside order refusing probe in Sonia Gandhi electoral roll case
World.content:
Sonia Gandhi

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: A Delhi court on Monday allowed a revision plea challenging a magistrate's order refusing to probe the allegation that Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's name was included in the electoral roll in 1980, three years before she acquired Indian citizenship.Special Judge Vishal Gogne delivered the judgment two days after deferring it. He quashed the order as "non-speaking" or an order that does not explain the reasons behind a judge's conclusion."The impugned order suffers from a manifest error in law on account of non-compliance with Section 175(3) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), inter alia, not hearing the submissions of the police officer concerned and non-calling of a status report from the police station concerned," the Special Judge noted."The 'non-speaking' nature of the order was evident as the magistrate did not consider the twin options under law of directing the registration of an FIR or alternatively conducting proceedings under the BNSS, and instead of considering the core aspect of whether the complaint disclosed the commission of a cognisable offence, the magistrate digressed towards the issue of citizenship," he added.The court remanded the matter back to the magistrate to pass a reasoned order after hearing fresh arguments.The matter has been posted for further proceedings on September 29.In September last year, advocate Vikas Tripathi filed a plea in a Delhi magistrate's court seeking action against Sonia Gandhi, claiming her name appeared on the electoral rolls three years before she became an Indian citizen in 1983. The plea had sought a police investigation into what it terms a possible case of forgery.The application had pointed to documents suggesting Sonia Gandhi took Indian citizenship on April 30, 1983. Yet, her name allegedly appeared as a voter in the New Delhi constituency roll in 1980, was deleted in 1982, and re-entered in April 1983 after she formally became an Indian national.Tripathi's plea was dismissed on September 11, 2025, prompting him to approach a higher court.

World.title: Search on for three persons who killed man during drunken dispute in Old Washermenpet
World.content:
The police are on the lookout for three persons who murdered a 35-year-old man during a drunken dispute in Old Washermenpet on Monday.

A senior police official said that when S. Saravanan of Moolakothalam was drinking alcohol near the railway tracks near his house, another group, comprising Ajithkumar, Vasanth, and Sathish of Vyasarpadi, arrived and started drinking as well. A argument broke between Saravanan and the others. Ajithkumar and the others suddenly hit Saravanan with a beer bottle and then stabbed him. Saravanan was killed on the spot. The Washermenpet police sent the body to the Government Stanley Hospital for a post-mortem and are searching for the group.

World.title: Doctors’ body seeks reduction in Category-A PG medical fees in Telangana
World.content:
The Healthcare Reforms Doctors Association (HRDA) has urged the Telangana Admission and Fee Regulatory Committee (TAFRC) to reduce the tuition fee for postgraduate MD/MS courses under Category-A, or Competent Authority/ Convenor quota, in private medical colleges for the 2023-2026 block period.

In a representation submitted to the TAFRC chairman on Monday, HRDA president Karthik Nagula said Category-A postgraduate seats were allotted through the Competent Authority quota based on NEET-PG merit and, therefore, the fee for these seats should remain reasonable and affordable, particularly for students from middle-class and lower middle-class families.

The association cited an NMC office memorandum dated February 3, 2022, which states that the fee for 50% of seats in private medical colleges and deemed universities should be at par with the fee charged in government medical colleges of the respective State or Union Territory. The memorandum also provides that the benefit should first be extended to candidates admitted through the government quota and, where government quota seats constitute less than 50% of the sanctioned strength, to other candidates based on merit.

The association also compared the postgraduate fee issue with the existing undergraduate fee structure. It pointed out that the Category-A MBBS tuition fee is ₹60,000 a year while the Category-B fee in private medical colleges is approximately ₹11.55 lakh to ₹13 lakh a year. “The difference demonstrates that a lower fee could be maintained for merit-based Competent Authority seats while retaining a differential fee for other categories,” they said.

Citing NMC guidelines, the association said fee fixation should take into account actual operating costs, audited financial accounts and relevant expenditure, while adhering to the principle that medical education should be conducted on a not-for-profit basis.

World.title: Wadiyars’ Dasara: Golden throne installation on Oct. 5, Khas Durbar on Oct. 11
World.content:
The golden throne at the Mysuru Palace will be installed on October 5, ahead of the traditional Dasara celebrations of the erstwhile Mysuru royal family, while the Khas Durbar (private durbar) will be held by royal family scion and Mysuru-Kodagu MP Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar on October 11.

Announcing the schedule of palace rituals at a press conference on Monday, Pramoda Devi Wadiyar said the installation of the imperial golden throne would be held between 10 a.m. and 10.20 a.m., following the customary rituals.

The assembly of the throne in the palace durbar hall is an important ceremony conducted under the guidance of Ms. Wadiyar.

The Khas Durbar, coinciding with the commencement of Navarathri festivities, will begin at 11.45 a.m. on October 11, following pujas scheduled to commence at around 6 a.m.

The private durbar, a tradition dating back to the era of the Mysuru Wadiyars, is now largely representative in nature and is conducted only during Dasara. Access is restricted to a select audience. The tradition evokes the ceremonial practices of the erstwhile royal household while retaining its place in the palace’s annual Dasara observances.

The Khas Durbar will be held on the remaining days of the festivities in the evening as part of the traditional rituals.

Saraswathi Puja will be celebrated on October 16 at around 10.20 a.m., while Ayudha Puja at the Kalyana Mantapa inside the palace is scheduled for October 20 at 11.35 a.m., according to Ms. Wadiyar.

The royal family’s Vijayadashami celebrations, which conclude the Navarathri rituals, will be held on October 21, beginning at 8.15 a.m. Vajra Musti Kalaga, one of the highlights of the celebrations, will be held in the palace courtyard, followed by other traditional rituals and a procession within the palace premises.

The Mysuru Wadiyars have been observing Navarathri rituals for centuries, with the palace celebrations continuing to be an important part of the Dasara tradition.

World.title: A.P. Minister asks party leaders and cadre to strengthen grassroots coordination
World.content:
Minister of Roads and Buildings B.C. Janardhan Reddy on Monday (September 21, 2026) asked the party leaders and activists to work in coordination to strengthen the party at the grassroot level.

The Minister held a meeting with party leaders, activists, and ward/cluster in-charges at the party office in Koilkuntla. During the meeting, he discussed about strengthening the party, coordinating with the public at the grassroots level, and effectively disseminating information about government welfare and development programmes to the people.

Mr. Janardhan Reddy advised the cadre to work in coordination, identify public issues, and strive for their resolution. He instructed the leaders and activists to remain accessible to the public and create awareness about government welfare and development initiatives.

Meanwhile, a section of workers met the Minister and explained their grievances. They submitted a representation requesting the allocation of land to establish a dedicated Auto Nagar for workers. They explained that the establishment of an Auto Nagar would provide necessary facilities and enable them to carry out their trade effectively.

Mr. Janardhan Reddy listened attentively to the issues faced by the workers and stated that the matter of land allocation for the Auto Nagar would be examined. He assured them that he would consult with the officials concerned and take necessary steps.

World.title: Ernakulam Boat Jetty Water Metro terminal to be completed in a year
World.content:
The construction of the new Water Metro terminal near the Ernakulam Boat Jetty is expected to be completed in a year. The terminal, costing ₹32 crore, will be the second-largest in the Water Metro network after the High Court terminal, according to an official communication.

Once it becomes operational, direct services can be operated from the terminal to Mattancherry, Fort Kochi, Kumbalam, and Edakochi. The piling work commenced on September 8. The facility, which will be designed in the traditional Kerala architectural style, will have two floors and a total area of ​​18,000 square feet, according to the communication.

The first floor will be dedicated to commercial purposes. Piling work is being carried out round the clock. Two floating jetties are envisaged as part of the project, and one of them will be completed in the first phase. Charging points for boats and a fueling station will also be set up. The tender procedures for 15 new boats are under way.

Meanwhile, the tender process for the Edakochi and Varapuzha terminals is nearing completion. The estimated costs of the Edakochi and Varapuzha terminals are ₹20 crore and ₹16 crore, respectively, according to the communication.

World.title: Jewels, cash stolen from locked house in Singampunari
World.content:
About 30 sovereigns of gold jewellery and ₹1 lakh in cash were stolen from a locked house in Singampunari.

Police said J. Alamelu of Sandhiveeran Kudam area in Singampunari had been living with her two sons since the death of her husband. A few days ago, she had gone with her family to Periyakulam in Theni district.

When they returned home on Sunday night, they found the lock broken and the door open. On entering the house, they found that 30 sovereigns of jewellery and ₹1 lakh kept in a wardrobe had been stolen.

The Singampunari police have registered a case and are investigating.

World.title: Two injured as wild gaur hits scooter in Keralam’s Kasaragod
World.content:
A wild gaur that was crossing the road reportedly hit a scooter at Manjakal near Bovikanam in Kasaragod in Keralam in the early hours of Monday (September 21, 2026), seriously injuring two people.

The injured are C.M. Jithina, 22, a BSc Nursing student from Thankethadukka at Karivedagam and P. Amalraj, 24, of Alathumkadavu. Amalraj was riding the scooter at the time of the incident.

The two were thrown onto the road after their scooter reportedly collided with the animal. Jithina, who suffered injuries to her chest, was initially admitted to a hospital in Kasaragod. She was later shifted to a hospital in Mangaluru as her injuries were serious.

Amalraj, who also sustained serious injuries, is undergoing treatment at a private hospital in Cherkala.

Residents said the presence of wild gaurs has become frequent in the Manjakkal area for the past two years. However, there had been no reported incidents of wild gaurs attacking people.

They demanded urgent measures, including the construction of safety fencing, to control the movement of wild gaurs in the area.

World.title: Over 81,000 Ganesh idols immersed across Cyberabad in six days
World.content:
More than 81,000 Ganesh idols were immersed at designated locations across the Cyberabad Municipal Corporation (CMC) limits over the past six days, with civic authorities deploying sanitation, engineering, traffic and safety teams to manage the immersion process.

According to the consolidated immersion report, a total of 81,315 idols were immersed across 53 designated immersion points. Of these, 66,530 idols were below three feet in height, while 14,785 idols were above three feet.

Kukatpally Circle recorded the highest number of immersions with 23,501 idols, followed by Kompally with 11,526 and Serilingampally with 8,495. Jeedimetla recorded 7,145 immersions, followed by Miyapur with 6,256, Chintal with 4,408, Ameenpur with 4,274, Allwyn Colony with 4,015 and Patancheru with 3,661.

While 3,257 immersions were recorded in Nizampet, it was 3,024 in Narsingi, 2,828 in Madhapur, 1,846 in Dundigal and 1,079 in Medchal.

The CMC officials said field-level coordination was being maintained continuously at all 53 immersion points to ensure sanitation, waste clearance, access and other civic arrangements. Special attention was given for prompt removal of pooja material and other immersion-related waste to maintain cleanliness around the designated locations.

CMC Commissioner G. Srijana directed officials and field teams to maintain continuous monitoring, ensure timely deployment of manpower and machinery, and coordinate with various line departments for the smooth conduct of the immersion process.

The civic body said it would continue monitoring arrangements at all 53 designated immersion points and take necessary measures to keep the locations clean, safe and well-managed during the immersion period.

World.title: Pakistan carries out 'calibrated’ airstrikes against terrorist targets in border region with Afghanistan
World.content:
Pakistan conducted airstrikes on terrorist sites “in the border region with Afghanistan”, killing more than 28 terrorists, the information ministry said on Monday.

In a statement, the ministry stressed that the “calibrated” strikes were carried out “against the hideouts and safe havens of terrorist organisations responsible” for the recent multiple terrorist incidents in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

“Based on credible intelligence, selective targeting of terrorist camps and hideouts belonging to Fitna al Khawarij and its affiliates has also been carried out in the border region with Afghanistan with precision and accuracy,” the statement said.

It added: “Three targets were destroyed with precision, including a suicide bombers’ training markaz (centre), killing 28 terrorists alongside multiple suicide bombers.

“Large quantities of weapons and ammunition stored at these marakiz (centres) and hideouts were also destroyed.”

The state uses the term Fitna al Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

Prior to the airstrikes, security forces conducted a “well-planned intelligence-based ground operation” on Sunday against a group of terrorists in KP’s Kohat and Hangu districts, the ministry said.

“As a result of precise and skilful engagement, nine khawarij belonging to Indian proxy Fitna al Khawarij were sent to hell, while several were injured,” the statement added.

The ministry highlighted that Pakistan had “always strived for the maintenance of peace and stability in the region”.

“However, the safety and security of our citizens remains our foremost priority. It is a matter of grave concern that Afghanistan continues to remain a hub of terrorism,” it said, specifying that the “threat to Pakistan emanates from Afghanistan”.

“In this context, our action precisely targeted the terrorist hubs. Maximum precautions were taken, and it was ensured that no collateral damage occurs,” the ministry asserted.

The airstrikes come a few days after a major attack in the old Police Lines in KP’s Kohat claimed 23 lives and injured about 100 others. Eight terrorists were killed during an overnight clearance operation launched to clear the area.

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar was in Kohat on Monday where he visited to the house of a police official martyred in the attack, according to state broadcaster Radio Pakistan.

Speaking to the media in Kohat, he said he had also visited the injured personnel at the Combined Military Hospital.

He added he was hopeful that terrorism would be eradicated from the country after meeting the heirs of the martyrs and ghazis.

“We will not rest until eradicate terrorism from its roots,” he asserted.

There has been a resurgence in terrorism in Pakistan since the Afghan Taliban returned to power in Kabul in 2021.

On Sunday, two officers and four others were martyred while eight terrorists were eliminated during a fire exchange between a security forces convoy and armed combatants, the military’s media wing said.

Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned TTP, that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded.

According to a UN Security Council-mandated monitoring report — covering the period from Dec 16, 2025 to June 9, 2026 — Afg­han Taliban’s continued support for TTP has contributed to a rise in the frequency and lethality of terrorist attacks in Pakistan, even as Kabul has taken some initial steps to rein in the group.

The report also pointed to growing operational and facilitation linkages among the TTP, Al Qaeda, Islamic State-Khorasan (ISIL-K) and the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA).

‘Ghazab lil Haq under vision Azm-i-Istehkam’

In its Monday statement, the information ministry reaffirmed that the “relentless counterterrorism campaign Ghazab lil Haq under vision ‘Azm-i-Istehkam’ by security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan will continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored and -supported terrorism from the country”.

On the night of February 26, following unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban from across the border, Pakistan launched Operation Ghazab lil Haq against terrorist hideouts.

The last time Pakistan carried out strikes in the border region with Afghanistan was in late June, with the government saying they were in response to a wave of terrorist attacks, including one on a Rangers camp in Karachi.

According to Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, 25 terrorists were killed in those strikes in Paktia, Paktika and Kunar.

Pakistan had also carried out similar strikes on terrorist hideouts along its border with Afghanistan earlier that month, killing 26 terrorists.

In July, security forces responded to unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban at border posts in Kurram, security sources had said.

Earlier this month, the Foreign Office (FO) declared that meaningful progress in relations with Kabul would depend on the Taliban taking concrete and verifiable action against TTP and other terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory.

It maintained that while Islamabad welcomed China’s continuing engagement, the external facilitation could not substitute for action by Kabul against terrorist infrastructure.

Last week, responding to Afghan Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid’s remarks, the information ministry had stressed that Pakistan consistently pursued constructive engagement with the Afghan Taliban, but would not allow what it called the “pretence of dialogue” to shield those threatening its people.

In his remarks, Mujahid had said Kabul wanted dialogue with Islamabad, but had also warned of “retaliatory action” if Pakistan carried out military operations inside Afghanistan — a warning that the information ministry rejected.

World.title: Interior Minister Naqvi warns PTI against Sept 27 protest call, urges party to change course
World.content:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Monday warned PTI against its proposed September 27 long march, urging the party to refrain from proceeding with the protest.

Naqvi’s remarks come as the party prepares for a nationwide protest and march towards Islamabad on September 27 to press for the release of its incarcerated founder, Imran Khan.

“We have clearly told them (PTI) that they can never achieve anything through such drama, and I will say again that there is still time; they should not go into this situation,” Naqvi said during a press briefing, advising the party to “not enter a dead-end street”.

The interior minister vowed the government will not “leave any loopholes” in its response if the party went ahead with the protest.

He held that PTI’s majority leadership was not in favour of the march. “[However], if they do, then we have the Islamabad High Court (IHC) order, and the government will ensure its implementation.”

The IHC order, issued on September 14, ruled that no political party or its leadership has the “lawful right to occupy public roads, highways, interchanges, toll plazas and buildings in Islamabad”.

Naqvi appealed to PTI to adopt a different approach.

“Do not harm yourself and your workers,” he said.

On being asked if the government had any “long-term solution” to PTI’s frequent protest calls, the interior minister said, “I believe this time we will find a permanent solution; we will not leave it halfway.”

When asked why the government was reluctant to shift PTI founder Imran Khan to a private health facility — as requested by his party and family — amid concerns about his health, the minister said doctors examined Imran last night.

“If they demand that his check-up should be done at a hospital, then we did have one last night [..] we are already fulfilling the demand,” Naqvi said.

“As for the treatment that is prescribed under the law, we will do everything according to the law. But we will not do it simply because they are demanding it,” the interior minister added.

Naqvi, during his talk, reiterated that PTI’s senior leadership was not in favour of the march.

On being asked if the interior ministry will fulfil its role in the upcoming protests, he said, “This time, we will fulfil our role completely. As I said, it will be once and for all.”

When asked whether the federal government had any plans to ban the party, the interior minister reiterated, “As I am telling you, this time we will find a once-and-for-all solution. We cannot afford this every time.”

Naqvi was also asked if the government was considering imposing governor rule in PTI-led Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP). At this, the minister said, “Look, we have already made it clear to them that whatever legal options are available, the prime minister, in consultation with our law ministry, will utilise them.”

However, he clarified that the party will not be allowed to “come to Islamabad and shut down the city for ten days. That possibility does not exist”.

Naqvi also spoke about the creation of new provinces, saying that the matter was progressing rapidly and that public participation in the campaign had increased.

He said: “The new provinces issue is moving forward at a pace that we cannot even imagine. The way people are practically coming forward, whether they are chambers, traders or individuals, everyone is playing their role in one way or another. I am very hopeful that, God willing, and if the public wants it, new provinces will certainly be created.

“And as far as the movement for new provinces is concerned, I believe it is moving ahead rapidly,” he added.

Naqvi’s warning comes as part of the government’s pushback against the party’s proposed march.

Last week, following the IHC judgement, Naqvi warned that the government would stop anyone from marching towards the federal capital “in every possible way”.

‘No violent group will be allowed’

Speaking to media in Kohat later in the day, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar reiterated that no “violent group will be allowed to descend upon Islamabad”.

“I cannot remember a peaceful PTI protest in the recent past,” Tarar said.

“Though I absolutely remember that Rangers and police personnel were martyred. Peaceful protesters do not leave their homes armed with sticks, nails, glass or slingshots,” he added.

The information minister accused the party’s demonstrators of damaging state property and harassing women, recalling that they had allegedly set a Metro station and trees on fire during one of their demonstrations in Islamabad.

“They should never even use the word ‘peaceful’ since they have never been peaceful nor can remain so. Therefore, no violent group can be allowed to enter Islamabad,” he declared.

Tarar also accused the PTI government of corruption and “bad intentions” in KP, questioning where the law and order funding was being spent in the wake of last week’s deadly Kohat blast.

He slammed KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi for going to Lahore and “recording videos on a charpoi” — a trip that concluded days before the Kohat blast — rather than staying in his province.

“Who will answer for the additional NFC (National Finance Commission Award) funds that have exceeded Rs150 billion?” Tarar asked, alleging that the funds were being used for political purposes.

“You have to answer for where you spent the law and order fund as policemen are sacrificing their lives,” he added, addressing Afridi and noting that the money should have been invested in police training and technical enhancement.

Tarar had also expressed the government’s determination not to allow any violent group to enter Islamabad or block roads on Sunday, stressing that the administration would ensure compliance with an IHC order against disruption to public movement.

Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb on Sunday also warned that strikes, sit-ins, long marches and road closures could cause an estimated Rs120 billion loss to the economy each day.

World.title: Mir Raza murder case: Judicial commission turns down MLO's request to record further statement
World.content:
KARACHI: A judicial commission formed to investigate the circumstances and possible negligence in the Mir Raza Ali murder case declined on Monday a request by Dr Osama Shaikh — the medico-legal officer who conducted the slain businessman’s first autopsy — to record a further statement.

Sindh High Court’s Justice Omar Sial, who heads the one-member commission, observed that Sheikh had “appeared on social media” and said that he had “more to tell the commission than what he told it earlier”, according to the order released after the latest hearing.

“Upon a query as to whether he wanted to say that the death of Mir Raza was a suicide and not a murder, he said that is not what he wanted to say. He clarified that it was not a suicide. He wanted to justify his finding that the bullet came from the front,” the order, a copy of which is available with Dawn, said.

There has been a controversy over Ali’s autopsy in the case, with Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiyya Syed pointing out flaws in the first postmortem findings. Following that, Ali’s body was exhumed and a second post-mortem was conducted. Its findings concluded that the 25-year-old was shot in the back and ruled out the possibility of a suicide.

Dr Syed also told the commission at a previous hearing that she faced “threats” after disputing the findings of the first postmortem.

In his order on Monday, Justice Sial stated, “I also sense from the questions I asked of him (Sheikh) that his sole purpose in recording a further statement is to throw mud at the police surgeon and the worthy chief minister. I will not allow either. The commission is not a forum for mud-slinging.”

The order added that the terms of reference of the commission required it determine the true facts and circumstances of the case and to attribute negligence.

“I have enough information for that. The commission has its own mind to determine what has transpired. Therefore, I decline Dr Osama Sheikh’s request,” Justice Sial added.

During his previous appearance before the commission on Sept 1, Sheikh had told the judicial commission that he was not under any influence or pressure while conducting the postmortem and had nowhere stated in his report that Ali had died by suicide.

For its part, the commission had expressed dissatisfaction with Sheikh’s answers, questioned the discrepancies between his initial and final reports and asked whether he or a sweeper had conducted the autopsy.

Sheikh had maintained that he had conducted the procedure and that the final report was issued after the exhumation and second autopsy, following 14 objections by the police surgeon.

He had added that he had declined to provide information when called to the chief minister’s house on Aug 9 in the absence of relevant documents, while the second investigation team recorded his statement on Aug 17.

The case’s investigation team was changed following objections raised by Ali’s family.

On Friday, the judicial commission had deplored that the first investigating officer of the case had hardly made any effort to probe the matter and did not fulfil legal formalities during the investigation.

According to the order, witness Ahmed Hassan Shaikh placed on record an investment and profit sharing agreement dated July 4, 2026, executed between him and Wafflix owners Ali and Ahmed Bhardey.

Hyderabad Health Services Director General Pervez Ahmed Shaikh also placed on record the following documents: a letter dated August 6, 2026, regarding the constitution of medico-legal board for Ali’s exhumation; an order dated August 6, 2026, under Section 176(2) of the Criminal Procedure Code; Office order dated August 6, 2026, issued by Pervez Ahmed Shaikh regarding appointment of the convener of the exhumation board; and notification dated March 30, 2026, regarding powers to dispose of cases relating to the constitution of special medical boards.

“After his media interviews, in which he complained that he had much more to say than he had told the Commission, Bhardey was given an opportunity to answer the family’s questions and tell them what he knew. The meeting was held on August 19,” Justice Sial said.

“The family has however informed me today that despite repeated requests to Bhardey to tell them what he knew, he said nothing beyond what he had already told the Commission.”

The case so far

Ali’s body was found a day after he went missing on July 28. Since then, the case has been mired in controversy, with the deceased’s family accusing the police of trying to bury the facts while the investigators initially attempted to build the case around the possibility of a suicide.

Days after the recovery of Ali’s body on July 29, Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed had told Geo News that the post-mortem findings in the case had raised several questions, as some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs.

On August 6, a Karachi court took up an application by Ali’s father, allowed the exhumation of his body, ordered the formation of a medico-legal board for the purpose and directed that a second autopsy of Ali’s body be conducted.

The Sindh health department then constituted an eight-member board, with police surgeon Dr Syed as the convener. However, in the early hours of August 7, the board was reconstituted through an order issued by the director general of the Sindh health department.

While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new five-member board, its members were changed.

But Ali’s family rejected the new board, which also resulted in the deferment of the planned exhumation on Friday. Meanwhile, the counsel for Ali’s family, Nasir, accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts.

The Sindh government then restored the original medical board, following which Ali’s body was exhumed on August 8.

A day later, the Sindh inspector general of police’s (IG) office notified the reconstitution of the investigating team probing Ali’s death, while Karachi Additional IG Azad Khan transferred the investigation into Ali’s murder to Zaman Town police station from Ferozabad Police Station, where the case was registered under charges of kidnapping.

The order for the probe team’s reconstitution also showed that a murder charge had been added to the first information report.

The same day, the Sindh government decided to seek a judicial commission for the case’s investigation, only to defer the plan a day later after Ali’s family said they had made no such demand and had faith in the new investigation team.

On Aug 19, Ali’s parents, Mir Hussain and Mariam Hussain, wrote to Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah, seeking his “direct supervision of the murder investigation”. They also urged the chief minister to order an investigation and departmental inquiry into the previous investigation team and immediately suspend the officers involved.

The provincial government acknowledged the letter and announced the decision on Aug 23 to form a judicial commission to determine whether the investigation in the case was being conducted impartially and to investigate the circumstances surrounding Ali’s death.

However, the counsel for Ali’s family approached the SHC, objecting to the provincial government’s decision to form a judicial commission and seeking the formation of an independent and multi-agency JIT “comprising officers who have had no previous involvement in the case”.

On Sept 2, the SHC dismissed that petition filed by Ali’s family, observing that constituting such a body was the “prerogative of the government”.
